author: winter oak
title: Feted or forgotten? A tale of two very different anarchists
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


An important split took place in the French anarchist movement at the very end of the nineteenth century.


This revolved around the question of whether the conviction of Jewish army captain Alfred Dreyfus for treason represented an important question of injustice and institutional anti-semitism or whether,

au contraire

, the case was irrelevant to the anarchist struggle.


François Jarrige writes in the

latest issue

 of

Brasero: revue de contre-histoire

: “The Dreyfus affair, which tore France apart from 1897-1898 onwards, also divided the anarchist milieu”. [1]


In what he terms “an extreme polarisation”, anarchists, “traditionally distrustful of the army and the state, split into convinced

dreyfusards

 and supporters of a strict indifference to what they considered an internal conflict within bourgeois institutions.


“Sébastien Faure, a major figure in the anarchist movement and co-founder of

Le Libertaire

, nevertheless managed to drag a number of activists into the active defence of Dreyfus”. [2]


We’ll come back to Faure later, but first I want to relate what Jarrige has to say about one of the anarchists who refused to climb on board the

dreyfusard

 bandwagon –

Emile Gravelle (1855-1920)

.


He was the founder of a current in the French anarchist movement called

naturien

 – there is no real English equivalent but the meaning is nature-loving or nature-based.


This, Jarrige explains, emerged in the Parisian

quartier

 of Montmartre and was a current that was “critical of industrial society and its goods, idealising prehistorical and primitive living and calling for a return to nature”. [3]


Gravelle, an anarchist painter, illustrator, pamphleteer and activist, was one of the first to formulate such a critique of “progress” and “civilisation”, prefiguring the green anarchism that emerged towards the end of the twentieth century. [4]


An important influence on Gravelle’s understanding of the world was his five-year stay in Buenos Aires, after leaving his home town of Douai in northern France at the age of 30.


Jarrige writes: “At the time Argentina was going through a phase of expansion: political stabilisation after civil wars, the conquest of indigenous lands, the expansion of cattle-rearing on the great plains of the

pampa

 and a massive influx of European immigrants. This context of brutal modernisation, mixing prosperity and social violence, had a deep impact on Gravelle…


“When he returned to France in 1890 he brought out a pamphlet in which he related his unpleasant experience. In this virulent text,

La République argentine dénoncée

 (‘The Argentine Republic denounced’), he describes how he had been taken in by the embroidered tales of a ‘shipping agent in the

rue de Dunkerque

‘, only to discover a reality of misery, exploitation and disillusionment.


“He writes about the diseases, the violence of the

gauchos

, the insalubrity of the towns and the suffering of immigrants pushed into suicide or madness. This pamphlet, laced with bitterness, also bears witness to a political realization: Gravelle denounces the illusions of progress and the mechanisms of capitalist exploitation”. [5]


Gravelle’s years in South America shaped his understanding of modernity in another way. Through his encounters with indigenous Guarani people he discovered “man, in the midst of nature, happy as a god in the triumphant splendour of its strength and beauty”. [6]


Jarrige says this provided him with “an alternative model to the European ways of living shaped by industry, the growing consumerism and imperialism”. [7]


It fed his rejection of modern urbanisation and his aspiration to a way of life founded on simplicity, autonomy and closeness to nature – “when Gravelle returned to Paris, he was thus no longer simply an illustrator looking for work: he was the bearer of a vision of the world opposed to that of the European civilisation of his age”. [8]


In the early 1890s Gravelle set up home in Montmartre, a bohemian, artistic and anarchic enclave on a hill in Paris. At the time, it was still semi-rural and was imbibed with the spirit of resistance to the new urban order, inherited from the Paris Commune of 1871.


Says Jarrige: “This landscape in transition, where the industrial smoke of the capital mixed with the last remains of rurality, deeply nourished Gravelle’s anarchist imagination”. [9]

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Baclaran vendors bear the cost of ASEAN Summit
content:
By Reachelyn Esona and Roselle Ochobillo

From bustling streets to empty sidewalks.

This may be an image of order for some, but for Baclaran street vendors, it can mean another day of uncertainty over whether they will have earnings to take home.

In the first week of November, the local government of Parañaque City ordered a clearing operation in barangay Baclaran in time for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nation (ASEAN) summit from November 15 to 17.

The Parañaque local government said that the barangay would temporarily prohibit street vendors along Roxas Boulevard, service roads, Redemptorist Road, Quirino Avenue, and beneath LRT-1 from November 2 to November 20, to clear the way for the arriving delegates.

Among those forced to leave their usual vending spots is Eduardo Bargas, 59, who’s been selling toys along Baclaran for almost 20 years to support his wife and only child. After being dislocated, he resorted to selling bottled water to earn a living despite the imposed clearing operation.

According to Bargas, they were informed about the operation as early as November 1. While larger vendors operating inside stall establishments were allowed to continue selling, ambulant vendors like him were temporarily ordered to stop their operations.

Bargas was nearly apprehended once by the authorities. Had he been caught, he said, his goods would have been confiscated. He begged the authorities not to take his items as it was all he had to live on.

Like other vendors, Bargas’s income was severely impacted by the clearing operation. He said he used to earn up to P1,000 (approximately US$ 15.63) a day before the policy was implemented. Now, he takes home only around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69).

The same concern was shared by a 50-year-old towel and sack bag vendor, Marlyn Merioles. She sells along Baclaran to sustain her elderly mother who is on maintenance medication, and her sibling who is a person with disability.

Before the clearing, Merioles was earning around P300 (approximately US$ 4.69) to P500 (approximately US$ 7.82) a day. Since the operation began, there were days she went home with empty pockets.

Merioles said she felt disheartened by the policy. Vendors, she said, are now anxious and find it difficult to sell their goods. They are constantly on their feet, keeping an eye out for patrols roaming the area. Merioles fears that she might not see them coming as her eyesight is already failing.

They were also warned that their goods would be confiscated if they were caught. Merioles said it would be a loss they could not afford because even a whole day of selling was not enough to recover the capital they had borrowed.

Merioles said it would help if the government would sustain their daily expenses. However, she said, only a few of the vendors benefitted from the financial assistance provided for the vendors.

While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) promised P10,000 (approximately $156.35) in cash assistance to vendors affected by the clearing operations in Baclaran, some vendors said they struggled to access the financial aid because it was reportedly limited to registered voters of Baclaran.

Rochelle Maale, who has been renting a stall in Baclaran for 10 years to sell ready-to-wear clothes, was among those who did not receive the assistance because she is not a registered voter in the area.

“The distribution of funds should be balanced… What about those who have been here for a long time but didn’t get anything?”Maale retorted.

Vendors argued that the assistance should be extended to everyone affected by the clearing operations, regardless of their place of residence, since they all experienced the impact of the clearing operations.

However, for many vendors, the issue goes beyond the limited eligibility for financial assistance.

They also questioned whether the P10,000 (approximately US$ 156.35) would be enough to sustain them after nearly 20 days of restricted operations.

Maale shared that the amount was insufficient to cover their daily expenses, especially amid rising costs of goods. “Will that P10,000 even last for a few days? No, it’s still not enough. That’s why vendors are struggling to make ends meet.”

She said some vendors have resorted to taking out loans to meet their everyday needs and restore their capital.

For vendors like Maale, the struggle extends beyond the clearing operations and financial assistance. What they need is a permanent and secure …

author: Jacob Hoffman-Andrews
title: Outage Chaos: Who Turned Off All The Computer?
content:
It's been a tough couple of weeks for anyone trying to

use email

,

fly

,

spend money

,

use an Apple device

*, or do

signals intelligence

. Technical service outages are nothing new, but why do so many big ones seem to be happening all at once? Are hackers, AI, and international conflicts to blame? And what can we do about it?


Since most service interruptions don't make the news, it's hard to get a baseline on how often we see them happen normally. But after a major incident like the

Microsoft cloud outage on November 12

, any smaller disruption is more likely to become a story as part of a pattern instead of an isolated incident. We would have heard plenty about the 

Air Traffic Control problems

 anyway, but the November 18 disruption to the

PlayStation Network

 might have gotten less attention. There might appear to be a spike or an upward trend in outages, but we can't easily verify that, and the increased coverage will tend to make it seem more significant and interconnected than it necessarily is regardless.


One boring reason we might see an uptick in problems right now is the date on the calendar. With Thanksgiving travel, Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Giving Tuesday, and Surveillance Sunday (we assume) all coming up, organizations often schedule major system updates for the first three weeks of November. This helps them prepare for holiday traffic, and lets them shift the outage risk to the time before those dates when they may consider it far more important to maintain reliable service.


While none of these particular outages have yet been directly attributed to AI (

or to malicious hackers

), bank CEOs and the NSA briefed congress and

reportedly attributed

 at least some of them to rushed attempts to patch vulnerabilities found by AI. That’s understandable: all software updates carry risk, and companies and governments are having to deploy more updates, and faster, than they’ve ever needed to before. Some of those updates are to important infrastructure, where an outage would be very disruptive, but the impact of leaving vulnerabilities unpatched would be even worse.


Vulnerabilities are a type of software bug that affects security. Once a vulnerability is found in a given piece of software and disclosed, typically the software maker will release a patch fixing that vulnerability. That’s why so many update notes say things like “performance improvements and security fixes”

—

 the security fixes are patches to vulnerabilities.


Companies and governments that run infrastructure face a challenging tradeoff: deploy patches quickly or slowly and cautiously? Patching quickly is important to keep systems secure. But every software update runs a risk: any change to a deployed system can have unintended consequences that snowball into a disastrous outage.


This exacerbates a much deeper problem long discussed in the engineering culture of many, if not most organizations. Keeping networks, servers, and applications not just secure but resilient in the face of patches, reboots, and capacity changes requires an investment in staff, time, hardware, and processes for frequent maintenance, redundant systems, realistic staging environments, automated rollbacks, monitoring, and pre-deployment testing. These investments are rarely as attractive to decision

-

makers as a new product or feature, or at times, sadly, as layoffs.


This should come as no surprise when we think of our apps, web sites, airlines

,

 and bank cards as supported by electronic infrastructure. As in the more visible physical world, maintenance can only be deferred for so long before the costs become immediate and dramatic. We accept the cost of an occasional short term bridge closure to reduce the risk of a bridge collapse, and highway departments schedule road work nearly every night of the year to repair and prevent the worst potholes.


When this kind of work is endlessly deferred in the world of software, we speak of

technical

 debt

:

issues we already know about that aren't causing a big enough problem right now to divert us from other work, but that, if left unaddressed, can easily multiply and interact to cause outages or other complications

.

 This can show up as routine steps that have to be done by hand instead of automatically on a schedule, a programmer's shortcut that works well in one specific situation but is more fragile in general, an operating system six months (or years) overdue for a reboot, or a …

author: By Clint Combs, Contributor
title: Agent Who Recorded Activist’s Arrest That Turned Into Racist White House Meme Identified
content:
St. Paul, MN — Homeland Security Investigations Special Agents Charles Engle and John Zappone sat parked outside the Aloft Hotel in downtown Minneapolis on Jan. 22. Their boss, Tonya Price — promoted to assistant special agent in charge six months earlier — instructed them to record the arrest of civil rights attorney and activist Nekima Levy Armstrong.


The testimony emerged during a recent federal court hearing detailing how Homeland Security Investigations, or HSI, carried out arrests against the federally charged Cities Church protesters, known as the

Righteous 39

. Not long after ICE agents fatally shot

Renee Good

 and

Alex Pretti

, activists learned that St. Paul ICE Field Director David Easterwood also served as a pastor at Cities Church in St. Paul.


Following a peaceful protest that interrupted a church service on Jan. 18, President Donald Trump suggested on Truth Social that the demonstrators and a journalists “should be thrown in jail, or thrown out of the Country.” Attorney General Pam Bondi announced an active investigation after speaking with lead pastor Jonathan Parnell.


Trump Admin Targets Press and Activists in Minnesota, Indicts ‘The Righteous 39’


On the hotel’s third floor, FBI agents tackled Satara Strong-Allen, a Black woman who stepped out of Levy Armstrong’s room to walk next door.


Levy Armstrong had a hunch that she would be targeted. “My suspicions at the time were correct because they thought she was me, even though I am several inches taller than my friend,” she said. “We saw a man run out of the hotel room across the hall from mine and start chasing her. These goons were willing to tackle and attack me in the hallway, not saying freeze, not saying you’re under arrest, but acting like they were on a football field with regard to the brutality that they exhibited towards another Black woman, again, thinking that it was me. That’s absurd and it’s unconscionable.”


Levy Armstrong fired off text messages to an organizer at 2 a.m. saying she wanted to turn herself in. Diagnosed with a brain tumor in 2022, she did not want to risk getting tackled in the hallway. Her attorney Jordan Kushner said he

called

 U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen to arrange a peaceful surrender.


Nekima Levy Armstrong speaks outside the federal courthouse in St. Paul on Feb. 27, 2026.


Chauntyll Allen speaks with her wife Satara Strong-Allen on the left of the image in the gray jacket.


“So I gave him my proposal, which is, we can take her down to the federal courthouse in Minneapolis,” Kushner said. “She can go the Marshals office and turn herself in there, and we don’t have to have any incident, no circus, no nothing. He agreed.”


Charles Engle, one of the HSI agents tasked with filming Levy Armstrong’s arrest, recently testified that his supervisor told him that she “couldn’t turn herself in.”


“Ms. Price notified me that she had heard that [Nekima] was going to try to turn herself in,” Engle said. “I was not told that she couldn’t turn herself in at the courthouse. We had heard that she was going to try to turn herself in at the courthouse.”


Also recently testifying was Special Agent

Zachary Kliniske

, who tasked with arresting St. Paul School Board Member Chauntyll Allen. He was questioned by Allen’s attorney Jill Brisbois.


“There was talk that they were going to self-surrender, but I never got any specifics on that,” Kliniske said. “I don’t know about why the arrest was supposed to be made. It’s just, I was the supervisor put in charge of arresting this person because they have an active arrest warrant.”


Kushner said Rosen later backed out of the courthouse plan.


“So [Rosen] calls me back and says, ‘Oh, no, we can’t do it that way. We have to arrest her at the hotel’ … because they wanted the photo op. It had nothing to do with justice, nothing to do with public safety,” Kushner said.


Rosen declined to say whether an agreement existed.


“The answer is any deal for her peaceful surrender was that she walk out of the hotel room she was hiding in and she says ‘I surrender to the federal law enforcement officers that were in the hallway’ and that’s exactly what occurred,” Rosen said.


Engle and Kliniske testified they were not issued body cameras, so Zappone recorded Levy Armstrong’s arrest on his cellphone.


“Why are you recording this?” Levy Armstrong said. “I don’t want to be a trophy for MAGA.”

title: Labor for Palestine National Network Solidarity with the Palestinian Trade Union Call for Global Action November 20-29, 2026
content:
Solidarity with the Palestinian Trade Union Call for Global Action November 20-29, 2026

The Labor for Palestine National Network stands in full solidarity with the Palestinian labor movement’s urgent call for global action to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing genocide and apartheid, from Friday, November 20, 2026 leading up to the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People on Sunday, November 29, 2026.

As the Palestinian labor call points out:

“Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.

“It is the duty of unions to ensure that the workers they represent—whether in ports, on ships, in businesses, or in government offices—are not involved, often without their knowledge and/or consent, in actions that involve complicity in atrocity crimes anywhere, including Israel’s war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against our people.”

Zionism is racism, and both the Democratic and Republican parties have blood on their hands for their deep complicity in Israeli settler colonialism, demonizing Palestinian resistance, and attacking the Palestine solidarity movement.

Although US workers have the power to end bipartisan-backed Israeli genocide, US labor leadership, which is closely tied to the Democratic Party establishment, has been deeply complicit with Zionism for more than a century, and most unions have—at best—remained silent.

Major unions who have nominally called for a ceasefire and arms embargo fail to acknowledge the Palestinan trade union calls or the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) picketline, and continue to resist members’ demands to use workers’ power—at the workplace, in the electoral arena, and in the streets—to shut down the genocide down, which continues to grind on with no end in sight.

This breach of solidarity was conspicuous during the historic October 30, 2026 international dockworker strike in solidarity with Palestine, which shut down 113 ports in five continents and 22 countries—none of them in the US—and now again during November’s week of global actions.

The indifference of union officialdom is a betrayal of the most basic labor principle, “An Injury to One Is an Injury to All.” As the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions-Gaza reminded US unions in 2025: “True labor solidarity is demonstrated through actions, not just words, and we count on your awareness and determination to take concrete steps to end this tragedy.”

Now is the time to reaffirm and escalate more than a half-century of rank-and-file labor solidarity with Palestine, including groundbreaking statements by the League of Revolutionary Black Workers in 1969, Arab worker-led strikes and protests against the UAW leadership’s support for Israel in 1973, ILWU dockers’ refusal to handle Israeli Zim Line vessels since 2014, the UAW’s 2026 divestment from Israel Bonds, and other grassroots Palestine labor solidarity since 2023.

As the November 21 Bay Area Mobilization for Palestine and Against War points out:

“This call to action comes at the heels of the US midterm elections, when voters this month delivered a strong rejection of US support for Israel and its genocide in Gaza, the war on Iran, the militarized brutality of ICE, and Trump’s racist and authoritarian agenda. Our movement has made clear that Palestinian liberation is inseparable from all struggles against racism, exploitation, and oppression everywhere. Let’s mobilize to show the people of Palestine our unwavering support, and to amplify to those in power what people everywhere are demanding: Stop Arming Israel, and No to War on Iran!”

In solidarity with the Palestinian trade union call, we support:

Strikes, walkouts, rallies, teach-ins, and protests at schools, colleges and universities in solidarity with the November 20 International Youth Strike Against War.

Direct action, withholding labor, and other forms of solidarity throughout the week of November 20-27, including a focus on Black Friday, November 27, to stop arming Israel and end the genocide.

A Brief History of Anarchism in Indonesia

Punk and the Re-birth of Anarchism in Indonesia

Repression of Punk and Anarchism

Resistance to Neoliberalism (and Neoliberal Policing)

Anarchism in contemporary Indonesia shares numerous connections with punk counter-culture. Repression against punks and anarchists has long been a problem for the movement there, but the motivations behind that repression have changed in recent years, as has the response of punk and anarchist communities to this repressive context.

This article will provide a quick overview of the historical trajectory of anarchism in Indonesia over the last century, before focusing on the re-emergence of anarchism alongside punk in the very late 1980s and 1990s. Some of the forms of repression faced by punks and anarchists will be detailed, especially the religious dimension of that repression, before charting a partial shift in the authorities’ understanding of anarchism and how that has altered the form and scope of repression.

To set some historical context then, it is well-known that Marxism was the dominant ideology of the revolutionary Left in Indonesia throughout the first half of the twentieth century and into the 1960s, especially as manifested in the mass-movement Partai Komunis Indonesia (PKI, Communist Party of Indonesia)—this was at one point the largest Communist Party in the world that hadn’t yet seized power, with several million members. However, anarchism was also a significant political strand, not least within the wider movement opposing the Dutch colonial government. Anarchism even had some influence within the explicitly Marxist PKI. In 1926, the Party’s newspaper, Api, featured quotes from the anarchist political philosopher Bakunin on its front page, and this was such a strong influence that a leading PKI figure named Darsono insisted that members should remember that ‘the Communism of Marx and not the anarchism of Bakunin must govern the party’ (Benda & McVey 1960). According to Bima Satria Putra’s (2018) book about anarcho-syndicalism in Indonesia in the early twentieth century, anarchist ideas have coloured Marxist and social-democratic organisations throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, and, in fact, differences in political ideology within the Indonesian Left were not a significant problem, because they had a common enemy in the ‘invaders’ of the Dutch East Indies.

It appears that this anarchist current in the PKI was successfully suppressed by the orthodox Marxists, and, indeed, anarchist-minded activists would have been able to organise independently within specifically anarchist organisations and unions. Despite the increased dominance of the PKI and Marxism over the Left towards the mid twentieth century, anarchism persisted to at least some extent within the political lexicon of Indonesia into the 1960s. content:
Çorum- Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu (KESK), 2027 yılı bütçesinde emekçilere yeterli pay ayrılmadığı gerekçesiyle Çorum’da basın açıklaması düzenledi. KESK Eş Genel Başkanı Ahmet Karagöz’ün katıldığı açıklamada, bütçenin emekçilerden yana hazırlanması çağrısı yapılırken, 12 Aralık’ta Ankara’da düzenlenecek mitinge katılım çağrısında bulunuldu.

KESK Eş Genel Başkanı Ahmet Karagöz, Eğitim Sen Örgütlenme Sekreteri İzzet İldeş ve KESK’e bağlı sendikaların yöneticilerinin katılımıyla Kadeş Barış Meydanı’nda basın açıklaması düzenlendi. “Sermayeye değil, emekçiye bütçe”, “Gün gelecek devran dönecek, AKP halka hesap verecek” ve “Kurtuluş yok tek başına, ya hep beraber ya hiçbirimiz” sloganlarının atıldığı açıklamaya KESK’e bağlı sendikaların şube başkanları ve üyelerinin yanı sıra Yeni Parti İl Başkan Yardımcısı Garip Özgür, Emek Partisi İl Başkanı Muharrem Özünel, DEM Parti İl Başkanı Hasan Satılmış ve Çorum Emek ve Demokrasi Platformu Sözcüsü Av. Ahmet Özdel de destek verdi.

Basın açıklamasında konuşan Karagöz, AKP’nin 25 yıl önce yasaklar, yoksulluk ve yolsuzlukla mücadele vaadiyle iktidara geldiğini ancak bugün ülkenin ağır sorunlarla karşı karşıya olduğunu söyledi. Karagöz, 86 milyon yurttaşın oluşturduğu kaynakların toplumun geniş kesimlerinin ihtiyaçları doğrultusunda kullanılmadığını savunarak, bütçeden emekçilerin, işçilerin, emeklilerin, çiftçilerin, öğrencilerin ve kadınların yeterli pay alamadığını ifade etti.

Bütçelerin, gelirlerin kimlerden toplandığını ve hangi kesimler için harcandığını gösteren belgeler olduğunu belirten Karagöz, mevcut bütçede sermaye gruplarının, cemaatlerin, tarikatların ve çok uluslu şirketlerin öncelikli olduğunu kaydetti. Toplumun ortak kaynaklarını oluşturmasına rağmen geniş kesimlerin bütçeden yeterince yararlanamadığını dile getiren Karagöz, 12 Aralık’ta Ankara Tandoğan Meydanı’nda KESK, DİSK, TMMOB ve TTB tarafından “Gelirden, vergiden adalet; halk için bütçe, demokratik Türkiye” sloganıyla miting düzenleneceğini açıkladı.

2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerine de değinen Karagöz, bütçede emekçilere yeterli pay ayrılmadığını, buna karşın faiz, rant, savunma sanayisi, silah şirketleri, cemaatler ve tarikatlara kaynak aktarıldığını belirtti. Çocukların okulda tükettiği simit ve ayrandan alınan vergilerin dahi bütçeye katkı sunduğunu belirten Karagöz, okula giden her dört öğrenciden birinin aç olduğunu öne sürdü. Üniversite öğrencilerinin barınma sorunları nedeniyle eğitimlerini bırakıp ailelerinin yanına dönmek zorunda kaldığını kaydetti.

Çiftçilerin ürettikleri ürünleri değerinde satamadığını, borçlarını ödeyebilmek için ürünlerini veya topraklarını elden çıkarmak zorunda kaldığını ifade eden Karagöz, esnafın da ekonomik sıkıntılar nedeniyle kepenk kapattığını, iş yerlerinin iflas ettiğini ve çalışanların işten çıkarıldığını söyledi. Ülkenin insan onuruna yakışır bir yaşam için yeterli kaynaklara sahip olduğunu savunan Karagöz, kaynakların adil dağıtılmadığını dile getirdi.

Emekçilerin yoksulluk, emeklilerin açlık, gençlerin geleceksizlik ve belirsizlik, kadınların ise yoksulluk ve eşitsizlikle mücadele ettiğini belirten Karagöz, bu kesimlerin ihtiyaçlarına yönelik kaynak aktarılmadığını söyledi. Meraların, ormanların ve doğal alanların talan edildiğini, işçilerin iş yerlerinde yaşamını yitirdiğini ifade eden Karagöz, AKP’nin 25 yıllık iktidarı döneminde Türkiye genelinde 39 bin işçinin hayatını kaybettiğini belirterek, işçi sağlığı ve iş güvenliğine daha fazla kaynak ayrılması gerektiğini vurguladı.

2027 yılı bütçe taslağında kaynakların yüzde 20’sinin faize, yüzde 18’inin silah sektörüne ayrıldığını ifade eden Karagöz, ülkede yürütülen barış sürecini değerli bulduklarını ancak savunma ve silah sektörüne yüksek miktarda kaynak aktarılmasını düşündürücü olarak değerlendirdiklerini söyledi. Kaynakların işçilerin, emekçilerin ve emeklilerin talepleri doğrultusunda kullanılmasını istedi.

Kamusal hizmetlerin azaldığını, kurumların ve fabrikaların özelleştirildiğini belirten Karagöz, kamu yatırımlarına daha fazla pay ayrılması, özelleştirmeler yerine kamulaştırmaya kaynak aktarılması çağrısında bulundu. Meraların, doğal alanların ve zeytinliklerin sermayeye açılmasına tepki gösterdi.

Ülkede yoksulluğun yanı sıra yasaklar ve adaletsizliklerle de mücadele edildiğini savunan Karagöz, gazetecilerin, seçilmiş belediye başkanlarının, milletvekillerinin, hak arayan işçilerin ve sendikacıların tutuklu olduğunu, öğrencilerin gözaltına alındığını söyledi.

Asgari ücretin 28 bin …

author: Unknown
title: Belediye meclislerinde başkan seçimine ilişkin yeni usul Resmi Gazete'de
content:
Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı'nın hazırladığı yönetmelik değişikliği 20 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. Düzenleme, belediye meclislerinin kendi üyeleri arasından yaptığı başkan ve başkanvekili seçimlerinin kurallarını yeniden belirliyor.


9 belediye başkanı AKP'ye geçti


19 Kasım 2026


Yeni oylama usulü


Oylamada basılı birleşik oy pusulası kullanılacak. Üyeler, tercih ettikleri adayın adının yanına mühür basacak. Oy pusulasına elle isim yazılmayacak.


Meclis salonunda en az iki kapalı oy kabini bulunacak. Mühürlü zarflar şeffaf sandığa atılacak. Adaylar oturumu yönetemeyecek, ancak oy kullanabilecek. Her parti grubu ile bağımsızlar birer gözlemci bildirebilecek.


Ahmet Özer: "Ver belediyeyi gir içeri suçuna sonra bakarız dediler"


11 Kasım 2026


Adaylık ve geçersiz oylar


Adaylık başvuruları, valinin belirleyeceği seçim toplantısının ilk oturumunda meclis başkanlık divanına bildirilecek. Bu oturumdan sonra yeni başvuru alınmayacak. Adaylar her tur öncesi çekilebilecek.


Mühür taşımayan, tanıtıcı işaret içeren ya da birden fazla adaya mühür basılmış pusulalar geçersiz sayılacak. Sandıktan çıkan zarf sayısı oy kullanan üye sayısını aşarsa ilgili tur iptal edilip yeniden oylama yapılacak.


Saklama


Pusulalar ve zarflar, dava süresi dolana kadar saklanacak. Dava açılmışsa mahkeme kararı kesinleşene kadar saklanmaya devam edilecek.


Ne olmuştu?


Düzenleme, oylamada gizliliği ve şeffaflığı artırmayı, adaylık ve oy kullanma süreçlerini standartlaştırmayı ve itirazlarda izlenebilirliği sağlamayı amaçlıyor. Haberde 31 Mart 2024'ten bu yana, 4'ü büyükşehir olmak üzere 117 belediyede yönetimin transferlerle değiştiği belirtiliyor.


(FY)

author: Unknown
title: Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan: 589 milyon zarok li herêmên şer dijîn
content:
Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan (Save the Children) têkildarî zarokên li herêmên şer dijî raporek belav kiriye. Li gorî raporê zarok herî zêde di sala 2025an de li herêmên şer jiyaye ango rûbirûyê şer bûne.


Di heman demê de binpêkirinên wekî rêgirîkirina li gihîştina alîkariyên mirovî, revandin û tundkariya zayendî bi awayekî berbiçav zêde bûne.


Li Afganistanê 3,7 milyon zarok bi xetereya birçîbûnê re rûbirû ne


5 Tebax 2026


Di rapora herî nû ya rêzeraporên bi navê "Şerê li Dijî Zarokan Rawestînin" de hat eşkerekirin ku sala 2025an li cîhanê 589 milyon zarok li herêmên şer jiyane.


Ev hejmar ji sala 1990î û vir ve ku tomarkirina amaran dest pê kiriye amara herî bilind e û ji du qat zêdetirî hejmara giştî ya nîvê salên 90î yên sedsala borî ye.


Artêşa Îsraîlê di 20 rojên dawî de 490 zarok qetil kirin


7 Nîsan 2025


Birêvebirê Rêxistina Parastina Zarokan a Almanyayê Florian Westphal got:


"Ji bo bi milyonan zarokan tirs, tundî û koçberî bûne beşek ji jiyana wan a rojane." 


Westphal her wiha amaje pê kir ku divê ev amar ji bo civaka navneteweyî bibin"zengilekî hişyarkirinê."


Herêmên şer ên ku zarok lê dijîn


Li gorî raporê  sala 2025an li parzemîna Afrîkayê û li Rojhilata Navîn ji her 5 zarokan nêzîkî 2 zarok li herêmên şer jiyane.


Li cîhanê ji zarokên ku li herêmên şer dijîn jê ji sedî 44ê wan tenê li parzemîna Afrîkayê ye.


Rêjeya zarokên ku li wê parzemînê rûbirûyê şer dibin di 15 salên borî de ji 3 qatan zêdetir zêde bûye; sala 2010an ji sedî 12 bû lê sala 2025an derketiye ji sedî 39an.


UNICEF: Ji Helebê 228 zarok gihîştin Rojava


16 Çile 2026


Li Rojhilata Navîn jî sala 2025an ji sedî 40,2yê zarokan li herêmên şer jiyane. Hejmara zarokên ku li herêmê di bin bandora şer de mane bi rêjeya nêzîkî ji sedî 29an zêde bûye; sala 2024an 52 milyon zarok bûn, sala 2025an derketiye 67 milyon zarokî.


Binpêkirinên metirsîdar


Li gorî raporê di sala 2025an 8 hezar û 322 bûyerên piştrastkirî yên rêgiriya li alîkariyên mirovî hatine tomarkirin ku li gorî dehsaleke berê 16 qat zêde bûye (sala 2015an tenê 509 bûyer û sala 2005an tenê 8 bûyer hatibûn tomarkirin).


Piraniya van bûyeran li Filistînê bi 5 hezar û 946 bûyeran hatine tomarkirin ku ev hejmar zêdetirî ji sedî 70yê hemû bûyerên tomarkirî yên cîhanê pêk tîne. Bi vî awayî, rêgirîkirina li alîkariyên mirovî piştî kuştin û kêmendamkirina zarokan bûyeduyem binpêkirina herî berbelav.


2025: Zarokan di bianet kurdiyê de çawa cih girtiye?


31 Kanûn 2025


Komkirina binpêkirinan


Li gorî lêkolînê, Neteweyên Yekbûyî bi giştî 38 hezar û 967 binpêkirinên giran ên li dijî zarokan ên sala 2025an piştrast kirine ku piştî amara rekor a sala 2024an (41 hezar û 763 binpêkirin) duyem amara herî bilind a salane ye.


Zêdetirî nîvê van binpêkirinan tenê li 3 deveran qewimîne ku ew jî Filistîn, Komara Demokratîk a Kongoyê û Nîjerya ne.


Tenê li Filistînê 12 hezar û 449 binpêkirinên piştrastkirî hatine tomarkirin ku nêzîkîsêyeka hemû bûyerên li cîhanê ye.


UNICEF: Li Xezeyê rojane 28 zarok dimirin


5 Tebax 2025


Amarên herî berbiçav ên binpêkirinên sala 2025an ev in:


Li gorî raporê, di şer de 14 hezar û 224 zarok hatine kuştin an kêmendam bûne. Di revandina zarokan de hejmareke rekor hatiye tomarkirin ku gihîştiye 5 hezar û 128bûyeran.


Hezar û 787 bûyerên tundiya zayendî hatine tomarkirin (di dehsaleke borî de bi rêjeya ji sedî 71 zêde bûye û ji sedî 86ê bûyeran li herêmên şer ên Afrîkayê, bi taybetî li Kongoû Sûdanê qewimîne).


Êrişên li ser dibistan û nexweşxaneyan ji bo sala 5an li ser hev zêde bûne û gihîştine 2hezar û 930 bûyeran; bi 837 êrişan li ser axa Filistînê û 643 êrişan li Ukraynayê ji nîvîzêdetirî êrişên cîhanê pêk anîne.


(AY)


*Çavkanî: Rudaw

author: infolibre
title: Συγκεντρώσεις για τη Διεθνή Ημέρα Τρανς Θυμάτων, Παρασκευή 20/11
content:
Συγκεντρώσεις καλούνται σε Αθήνα και Θεσσαλονίκη για την 20η Νοέμβρη, διεθνή ημέρα τρανς θυμάτων. Συλλογικότητες, ομάδες, οργανώσεις καλούν σε μία ημέρα διεκδίκησης και μνήμης.


Αθήνα:

 Στις 18:00 στην πλατεία Κλαυθμώνος


Θεσσαλονίκη:

 Στις 18:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


ΑΘΗΝΑ


ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗ


20 Νοέμβρη


ΗΜΕΡΑ ΜΝΗΜΗΣ ΤΡΑΝΣ ΘΥΜΑΤΩΝ


Διεκδικούμε φροντίδα // μέριμνα // συμπερίληψη // αποδοχή για τα τρανς αδέρφια μας


Και αυτή η 20η Νοέμβρη θα είναι μέρα μνήμης και διεκδίκησης,


Επειδή μέσα σε έναν χρόνο έχουμε χάσει 273 τρανς αδέρφια μας, χωρίς να μπορούμε καν να υπολογίσουμε τις αυτοκτονίες, καθώς συχνά οι άνθρωποι που αυτοκτονούν καταγράφονται με το φύλο που τους αποδόθηκε κατά τη γέννηση


Επειδή κάθε 32 ώρες ένα τρανς ή φυλοδιαφορετικό άτομο δολοφονείται σε κάποιο σημείο αυτού του κόσμου, με 106 δολοφονημένους ανθρώπους μόνο στη Βραζιλία


Επειδή, από αυτούς τους ανθρώπους, ένα στα τρία άτομα είναι γυναίκα σεξεργάτρια


Επειδή οι τραμπικής έμπνευσης παραλογισμοί περί «woke ατζέντας» και στις δύο πλευρές του Ατλαντικού οπλίζουν το χέρι φασιστών και ομοτρανσφοβικών


Επειδή το σύστημα εκπαιδεύει κοινωνίες ολόκληρες στη ματσίλα, την τοξική αρρενωπότητα και το στερεοτυπικό έμφυλο δίπολο, όπου οι τρανς υπάρξεις εξοβελίζονται, περιθωριοποιούνται, υφίστανται συνεχή βία


Επειδή οι αστικές κυβερνήσεις όχι μόνο δεν ευνοούν, αλλά αντιθέτως βάζουν κωλύματα και απαγορεύουν τη φυλομετάβαση σε ανήλικα τρανς άτομα


Επειδή σε μια περίοδο πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, οι δημόσιοι πόροι κατευθύνονται σε θηριώδεις στρατιωτικούς εξοπλισμούς και όχι σε ερευνητικά ιατρικά προγράμματα ή στην κατάλληλη εκπαίδευση του ιατρικού και νοσηλευτικού προσωπικού ως προς τη φροντίδα που οφείλουν να παρέχουν σε τρανς ανθρώπους


Επειδή δεν έχει εισαχθεί ακόμα το μάθημα της σεξουαλικής αγωγής στα σχολεία με ισότιμη παρουσίαση όλων των ταυτοτήτων φύλου, έκφρασης φύλου και σεξουαλικότητας


Επειδή οι υπηρεσίες υγείας (τεστ παπ, μαστογραφίες) δεν είναι απεμφυλοποιημένες, ώστε να είναι προσβάσιμες σε όλα τα άτομα


Επειδή δεν έχει εισαχθεί η χρήση ουδέτερης ως προς το φύλο γλώσσας στα κρατικά έγγραφα, ώστε να μην απαιτείται η δήλωση ταυτότητας φύλου


Επειδή παραμένουν οι διακρίσεις για το δικαίωμα στη γονεϊκότητα


Αυτόν τον Νοέμβρη, με τις φωνές της Πάολα Ρεβενιώτη και της Νικόλ να ηχούν στα αυτιά μας, βγαίνουμε στον δρόμο και διεκδικούμε φροντίδα, μέριμνα, συμπερίληψη και αποδοχή για όλα τα τρανς/φυλοδιαφορετικά αδέρφια μας.


Καλούμε αυτή την Παρασκευή 20 Νοέμβρη στις 18:00 στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


REclaim PRIDE-Thessaloniki


273 θύματα σε όλο τον κόσμο θρηνούμε τη φετινή Διεθνή Ημέρα Μνήμης Τρανς Θυμάτων. Για άλλη μια φορά η

μεγάλη πλειονότητα ήταν τρανς γυναίκες ή θηλυκότητες (95%) και μαύρα ή μη λευκά τρανς άτομα (75%). Η αντι-τρανς εκστρατεία της ακροδεξιάς παγκοσμίως οπλίζει το χέρι των δολοφόνων, είτε αυτοί είναι μέσα στο σπίτι των τρανς (20% των δραστών ήταν ερωτικοί σύντροφοι των θυμάτων) είτε έξω από αυτό.


Όσο και αν η τρανσφοβική βία είναι επικίνδυνη και τρομακτική, τα τρανς άτομα θα συνεχίσουν προπαντός να χαίρονται το φύλο με το οποίο αυτοπροσδιορίζονται. Αυτό δεν μπορεί να μας το στερήσει κανένας.


Διεκδικούμε το δικαίωμά μας να υπάρχουμε με όποιο φύλο μας εκφράζει.


Διεκδικούμε τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα που θα έπρεπε να έχουμε ήδη.


Διεκδικούμε να είμαστε ο εαυτός μας. Και θα είμαστε!


Όλες, όλα και όλοι την Παρασκευή 20 Νοεμβρίου στις 18:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου για την Πορεία της Διεθνούς Ημέρας Τρανς Μνήμης. Θα μας βρείτε εκεί με το πανό και τις σημαίες μας.


ομάδα Sylvia Rivera – για ένα κινηματικό Thessaloniki Pride


Συγκέντρωση για την ημέρα μνήμης trans θυμάτων


Αν τα παιδιά σας είναι τρανς και δε σας το λένε, είναι γιατί φοβούνται τη βίαιη αντίδρασή σας. Κουράστηκαν να σας εξηγούν. Κουράστηκαν τον έλεγχό σας και τον έλεγχο της κοινωνίας. Και δε θα σταματήσουν να είναι, είτε το ξέρετε είτε όχι. Το λιγότερο που έχετε να κάνετε είναι να τα προστατέψετε.


Κάθε χρόνο διαβάζουμε ονόματα που αρνούμαστε να ξεχάσουμε. Η 20ή Νοέμβρη μνημονεύει τα τρανς αδέρφια μας που δολοφονήθηκαν από το τρανσφοβικό σύστημα. Δηλαδή, από ανθρώπους που ενεργά μισούν, πιέζουν, κυνηγούν ή λοιδορούν την ύπαρξη των τρανς ανθρώπων. Ξεκίνησε το 1999 ως μια πρωτοβουλία ενάντια στη διαγραφή των τρανς ατόμων από τη συλλογική μνήμη, από ακτιβίστριες όπως η Gwendolyn Ann Smith, έπειτα από την αυξανόμενη δολοφονική τάση ενάντια σε τρανς άτομα. Σήμερα, η ημέρα αυτή σηματοδοτεί μια διεθνή πρωτοβουλία ενάντια στην τρανσφοβική βία.


Κάθε χρόνο θρηνούμε αμέτρητα …

author: Unknown
title: Теория коммунизации: Коммунизм > Социализм
content:
Процессуальное понимание коммунизма лишь относительно недавно пришло в современное левое движение. Традиционно устоялось понимание коммунизма как статичной общественно-экономической формации, чему линейно предшествовал этап диктатуры пролетариата, сохранявшийся как посреднический этап даже в представлении левых коммунистов, которые оказались ближе всех к реальному пониманию государства как враждебного буржуазного института.

Переосмысление этого положения вещей в современном марксистском дискурсе осуществили Жиль Дове и французский коллектив Tiqqun во второй половине XX века, сформулировав т.н «теорию коммунизации» — идеи о том, чтобы осуществлять коммунистическое общество без переходных этапов в виде диктатуры пролетариата и воссоздания вертикальных структур управления социалистическим обществом. Ничего не напоминает, правда? Подобного рода достижениям в левой мысли можно только радоваться, потому как это отвечает нашим анархическим структурным интересам в организации глубинных общественных изменений.

Разумеется, «теория коммунизации» — это дублирование анархо-коммунистического подхода к организации общества, что Жиль Дове и не скрывал, отсылая к Кропоткину в формулировке этой теории. К тому же, современность предоставляет нам пласт для эффективной коммунизации на базе кибернетического платформенного самоуправления социоэкономическими процессами.

В первую очередь, мы, анархисты, поддерживаем понимание политики и социальных противоречий как динамического, а не статического процесса, следовательно, и коммунизм — как практику и процесс, а не абстрактную онтологическую цель.

Собственно, нам есть чем возразить Жилю Дове и его представлению о коммунизации со стороны первоисточника и реальной системной практики. Разумеется, переходный этап как состояние и процесс — это устаревшее линейное модернистское представление, на практике своей редко перевешивающее реформистскую практику по своей эффективности — в критике переходности мы проблем не видим.

Другое дело — в методологическом «катастрофизме» и разрыве будущего с прошлым, неизбежно сводящемуся к безосновному ожиданию накопления тщательно скрываемых противоречий современного мира. Коммунизация — вне сомнений, процесс необходимый и чрезвычайно важный, но ключевой акцент на том, что это — процесс, что вульгарно упускается из внимания «катастрофистами» и апологетами деструктивного подхода к политике.

Любой процесс на этапе своего возникновения или развития нуждается в корректировке и оптимизации тех методов, которыми он достигается — без этого императива жизнеспособность системы практически предрешена, поскольку не осуществляется никаких мер для поддержания её гомеостаза и выработки ответов на вызовы. Целеполагание такой системы при этом прямо зависит от подбора методов, которые она использует, что требует их отбора в реальном времени.

Простыми словами — коммунизация должна проходить здесь и сейчас, через практику и внедрение механизмов, ликвидирующих участие государства и капитала в самоорганизации и ликвидирующих товарно-денежные отношения в производстве и потреблении, в противном случае — мы наблюдаем реформизм и смену лиц в системе, полностью сохранившей свою семантическую основу.

Поэтому методология коммунизации — это либо её практика через префигурацию, либо полное отсутствие этой методологии до «часа Х», когда намеченная французскими постмарксистами ситуация достигнет состояния, когда необходимо будет её проводить. И, разумеется, в кризисных условиях, когда вертикаль выигрывает у горизонтали за счет простоты мобилизации системы, это будет обречено на ещё один цикл прохождения доминирующих вертикальных систем через железный закон олигархии Михельса, и — voilà — реставрация государства и капитализма.

Потому что дать реальное понимание фундамента будущего общества может только его отражение в настоящем и диалектическое прохождение через разнообразие тех методов, которые мы могли бы использовать.

title: Nvidia agli onori della cronaca: il mercato dei chip tra USA e Cina
content:
La vicenda salita gli onori della cronaca per il gossip tra gli Huang che ha in seguito portato alle dimissioni dell’ad di Nvidia, leader mondiale nel settore dell’intelligenza artificiale, ha riaperto il dibattito sul mercato dei microprocessori e, sullo sfondo, dello scontro tra USA e Cina. 


Al di là dello “scandalo” per la relazione tra l’ad di Nvidia e Alice Huang, dirigente dell’azienda Megaspeed con sede a Singapore e presunta spia cinese (dettaglio lasciato poi nel dimenticatoio), è interessante interrogarsi sullo stato dell’arte del comparto delle Big Tech a livello mondiale. 


Le catene del valore nel settore dei microchip intraprendono delle strade spesso considerate “zona grigia” e gli scambi tra aziende cinesi e statunitensi sono di là dall’essere una novità. Questo interroga sull’eventualità della bolla dell’ai, della posizione sul mercato di queste aziende e quali sono i fattori che poi ne determinano l’egemonia su di esso.

author: L214
title: Carrefour Noel 2026
content:
Pour le seul mois de décembre, 10 230 000 animaux sont tués pour Carrefour. L’enseigne atteint ce nombre effarant en recourant massivement à l’élevage intensif : pour Carrefour, poulets, cochons, moutons et lapins endurent l’entassement les uns contre les autres dans des bâtiments fermés ou l’isolement dans de petites cages, les mutilations, la sélection génétique poussée.

Pour les fêtes, nous faisons un vœu simple : Carrefour doit s’engager à diminuer de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués !

Pour rendre hommage aux plus de 10 millions d’animaux qui seront abattus pour Carrefour en décembre, nous distribuons plus de 10 millions de décorations de fêtes porteuses de messages pour les animaux.

Commandez gratuitement votre enveloppe de décorations militantes

Agissez tout au long des fêtes en répandant ces confettis dans les rayons des magasins Carrefour

Toutes les décorations de fêtes ont été commandées ! Si vous souhaitez tout de même participer à cette action, téléchargez et imprimez des décorations militantes sur ce lien. Merci d’agir pour les animaux avec L214 !

Les champs suivis d’un astérisque (*) sont obligatoires. Les commandes ne sont possibles qu’en France métropolitaine.

Chaque enveloppe contient 1000 décorations militantes.

Vous recevrez une enveloppe contenant un millier de petits flocons porteurs de messages pour les animaux, à répandre dans les magasins Carrefour.

Cette action s’effectue tout au long des fêtes de fin d’année. Vous pouvez disperser les décorations dans les rayons de Carrefour à chacun de vos passages en magasin.

Carrefour market, Carrefour city, supermarché, hypermarché… C’est vous qui choisissez !

Rayons conserve, frais, jouets ou même petit-déjeuner : saupoudrez les confettis dans le rayon de votre choix.

Expliquez que vous participez à une action citoyenne afin de demander à Carrefour de s’engager à sortir de l’élevage intensif, et à réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués.

Ne répandez pas les décorations près de produits sans emballages, qu’elles seraient susceptibles d’endommager : produits frais type viande, fromage, etc. Ne les répandez pas sur le sol du magasin.

depuis votre arrivée sur le site

Pour que Carrefour réduise de 50% le nombre d’animaux tués pour ses rayons

Contre la souffrance des animaux, agissez à nos côtés avec un don.

Choisissez le montant de votre don

80 % des achats alimentaires en France sont réalisés dans les enseignes de la grande distribution. Pour les animaux, le bilan est lourd : l’élevage intensif, et ses pratiques cruelles, est la norme, son cadencement infernal aboutit chaque année à la mise à mort de 1,2 milliards d’animaux terrestres pour la consommation française. L’aquaculture et la pêche industrielle alourdissent ce total de plus de 7 milliards de poissons.

Pour faire face aux urgences éthiques, écologiques, sanitaires et sociales, L214 propose un objectif, consensuel et atteignable à moyen terme : diviser par deux le nombre d’animaux tués pour l’alimentation française d’ici 2030.

Le Plant Protein Pact (PPP) est la traduction concrète de cet objectif, il appelle les enseignes de la grande distribution à s’engager à rééquilibrer les sources de protéines dans leurs ventes avec l’objectif que les protéines végétales représentent au moins 60 % de leurs volumes de protéines vendus à horizon 2030.

À l’occasion des soldes d’été, les bénévoles de L214 se mobilisent pour demander à Carrefour de ne plus « solder la vie » des animaux. Ils rappellent que l’enseigne recourt massivement à l’élevage intensif pour faire baisser les coûts – au prix de la vie des animaux.

L214 organise une manifestation hors norme dans le plus grand magasin Carrefour de France, à Villiers-en-Bière (Seine-et-Marne) : 120 militants ont brandi les portraits d’animaux photographiés dans des élevages intensifs fournissant Carrefour. Le même jour, des bénévoles ont exposé ces portraits devant des dizaines de supermarchés Carrefour, partout en France.

L214 publie une nouvelle enquête sur un élevage intensif du Maine-et-Loire approvisionnant Carrefour. Les dindes y vivent dans leurs déjections, elles montrent des signes de souffrances, jusqu’à en mourir, pour certaines. author: Keith Ang'ana
title: Kenya’s litmus test
content:
Kenya has a long and uneasy relationship with the Finance Bill. Every year, the Treasury returns with its plans for raising revenue, setting out the sums the country needs and the measures through which it hopes to collect them. On paper, these are questions of budgets and tax policy. In practice, they shape the terms of everyday life: what food costs, what it takes to keep a business running, how much remains in a payslip after deductions, and how far a household’s income can stretch.

The events of 2024 changed the way this conversation unfolded. Opposition to the Finance Bill grew into a nationwide protest movement, culminating in the breach of Parliament on June 25 and the eventual withdrawal of the bill. But the retreat was less an ending than a pause: some of its proposals would find their way back through the

Tax Laws

, Tax Procedures, Public Finance, and Business Laws Bills of 2024.

The 2025 Finance Bill emerged in the aftermath of the 2024 protests, with the government under pressure to raise revenue without reigniting public anger over taxation. The Treasury presented its proposals largely as measures to improve compliance and close loopholes, but the bill also proposed substantive changes to Value Added Tax (VAT) exemptions and other tax provisions that could increase costs for businesses and consumers. The proposed measures were expected to raise approximately KSh 25–35 billion in additional revenue.

By 2026, the pressure to raise revenue had not eased. The government was still grappling with public debt and a difficult economic climate, while households and businesses faced the question of how much more they could absorb. The proposed tax measures were projected to generate approximately KSh 98.9 billion in additional revenue, largely through administrative reforms, tax base expansion, and improved compliance. The bill sparked debate over a proposed increase in mobile phone excise duty from 10 percent to 25 percent, potential VAT changes affecting digital payment services, and proposed taxes on

mitumba

 imports. Other concerns centered on VAT exemptions for locally manufactured goods, access to taxpayer data by the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), and the effect of proposed tax changes on workers’ take-home pay.

In a live lecture, Churchill Ogutu helps make sense of the Finance Bill 2026, taking its figures and proposals out of the language of legislation and placing them in their wider economic context. The government’s revised tax revenue target rises from about KSh 2.6 trillion in FY26 to KSh 2.86 trillion in FY27, with the Finance Bill expected to generate

approximately KSh 98.9 billion

 in additional revenue from the proposed tax measures.

On May 21, 2026, four days before the deadline for public submissions on the bill, Churchill Ogutu delivered a lecture to

Bunge la Mayut

 on the Finance Bill 2026. He set out the budget cycle and revenue targets behind the bill, then walked through its proposed amendments to seven tax laws — the Income Tax Act, the Value Added Tax Act, the Excise Duty Act, the Tax Procedures Act, the Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act, the Stamp Duty Act, and the road maintenance levy — before fielding questions from Keith Ang’ana on the 25 percent excise duty on mobile phones, the taxation of retained profits as deemed dividends, the powers of the Kenya Revenue Authority, and the prospects for PAYE relief. A cleaned transcript follows. Shilling figures are converted to US dollars at approximately KSh 129.5 to the dollar, the prevailing rate at the time, and rounded. Submissions closed on May 25. The National Assembly passed the bill on June 18, and President William Ruto signed it into law on June 23, after MPs dropped some of its most contentious proposals, including the increase in excise duty on mobile phones.

Churchill Ogutu is head of research at Capital A Investment Bank, which he joined in April 2026 after more than 15 years in financial markets in Kenya and across Africa. He was previously an economist in IC Group’s pan-African asset management division and head of research at Genghis Capital, and is an advisor at Plato Group, a global economic and political advisory firm. He holds a BSc in actuarial science from the University of Nairobi and is a member of the Economists Society of Kenya. Keith Ang’ana is a writer based in Nairobi and the founder of Bunge la Mayut. author: ROAPE
title: Statement of the Finishers Revolutionary Movement
content:
At the beginning of this year, young Ugandans (activists, researchers, academics and lawyers) came together under one roof to confront a question that could no longer be postponed: what becomes of Uganda after the sham elections of January 2026?


With the possibility of Muhoozi Kainerugaba succeeding his father, we gathered around a simple conviction: Uganda must not be handed from one generation of the same ruling family to another. Succession is not liberation. Changing the face at the top while preserving the same machinery of patronage, militarism and corruption is not the future Uganda deserves.


Under the name Finishers Revolutionary Movement, we committed ourselves to organizing Ugandans to reject this succession project and to take up the unfinished work of national democratic liberation.


What we stand for


The Finishers is more than a name. It is an idea: that Uganda’s liberation cannot remain an unfinished historical promise, and that our generation has a responsibility to finish the task. That means we will:


End dictatorship.


Dismantle systems of patronage and impunity.


Reclaim democratic power for the people.


Build a country capable of true economic independence.


What have we done


Since the beginning of the year, we have been organizing, teaching and rallying people to confront injustice and corruption and to recover the spirit of resistance that every generation of Ugandans has inherited. We have reminded our people that oppression survives not only through the violence of the state, but also through fear, silence and the belief that nothing can change.


Because political freedoms in Uganda have been brutally restricted, we have had to organize with caution. Much of our work has been quiet and covert, because even the ordinary act of bringing Ugandans together has become dangerous.


Why we write in mourning


In the last month, the state has descended on the Finishers with an iron hand. Three of our comrades have been arrested or disappeared.


Praise Aloikin 

was arrested, later released on court bail, and continues to face the state through an ongoing court case.


Byakika Abubaker 

and 

David Musiri 

have been taken, and their whereabouts remain unknown.


We mourn them. We fear for them. We are angry.


Yet we refuse to let their disappearance become the disappearance of an idea. The state may arrest a Finisher. It may abduct a Finisher. It may intimidate a Finisher. But it cannot arrest the hunger for freedom that brought us together.


We are Finishers. We are not terrorists. We are young Ugandans who looked at the country we are inheriting and decided we cannot remain spectators to its destruction. We chose to organize. We chose to resist. And we choose to continue.


Our demands


That the state immediately disclose the whereabouts of Byakika Abubaker and David Musiri, and return them safely to their families.


That the state end enforced disappearances and abductions of Ugandans for their political beliefs and organizing.


That the state stop criminalizing the right to organize, assemble and hold political ideas.


That Praise Aloikin be afforded a fair process, and that the case against her be dropped.


Our appeal to the people of Uganda


Do not leave the Finishers alone. Protect your own. Protect the people who are standing up for the country we all claim to love.


When a Finisher is taken, ask where they are. When a family is left searching for a disappeared son or daughter, stand with that family. When the state attempts to criminalize an idea, refuse to repeat its lies. When fear tells you to look away, remember that the person taken today could be your neighbour, your child, your brother, your sister, or you tomorrow.


The Finishers belong to the people, and so does the idea. You do not have to carry our name to carry it. You do not have to stand where we stand to believe that dictatorship must end. You do not have to be an activist to understand that Uganda cannot be inherited like a family estate


Our resolve


We do not know what the state will do next. We know only that repression is meant to make us disappear one by one, to isolate us from each other and to convince Uganda that resistance is futile. We refuse that outcome.


The disappearance of our comrades has deepened our grief, but it has also clarified our resolve. We will remember those who have been taken. We will stand with their families. We will demand their return. And we will continue the …

author: Farai Shawn Matiashe
title: Electrification in Africa means closing the energy access gap and reducing energy poverty
content:
At the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the COP31 presidency is pushing for a global target to increase electricity’s share of final energy consumption to

35% by 2035

, a central pillar of the conference.


The COP31 Turkish presidency proposed the global electrification target at the 2026 Bonn Climate Change Conference in June to encourage countries and businesses worldwide to electrify transport, buildings, and industry using renewable energy, helping to accelerate the shift away from fossil fuels.


But as delegates gather in the Mediterranean country for the climate summit known as Conference of the Parties 31 (COP31), the target risks overlooking the different energy realities Africa faces unless they place energy access and development at its centre.


For industrialised economies, electrification is all about replacing existing fossil fuel systems, while in Africa, some countries still want to build electricity infrastructure and distribution networks.


The new target, up from the current global rate of electrification of about 20%, comes at a time when Africa faces energy poverty and a huge electricity access gap.


About 600 million people lack electricity access, with half of them living in three countries, namely Nigeria, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo,

according

 to the International Energy Agency.


Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for roughly 85% of the global population lacking electricity.


The 35 by 35 risks widening existing energy inequality


Dr Chigozie Nweke-Eze, founder of the Integrated Africa Power (IAP), an enterprise focused on solving energy and infrastructure deficits across the African continent, said the proposed 35 by 35 target risks overlooking the different energy realities Africa faces.


Some of the solar panels which are part of a solar mini grid in Hakwata Chipinge in Zimbabwe. Photo by Farai Shawn Matiashe.


“There is a fundamental distinction between the energy transition in industrialised economies and that in many African countries,” he said.


“There is also a risk that a global target expressed as the share of electricity in final energy consumption could obscure inequalities between countries.”


Nweke-Eze said a global increase in electricity consumption does not mean improved energy access for populations that remain disconnected from the grid.


“Nor does it automatically address the affordability and reliability of electricity for households and small businesses,” he said.


In industrialised economies, electrification is largely about replacing petrol and diesel vehicles with electric vehicles, and industrial gas boilers and household gas heaters with electric heat pumps.


For Africa, it means it must build entirely new energy systems to support its expanding population and development aspirations. The continent is simultaneously attempting to shift towards renewable energy that is both cleaner and more sustainable.


Nweke-Eze said electrification cannot happen at scale without adequate generation capacity, transmission and distribution networks, reliable electricity supply, and affordable connections.


But Nweke-Eze said that Africa should be an integral part of the 35-by-35 ambition, with the target adapted to the continent’s unique energy context, recognising its diverse starting points and prioritising pathways that expand energy access and address the needs of underserved communities.


Another initiative

launched

 at COP31 is the Global Rooftop Solar Declaration, which aims to double the number of solar-powered households globally to 300 million by 2030. Endorsed by a cross-continental coalition including Kenya and Nigeria, the initiative offers a practical pathway to addressing Africa’s energy access gap by accelerating the deployment of household solar, particularly in communities underserved by centralised electricity grids.


It focuses on overcoming barriers such as high upfront costs, complex permitting processes and skills shortages that can slow the adoption of decentralised

solar solutions

.


This, Nweke-Eze argued, also requires a broader understanding of how progress towards electrification is measured. Africa should not be judged solely against the pace at which industrialised economies replace fossil-fuel technologies, but also by how effectively its countries expand electricity access, develop productive energy infrastructure and improve the quality of energy services.

author: WoMin
title: Women Unite to Defend the Congo Basin Against Extractivism – A Call for Climate Justice at COP31
content:
As world leaders gather in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), taking place from 9–20 November 2026, women from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the Republic of Congo and Cameroon are raising an urgent message: there can be no climate justice without defending the Congo Basin, protecting community territories and recognising the leadership of women on the frontlines of environmental struggles.


The Congo Basin is one of the world’s most important ecological treasures, acting as the “

second lungs

 of the Earth”, after the Amazon, which is being decimated. Spanning over four million square kilometres across six countries, its forests, rivers and peatlands play a vital role in regulating the global climate, protecting biodiversity and sustaining millions of people. For Indigenous Peoples and local communities, the forest is not simply a natural resource; it is their home, heritage, identity and source of life.


Yet this vital ecosystem faces growing threats from mining, logging, oil and gas extraction, deforestation and expanding infrastructure. Across the Congo Basin, rising demand for minerals is increasing pressure on forests and community territories.


Recent investigations have

documented

 mining concessions overlapping with community forests in the DRC, gold-mining-related

forest destruction and water pollution

 in the Republic of Congo, and

concerns over the impacts

 of the Lobé-Kribi iron-ore project on forests and livelihoods in Cameroon.


This exposes a growing contradiction: while governments promote renewable energy as a solution to the climate crisis, the extraction of minerals needed for the energy transition can create new threats to forests, water resources and the communities that depend on them.


For women in the Congo Basin, this is not an abstract debate. It means polluted rivers, disappearing food sources, loss of agricultural land and declining access to forests.


Women on the frontlines expose the cost of extractivism


To strengthen collective resistance, women and community organisations from the DRC, the Republic of Congo and Cameroon came together for a

cross-border solidarity exchange

 to share stories of resistance, expose the impacts of extractivism and develop strategies to defend the Congo Basin.


Over three days, organisations including

Centre d’Encadrement pour la Promotion de la Femme et la jeune fille

 (CEPF),

Dynamique des femmes pour le développement

 (DYFED),

Green Development Advocates

 (GDA), and the Association pour le Respect des Droit des population autochtones et du développement rural et du Droit de l’homme (ARPA2DH)

shared their experiences and struggles. Testimonies from women in Lessoukou, Mayoko, Mangi, Bongonde and Bandzonko revealed the devastating impacts of mining and forest exploitation.


In Lessoukou, 17 of the community’s 24 villages are reportedly occupied by mining companies, threatening access to ancestral lands and traditional livelihoods. Élisé Matsanga, an Indigenous woman from Lessoukou, shared:


“

Agriculture once enabled us to feed our families and send our children to school. Today, because of corporate activities and the loss of access to our lands, we can no longer farm as we used to. We have lost our livelihoods

.”


In Mangi, Tshopo Province, Nyota described how communities are excluded from decisions affecting their territories while rivers become increasingly polluted.


“

We are forced to walk up to three kilometres to find safe drinking water, and sometimes even our children have no choice but to drink polluted water. Our lands, forests and rivers are our sources of livelihood, yet we watch helplessly as they are destroyed

.”


In Bandzonko, Republic of Congo, Odile, the village chief,

described how mining pollution

 has forced women to walk up to 15 kilometres in search of water, exposing families to serious health risks. In Bongonde, Équateur Province, Annie Mboyo, a community woman,

highlighted the disappearance

 of mushrooms, caterpillars, wild fruits and fish, resources that have traditionally sustained community food systems. Meanwhile, in Mayoko, Oko Jeanine, another community woman, denounced the lack of consultation and the destruction of agricultural fields by mining companies.

These lands belong to us. They are our heritage, our livelihoods and our identity. How can companies demand that we obtain permits to cultivate our own land while they extract …
