author: Stelinsky
title: Ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους του αγώνα
content:
«Ο φασισμός δεν έρχεται από το μέλλον, καινούργιο τάχα κάτι να μας φέρει». Δεν εμφανίζεται σαν κεραυνός εν αιθρία και η επανάνοδός του δεν αποτελεί έκπληξη. Αποτελεί βασική δικλείδα ασφαλείας για το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο: Είναι το πιο σκληρό τους πολιτικό εργαλείο, το οποίο αντλείται από την ίδια εργαλειοθήκη που περιέχει και τη δημοκρατία. «Αναβιώνει», πάντα, όταν η τελευταία παρουσιάζεται αδύναμη να διαχειριστεί τον κοινωνικό και ταξικό ανταγωνισμό, για να τις παράσχει εξωθεσμικές λύσεις.

Σε μια συγκυρία γενικευμένης πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, η εθνικιστική ιδεολογία εξυπηρετεί τη στροφή του πολιτικού σκηνικού σε ζητήματα «εθνικής κυριαρχίας» και αυστηρότερες συνοριακές πολιτικές. Ταυτόχρονα, η διάχυση του ρατσιστικού μίσους στην κοινωνία έρχεται να πλαισιώσει τις κρατικές αφηγήσεις περί εσωτερικού εχθρού – διεργασία που κυρίως γίνεται μέσα από τη στοχοποίηση των μεταναστ(ρι)ών, και τις επαναλαμβανόμενες αναφορές περί «συνεχούς επίθεσης και εισβολής», με σκοπό τον αποπροσανατολισμό της κοινωνικής βάσης από τα βασικά αίτια εξαθλίωσης της ζωής της, και τη συσπείρωσή της γύρω από την εθνική ιδεολογία.

Παράλληλα, οι φασίστες αποτελούν τον απαραίτητο παρακρατικό μηχανισμό που θα αναμετρηθεί με το ανταγωνιστικό κίνημα απέναντι στις επερχόμενες κοινωνικές διεκδικήσεις και αντιστάσεις: Μηχανισμός που δεν υπόκειται στους περιορισμούς της νομιμότητας, και με όρους δρόμου, δρα συμπληρωματικά στο μονοπώλιο της νόμιμης βίας του κράτους. Είναι ακόμα νωπές οι μνήμες από τη δράση των φασιστών κατά τα ταραχώδη χρόνια που ακολούθησαν την εξέγερση του 2008. Τότε, αφενός η προβολή της Χρυσής Αυγής από τα καθεστωτικά media, και αφετέρου η στήριξή της και η συνεργασία με κυβερνητικά στελέχη (κυρίως της Δεξιάς) συνέδραμαν προς αυτήν ακριβώς την κατεύθυνση. Ταυτόχρονα, η δραστηριότητά της αξιοποιήθηκε ως «αντιπολιτευτική» πίεση εκ δεξιών, ώστε το κράτος να ενσωματώσει υπό τον δημοκρατικό μανδύα τα προτάγματά της (χαρακτηριστικά παραδείγματα οι κρατικές επιχειρήσεις-σκούπα «Ξένιος Δίας» στο κέντρο της Αθήνας, όπως και οι επιθέσεις μπάτσων από κοινού με ναζί απέναντι σε αγωνιστές). Κατά τραγική ειρωνεία, η κυβέρνηση Σαμαρά, βασικός υποστηρικτής της Χ.Α., καρπώθηκε και την αντιφασιστική «αναγνώριση» ως αυτή που έβαλε τους φασίστες στη φυλακή. Εκείνα τα χρόνια, βέβαια, το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα έδωσε μεγάλες μάχες στους δρόμους, αναχαιτίζοντας επιτυχώς το φασιστικό φαινόμενο, διατηρώντας διαρκώς οξυμένα τα αντιφασιστικά κοινωνικά αντανακλαστικά.

Το τελευταίο διάστημα, η ακροδεξιά ρητορική και ο φασιστικός οχετός αναβιώνουν σε επίπεδο κεντρικής πολιτικής σκηνής, σε παγκόσμιο κλίμακα. Από τις ΗΠΑ και τη ρατσιστική αντιμεταναστευτική πολιτική του Τραμπ (ICE, τοίχος στα σύνορα με το Μεξικό, απελάσεις μεταναστ-ρι-ών), την επάνοδο ακροδεξιών φιλοαμερικανικών κυβερνήσεων σε χώρες της Νότιας Αμερικής (Χιλή, Βολιβία, Βενεζουέλα, Αργεντινή), μέχρι την εφαρμογή αντιμεταναστευτικών πολιτικών από χώρες της Ευρώπης (κλειστά σύνορα, pushbacks, κατάργηση ασύλου) και την άνοδο ακροδεξιών κομμάτων σε πολλές από αυτές (Ουγγαρία, Αυστρία, Γερμανία, Ιταλία, Γαλλία, Ουκρανία). Και φυσικά τη συνεχιζόμενη εξολόθρευση του παλαιστινιακού λαού από το γενοκτονικό κράτος του Ισραήλ, με τη στήριξη και συμμετοχή των ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ-ΕΕ.

Όλη αυτή η διεργασία διεξάγεται με τηναδιαμφισβήτητη στήριξη εκπροσώπων του κεφαλαίου: Ένας από τους πλουσιότερους ανθρώπους του πλανήτη, ο Ίλον Μάσκ, επιλέγει να στηρίζει οικονομικά την άνοδο φασιστικών/ακροδεξιών κομμάτων και οργανώσεων σε ολόκληρο τον κόσμο (Ρεπουμπλικάνοι-Τραμπ στις ΗΠΑ, Εθνικό Μέτωπο-Λεπεν στη Γαλλία, Λίγκα του Βορρά-Μελόνι στην Ιταλία, AfD-Βάιντελ στη Γερμανία, Κασιδιάρης στην Ελλάδα). Παράλληλα, η στήριξη κολοσσών της ενέργειας, μεγάλων βιομηχανιών και εταιρειών προς το κράτος του Ισραήλ, ώστε να συνεχίζει, χωρίς οικονομικό κόστος, το αιματοκύλισμα των Παλαιστινίων, αποτελεί την ιστορική συνέχεια της σύνδεσης βιομηχάνων-ναζί από τον Β’ Παγκόσμιο Πόλεμο.

Στον μικρόκοσμο της ελλαδικής επικράτειας, οι πολιτικές που εφαρμόζονται ενάντια στις/στους μετανάστ(ρι)ες (επανεξέταση ασύλων και αναστολή υποβολής νέων αιτήσεων, μαζικές δολοφονίες στην Πύλο και στην Χίο, pushbacks, τείχος στον Έβρο, στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης-κράτησης), όσο και η εθνικιστική ρητορική περί «εθνικών απειλών» και διαφύλαξης της «εδαφικής ακεραιότητας»συνθέτουν ένα ολοκληρωτικό τοπίο. Εντός αυτού λαμβάνει χώρα η αποφυλάκιση του Ηλία Κασιδιάρη, όπως και η ευρύτερη εμφάνιση φασιστικής δραστηριότητας, εν όψει και των επερχόμενων εκλογών: Από τη διάρρηξη στο 2ο …

author: Michael_1973
title: Socialism or Barbarism? - S'bu Zikode
content:
Keynote address by S'bu Zikode, from Abahlali baseMjondolo, at the Third National Conference of the Aotearoa New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies held in Ōtepoti Dunedin, on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

Comrade Programme director, thank you for welcoming me to Aotearoa once again. May I express my sincere gratitude to the New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies and Palestine Solidarity Network Aotearoa for inviting me to speak here today, and across the country. I bring greetings from Abahlali baseMjondolo, our movement in South Africa which now has more than 200,000 members.

I want to begin with the words of a song, a song about socialism, that is often sung in the struggles of the left in South Africa.

Yini iSocialism? Umhlaba wonke ezandleni zabantu Akunamuntu, akunamuntu ongaphatha umhlaba ngayedwa Ayayesaba bo, ayesaba amabhujwa, nongxiwa Ngoba bona, ngobabona befuna ukusetshenzelwa ngabantu

The song asks, ‘What is socialism?’ It answers that socialism is the whole world in the hands of the people. It goes on to say that no one person can own the world on their own. It concludes that the bourgeoisie are afraid of socialism, because they want the people to work for them.

Comrades, as you will all know, in 1915, during the mass slaughter of the First World War, Rosa Luxemburg wrote from a prison cell in Germany that humanity stood at a crossroads. Either it would move towards socialism, towards global justice and peace, or it would collapse into further barbarism. She was writing as millions of workers were being sent to kill each other in the trenches for the profits of their rulers. Four years later she was murdered.

In our movement we have our own version of this choice. Lindokuhle Mnguni, the gifted young chairperson of one of our branches, the eKhenana Commune in Durban, introduced the slogan ‘Socialism or Death’ into our movement. For Lindokuhle, socialism was not something that would come one day in the future, after a revolution, or after an election. Socialism had to be lived now, in the way we occupy land, ensure that it is not bought and sold, manage it democratically, grow food together, ensure that nobody goes hungry, care for each other, build and manage social infrastructure like halls, creches and kitchens, and make decisions together.

For us, like urban and rural movements elsewhere in the world, building socialism from below means building communes, connecting them and building wider forms of democratic popular power from these communes. In the same way that the liberated zones were the bases for anti-colonial movements in countries like Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau, communes – from South Africa to Brazil, Venezuela and elsewhere – are the strongest bases for our movements to build socialism. As Ruthie Wilson Gilmore says, ‘Freedom is a place’.

The price for challenging oppression can be very high. Many comrades around the world have given their lives. On 20 August 2022, Lindokuhle was shot dead in his home. He was the third leader of the eKhenana Commune to be assassinated in less than six months.

Frantz Fanon taught that ‘Each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfill it, or betray it.’ Comrades like Rosa Luxemburg and Lindokuhle Mnguni understood the mission of their generation, and gave their lives to it. Our generation also has a mission. We are living in a time of genocide, of wealth beyond imagination for a few and hunger for millions, of the far right and fascist forces rising and of the poor being turned against each other. We have to decide whether we will fulfil our mission or betray it. In our movement we have often used Fanon’s words. When people find themselves pushed to the margins of the city and of life, they have the opportunity to discover their mission and to decide whether they want to fulfil it or betray it.

I want to speak today about the barbarism that we see around us, in South Africa and around the world, and about the work of building socialism from below, as we have tried to do it in our movement.

When Luxemburg wrote about barbarism she was thinking of the slaughter of the First World War. Today we are witnessing another mass slaughter of human beings. We have all watched the genocide in Gaza. We have watched children being starved, hospitals and schools being bombed, and whole families being buried under the rubble of their homes. We have watched the most powerful governments in the world supply the weapons …

author: AusDemWeg
title: Neue Broschüre: Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs
content:
Auf unserer Website

www.ausdemweg.net/downloads/

 ist ab sofort unsere erste Broschüre „Der Antikapitalismus des III. Wegs“ zum Download bereit. Die Broschüre umfasst unsere drei bereits veröffentlichten Texte zum Thema, sowie eine Einleitung und einen Prolog, der auf die Rolle der Sozialpolitik im historischen Nationalsozialismus im Zuge der Machtergreifung eingeht. Falls ihr die Texte auf unserer Website verpasst habt oder nochmal alles in hübschem Design nachlesen wollt ist das jetzt die perfekte Gelegenheit.


Es stellt sich die berechtigte Frage, warum so viel Arbeit und Energie in eine Auseinandersetzung mit der Ideologie einer kleinen faschistischen Partei gesteckt werden sollte. Schließlich hat die antifaschistische Bewegung in der Vergangenheit oft sehr erfolgreich Treffpunkte und Kader solcher Gruppen oder Parteien unter Druck gesetzt. Doch einerseits funktionieren diese Vorgehensweisen bei wirklich großen Organisationen wie der AFD nicht mehr und andererseits bilden sich insbesondere in den letzten Jahren an vielen Orten wo faschistische Strukturen zerschlagen wurden wieder neue Zusammenhänge. Es reicht offenbar nicht die feindliche Bewegung zu zerstören, da sich nach einigen Jahren einfach eine neue bildet.


Der III. Weg ist eine Partei, die bundesweit viele erfahrene und gut organisierte Nazis in einer Partei vereinen konnte. Auch wenn die Partei immer wieder Rückschläge erlitten hat, ist ein stetiges Wachstum der Strukturen erkennbar. Ein Teil dieses Wachstums ist eine immer größere Zahl von Broschüren und Büchern im parteieigenen Onlineshop. Aktuell sind dort zehn Bücher und vier Broschüren erhältlich, wobei auch einige Schriften fehlen. Es wäre demnach ein Fehler der Partei wie der lokalen Kameradschaft eine mangelnde theoretische Grundlage zu unterstellen. Auch in den Reden und den Beiträgen in den sozialen Medien zeigt sich, dass diese theoretische Grundlage durchaus Anwendung findet.


Die Auseinandersetzung mit den Schriften der Nazis zeigt wenig überraschend eine Vielzahl an Schwächen, die ausgenutzt werden könnten. Dabei geht es sowohl um die innere Logik in ihrer Ideologie, als auch um Grundannahmen und sich daraus ergebende Theorien. Es wäre daher wünschenswert, wenn die antifaschistische Bewegung in Zukunft neben dem Kampf gegen faschistische Infrastruktur und die Aktivisten auch die inhaltliche Auseinandersetzung vorantreibt. Abgesehen davon hilft eine solche Auseinandersetzung mit den Positionen des Gegners auch bei der Schärfung der eignen politischen Vorstellungen. All das kann der antifaschistischen Bewegung nur gut tun.

author: Helmut Weiss
title: AfD-Meldeportale gegen Lehrerinnen und Lehrer: Teil einer weltweiten Kampagne der Rechten gegen emanzipativen Unterricht
content:
Dossier


Der

faschistische brasilianische Präsidentschaftskandidat

 hat es im Programm: Schule ohne Parteien (was bedeutet, schön, wie früher, kolonialistisch lehren, das Land sei am 22. April 1500 von den Portugiesen „entdeckt“ worden); die Teesäufer des Herrn Trump haben es als Ziel: Ideologiefreie Schulen (sprich wir haben den „Wilden Westen“ zivilisiert und die paar toten Indianer haben es eh verdient) und noch mehrere andere. Indische Safran-Faschisten wollen den muslimischen Teil der eigenen Geschichte nicht gerne hören, bei Orban sollen die Kinder auf Panzern rumklettern statt Sozialkunde  und so weiter – da konnte ein rechtsradikaler Ideologen-Verein wie die AFD nicht fehlen: Neutrale Schule nennen sie ihr Denunziations-Programm, erfindungsreich waren sie halt noch nie.

Die Neutralität

 soll dann vermutlich anfangen bei historischen völkischen Idiotien wie etwa der Frankenkönig (und Sachsenschlächter) sei der erste „deutsche“ Kaiser gewesen und enden mit dem Ende des Lehrplanes in bezug auf Nazi-Diktatur und (natürlich, schon aus Eigeninteresse) Kritik an Rassismus aller Art. Erfindungsreicher allemal als AFD-Hetze ist etwa der Protestmodus der fzs gegen diesen Vorstoß. Siehe dazu das allgemeine Echo auf die AFD-Denunziantenkampagne, gewerkschaftliche Stellungnahme und weitere Informationen:


AfD setzt Lehrkräfte unter Druck – Forscher fordert: „Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung“


„Sozialwissenschaftler Tim Engartner erklärt, warum politische Neutralität im Unterricht weder möglich noch gewünscht ist. Er fordert mehr Courage – auch angesichts der AfD-Meldeportale.


Erstarkende Kräfte von Rechts, namentlich die AfD, fordern Lehrkräfte zunehmend dazu auf, sich politisch neutral zu verhalten und berufen sich dabei unter anderem auf den Beutelsbacher Konsens. Der ist seit 50 Jahren die Grundlage politischer Bildung. Im Interview erklärt der Sozialwissenschaftler der Universität zu Köln, Tim Engartner, warum Lehrkräfte nicht nur Haltung zeigen dürfen, sondern sogar müssen, wo Grenzen von Meinungsfreiheit und politischer Einflussnahme liegen und weshalb der Beutelsbacher Konsens angesichts sozialer Medien und gesellschaftlicher Polarisierung weiterentwickelt werden sollte. (…)


Der Beutelsbacher Konsens kennt kein Neutralitätsgebot. Es geht darum, politische Mündigkeit und Urteilsfähigkeit zu fördern – und gerade nicht darum, politische Positionen aus dem Unterricht herauszuhalten.


[Was soll eine Lehrkraft tun, wenn sie von Schülerinnen und Schülern nach ihrer politischen Einstellung gefragt wird?]

Ja, das ist eindeutig erlaubt. Sie dürfte auch sagen, dass sie persönlich die AfD für eine Partei hält, die menschenfeindliche Positionen vertritt. Wo genau die Grenze zwischen zulässiger Kritik und unzulässiger Abwertung liegt, ist umstritten – und muss im Einzelfall entschieden werden. Was aber klar ist: Schulen und Lehrkräfte müssen zwar parteipolitisch neutral sein, nicht aber wertneutral. Das ist zentral. (…)


[Kann man denn politisch neutral unterrichten?]


Ich halte das für geradezu unmöglich – und es ist auch nicht das Ziel. Im Gegenteil: Die Lehrkraft soll ihre politische Position durchaus deutlich machen, um Diskussionen anzuregen. (…)


Mehr Haltung statt Zurückhaltung, denn wer schweigt, stimmt zu. Allerdings hat auch die Schulleitung eine wichtige Aufgabe: Sie muss die Lehrkräfte schützen, ihnen den Rücken stärken und darf nicht zulassen, dass Eltern oder auch Parteien einzelne Lehrkräfte persönlich anzugreifen, obwohl diese unsere demokratischen Werte verteidigen

author: Unknown
title: Women hold dialogue workshop in Qamishlo
content:
The workshop was attended by 300 participants, including members of women’s movements and organisations, as well as female intellectuals and politicians. Discussions focused on political and legal violence and the role of women in integration.


The declaration issued following the workshop highlighted the following points:


1. Guaranteeing women’s rights in the Syrian constitution and ensuring equality between women and men. No discrimination should be made on the basis of gender, nationality or religion, and women’s rights should be constitutionally guaranteed.


2. Guaranteeing women’s participation in legislative, executive, administrative and judicial institutions, ensuring that they are represented and have decision-making power at every level.


3. Guaranteeing education in the mother tongue in the constitution.


4. Fighting political and institutional violence against women, as well as taking a stand against policies of ignoring women. Women must be guaranteed the right to organise, express their opinions and participate in politics.


5. Protecting women from violence through laws and mechanisms. Ending domestic, social, economic and sexual violence, and punishing those who perpetrate violence against women. Ensuring women’s access to justice and protecting all women without discrimination.


6. Strengthening the role of women’s movements and organisations and ensuring their participation in the peace process and transitional justice.


7. Establishing autonomous mechanisms to legally pursue violations against women. Punishing those who undermine women’s achievements and rights.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: World of Hurt
content:
Abolitionist Reflections on the Root Causes of Harm


from the

CrimethInc.

 collective, 17/11/2026


What causes people to harm others? Reactionaries label certain individuals—or, worse, entire demographics—inherently harmful to justify their own efforts to inflict harm via vigilante attacks, policing, and the court system. Others suggest that experiencing harm can lead some to harm others, as suggested by the common catchphrase “

Hurt people hurt people

.” Here, we examine this popular notion and propose a more useful framework for understanding the root causes of harm.


Today, a ruling class headed by billionaires and aspiring autocrats is making

the celebration of violence

 central to their narratives and policies, openly campaigning against empathy itself. In this context, the question of what causes harm—and how to interrupt it without reinforcing cycles of suffering and oppression—has become increasingly urgent.


World of Hurt


Abolitionists

 who envision a world without

police

 or

prisons

 often face questions about how to address serious forms of interpersonal harm.

Mutual aid

 and resource redistribution may reduce behaviors that arise as a consequence of lack of access to basic needs. But how can we understand those who seem to hurt others out of cruelty or disregard? If we don’t accept the idea that some people are monsters who must be locked up to keep the rest of us safe, how can we make sense of their actions?


Defenders of the criminal legal system frequently cite rape and abuse to justify prisons and imprisonment. In response, abolitionists have devoted considerable energy to developing

alternative approaches

 to addressing sexual violence. Groups such as Generation Five have proposed

principles for responding to child sexual abuse

 through transformative justice frameworks. By focusing on one of the most stigmatized forms of harm, they aim to cut to the root of

carceral thinking

 in order to reimagine safety and justice.


But creative responses beyond the state are not enough. To end sexual violence, we also need to understand its root causes.


Feminist activists coined the term “

rape culture

” to describe how social norms and institutions enable sexual harm. In addition to these structural effects of gender and power, others argue that past experiences of harm shape the behavior of individuals who go on to harm others. One of the most common ways to articulate this principle appears in the phrase “

Hurt people hurt people

.”


Let’s take a closer look to see where this popular saying came from, how it is used, and its implications for an abolitionist understanding of harm.


The Trajectory of a Slogan


From

self-help books

 and

therapist blogs

 to the

writings of abolitionist activists

, “hurt people hurt people” has become an influential account of the psychology of violence. It suggests that some people harm others not because they are pathological monsters, but because they too are victims whose unresolved trauma shapes their hurtful actions.


The precise origins of the phrase are opaque, but it has been in circulation

at least since the 1950s

. It seems to have begun trending in the 1990s in therapeutic and pop psychology circles. A popular 1993 Christian self-help book titled

Hurt People Hurt People

 promised to support readers in healing from painful past relationships “with empathy and biblical insight.” In recent years, this phrase has been repeated by everyone from megachurch pastor Rick Warren to Hollywood actor Andrew Garfield to the stripper con artist character Destiny in the movie

Hustlers

 to

the metal band Mudvayne

. It appears most widely in discourse about therapy, self-help, trauma, and religion.


On the surface, “hurt people hurt people” might seem an odd slogan for radical critics of the

prison industrial complex

. As a maxim of folk wisdom that spans mainstream, religious, feminist, and radical circles, we should consider carefully whether it aligns with our values.


In some ways, it makes sense that abolitionists would find this formulation promising. It humanizes people who cause harm, whereas dehumanizing them paves the way for carceral responses. It attributes the roots of harmful behavior not to inherent depravity, but to contingent circumstances that can be changed. It resonates with the lived experiences of some people who are struggling to heal and to be accountable for hurting others. It seems to offer a hopeful …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Lo Ta-yu Stokes Controversy for Comments Lashing Out at Pan-Green Camp, Misogyny
content:
ICONIC SINGER-SONGWRITER Lo Ta-yu provoked controversy earlier this month after comments in an interview lashing out at the pan-Green camp.

Some of Lo’s comments strayed into misogyny. Specifically, Lo lashed out at former President Tsai Ing-wen and current Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim for being unmarried women who do not have children. Lo claimed that this marked their unsuitability for public office, in that not having children meant that they did not have a stake in the future of Taiwanese society.

Such claims have been used against Tsai and Hsiao in the past, as a form of misogyny directed at female politicians. Indeed, such claims have also occurred from within the pan-Green camp. Veteran independence activist and entrepreneur Koo Kwang-ming, who died in 2023 at age 96, previously made comments suggesting that the ROC military should not be led by a woman who wears a skirt, and suggesting that Tsai not having children made her unsuitable to lead the DPP. Koo suggested, then, that Tsai should step aside to become “mother of the nation” and allow a male leader–his preference being current president Lai Ching-te–to take power. Koo backed Lai in his unsuccessful challenge against Lai in 2020 for the DPP’s presidential nomination.

Nevertheless, one notes that frequent public scrutiny of female politicians has led many female politicians to remain unmarried in the public eye. Despite Taiwan’s prevalence of female politicians in both the pan-Green and pan-Blue camps, gendered biases against female politicians remain strong. Tsai later responded to Lo, criticizing his depiction of her as uninvested in Taiwan’s future.

Other comments by Lo lashed out at music critic Ma Shih-fan, long a champion of Lo’s work, as favoring the pan-Green camp, alleging that Ma was paid off by the pan-Green camp. Ma later responded by quoting Lo’s lyrics in a social media post in what was perceived as a veiled criticism of Lo. Among the online responses to Lo’s attacks on Ma was the view that Lo had unfairly attacked someone who had historically been one of his promoters.

Lo is a figure that is best known as associated with the 1970s campus folk song movement. Among his best-known songs is Lukang, the Little Town, highlighting the stark contrast between his rural hometown of Lukang and the bright lights of Taipei. At the same time, Lo’s pan-Blue-leaning views are well-known, in that while Lo previously criticized both camps, he eventually veered more toward the stances of the KMT. This included participating in commemorations of Ma Ying-jeou’s election victory.

Indeed, one notes that many artistic figures who are strongly associated with Taiwanese identity, such as filmmaker Hou Hsiao-hsien and fellow singer-songwriter Lim Giong, are in fact known for starkly pan-Blue views. This has at times included openly campaigning for KMT politicians, or lending the weight of their cultural prestige to the KMT. At the same time, one notes that in the present, there are fewer and fewer cultural figures who hold such views, which may be why Lo’s comments led to such controversy–as well as through the expression of misogynistic views seen as out of step with the times.

The Anarchist Network of “Vancouver Island” (“Victoria”) remembers our comrade Tasha Diamant fondly.

Tasha was a passionate ecological artist, firebrand sneaky actionist, a loving mother, rageful ecofeminist, and matriarch of the Network.

Tasha was an ardent revolutionary mother who fought against patriarchy, hierarchy, and colonization. She was a prolific organizer and consciousness raiser in “Victoria” (Lekwungen), anchoring major in-city supports and disruptions to bolster direct actions against domination in all its forms.

She also spearheaded The Human Body Project to rouse consciousness; in a misogynistic, dissociative society. She at the time did not have words for what she later understood simply as a violent culture, instead using her naked body to share and create space for vulnerability and a process of bearing witness to self participation in estrangement.

These consciousness raising efforts culminated in hundreds of street actions and performances. This work also extended itself into Humans of Fairy Creek, a theatrical series that focused on humanizing the thousands of arrestees in the struggle ignored by the self-appointed hierarchics in the Fairy Creek leadership.

While Tasha herself did not identify as an anarchist, (preferring the label ‘ecofeminist’) she was most often aligned with anti-patriarchal, anti-capitalist, and anti-hierarchical modes of organizing.

Tasha started FreeSkool Victoria in 2022, was involved in the ‘Victoria’ Anarchist Bookfair Collective in 2023, and supporting the People’s Park Palestine liberation encampment on the University of Victoria quad in 2025 through an “Elders” affinity group she started.

Upon connecting with anarchist youths (note from some youths: we playfully called ourselves “strays”) here, she explained:

“This whole time, in my whole life, no one told me the Anarchists were always there. I wish I’d found you all sooner.” When Tasha learned about the anarchist Mujeres Libres (Free Women) of the Spanish Revolution, she lamented she “would’ve surely joined and stood with them.”

Tasha also understood the privatized Victorian city as a collection of open canvasses that ‘ought to be reclaimed from “fuckers,” painting sanctioned murals and unsanctioned guerrilla artworks around the city. She was also a talented and seamless acquirer and redistributor of various goods to poor folks.

Tasha volunteered with William Head on Stage (WHoS, the only prison theatre company in ‘Canada’) for a number of years. She was blacklisted from volunteering at William Head Institution when the administration decided they did not approve of her friendships with incarcerated artists, as well as conducting The Human Body Project outside the prison, after arbitrary and misogynistic police interventions in street demos. Her shortfilm Handcuffed (2020) documents one of these interactions.

Tasha was an underappreciated …

author: MissyRedaktion
title: Der neue Medienpass
content:
Wir verbünden uns mit GoodImpact, Krautreporter, Übermedien und Surplus und launchen den Medienpass, mit dem du auf alle digitalen Inhalte von allen fünf Publikationen zugreifen. Das haben wir vor:

Gemeinsam mit GoodImpact, Krautreporter, Übermedien und Surplus launchen wir den neuen Medienpass. Dieser erlaubt dir, unbegrenzt auf alle digitalen Inhalte von allen fünf Publikationen zugreifen.

im Probe-Pass: 90 Tage lang als Jahrespass: 365 Tage lang

Und das für nur 15 Euro im Monat!

Fernab großer Verlage gibt es im deutschsprachigen Raum eine vielfältige, unabhängige Medienlandschaft – mit vielen tollen Inhalten.

Das Problem: Bisher bedeutete jedes neue Angebot auch ein weiteres Abo. Mehrere unabhängige Medien zu lesen und zu unterstützen, geht schnell ins Geld. Auf Dauer wird das schlicht zu teuer und zwingt zur Qual der Wahl. Das Ergebnis: Du verpasst spannenden Content bei anderen – und wir viele Leser*innen!

Das ändern wir jetzt: Mit dem Medienpass kannst du für einen günstigen Preis deinen Horizont erweitern und fünf unabhängige Medien supporten. Denn in Zeiten von Desinformation, KI-Slop und aufgeheizten Diskursen braucht es deren kritische Berichterstattung ganz besonders!

Mit dem Medienpass hast du Zugang zu den Themen, Expertisen und Perspektiven von fünf Medien, die sich für kritische Berichterstattung, verlässliche Fakten und eine starke Demokratie engagieren.

Der Medienpass kostet einmalig 180€ für ein Jahr oder 53€ für 90 Tage – das sind nur 15 € im Monat und über 50% preiswerter als die jeweiligen Einzelabos der fünf Medien kombiniert. (Wenn dir das zu viel ist: Wir freuen uns auch sehr, wenn du ein reguläres Missy Online-Abo für 5€/Monat abschließt.)

Uns kennst du ja schon <3 Wir stehen seit 18 Jahren für queeren und intersektionalen Feminismus in Pop, Kultur und Politik. Die Missy erscheint alle zwei Monate in Print und Online. Unser Online-Angebot umfasst zusätzlich mehr als 4000 feministische Texte zu Pop, Kultur und Politik sowie den Pissy Podcast.

Die Plattformen berichten seit 2010 konstruktiv über gute Ideen und Lösungen. Getragen wird ihre Arbeit aktuell von ca. 6.000 Menschen, die uns durch eine Good Membership und freiwillige Beiträge unterstützen.

Das genossenschaftliche Online-Magazin wird von über 15.000 Mitgliedern getragen. Die Redaktion berichtet seit 2014 ohne Drama und tiefgründig über Bildungspolitik, Klima und weitere aktuelle Themen.

Seit zehn Jahren ist das Team die Instanz für Medienkritik. Getragen wird das Online-Magazin von 7.000 Abonnent:innen.

Surplus ist das Wirtschaftsmagazin, das sich um die Interessen der großen Mehrheit und nicht der Reichsten dreht. Täglich veröffentlicht Surplus Texte, wöchentlich Video- und Podcastformate und zweimonatlich ein digitales sowie gedrucktes Magazin.

Bestehende Abos werden angerechnet Wenn du bereits ein Missy Online-Abo hast (oder auch ein Abo bei einer der anderen Medien), wird dir dieses angerechnet. Das System erkennt nämlich deine e-Mail Adresse wieder. Das heißt: Du musst für Abos, die du schon hast, nicht doppelt zahlen!

Der Medienpass ist kein Abo Die Laufzeit vom Medienpass ist ein Jahr. Es gibt keine automatische Verlängerung. Und wenn du dir noch nicht ganz sicher bist: Mit dem Probe-Pass kannst du 90 Tage lang testen, ob dir der Medienpass taugt.

Erstmal nur für jetzt Das Angebot ist zeitlich befristet und endet am 6. Januar 2027

Faire Verteilung Alle Einnahmen werden gerecht zwischen den fünf Medien aufgeteilt. Jedes Medium bleibt absolut eigenständig.

We <3 Community Statt (vermeintlich) gegeneinander zu konkurrieren, bieten wir euch diesen Pass gemeinsam an. Wir wollen miteinander statt gegeneinander gegen den Rechtsruck kämpfen!

Dein Medienpass unterstützt unseren feministischen und unabhängigen Journalismus und hilft dabei, Missy zu erhalten. Danke für deinen Support, wir wissen ihn sehr zu schätzen! <3

Übrigens: Den Medienpass kann man auch als Geschenk-Pass für jemand anderen kaufen. Stichwort Weihnachten. Just saying ;)

author: ANONYM
title: (Munster) Flammen im Herzen der Bestie! Für mehr Sabotage der Bundeswehr!
content:
Wir hatten in der Nacht, vom 06. auf den 07.11.2026 für Abrüstung gesorgt, in dem wir zu einem der größten Bundeswehrstandorte in Deutschland gingen, nach Munster. Wir öffneten den Zaun zur Kaserne „Unteroffizier Friederike – Krüger“ und zündeten auf dem Gelände mehrere Bundeswehrfahrzeuge an.


Just do it again! Für die Freiheit, für das Leben, für die Revolution!


Militarismus, Kapitalismus und Faschismus müssen wir zusammen denken, denn sie stärken sich gegenseitig und profitieren voneinander. Lasst sie uns gemeinsam bekämpfen!


Wir erleben eine Militarisierung in allen Bereichen der Gesellschaft. Seit langem ist dies ein schleichender Prozess, seit kurzem ein offen ausgerufenes Ziel. Wofür Aufrüsten? Unter anderem, um den deutschen Wirtschaftsstandort und seine global relevante Rolle aufrechtzuerhalten. Das kapitalistische System ist mal wieder in der Krise. Statt alternative Wirtschaftssysteme zu etablieren, die weniger Raubbau an Natur und Menschheit verursachen, wird ein autoritärer Staatsumbau legitimiert, der jegliche erkämpfte Errungenschaften wie Arbeitsrechte und Arbeitslosengeld, freie Bildung, den Klimaschutz,etc. über die Klinge springen lässt.


Gleichzeitig fließen massiv viele Ressourcen in den Ausbau eines Überwachungsapparats, der die Bevölkerung mittels KI ausspioniert, soziale und antifaschistische Proteste kriminalisiert, während eine faschistische Partei auf dem Vormarsch ist.


Junge Menschen haben keinen Bock ihr Leben und ihre Karriere aufs Spiel zu setzen, um Deutschland den Arsch zu retten. Sie wollen keinen Staat und kein Wirtschaftssystem, was ihnen eine positive Zukunftsperspektive verwehrt.


Wir grüßen an dieser Stelle die Gen Z- Proteste!


Faschismus ist die Herrschaftsform des Kapitalismus in der Krise.


In dem was „Zeitenwende“ genannt wird, geht es um die Erneuerung des Kapitalismus in einer Phase wirtschaftlichen Niedergangs. Diese Phase soll einmal mehr durch Aufrüstung, Krieg und die militärische Sicherstellung der Zugänge zu Ressourcen, auf die es vermeintlichen Anspruch gibt, überwunden werden.


Um die Militarisierung voranzubringen, wird vor allem Angst und Unsicherheit in den Köpfen verursacht. Bedrohungsszenarien und teils angestaubte Feindbilder sollen die breite Präsenz und Einflussnahme des Militärs in den zivilen Bereich legitimieren. Schulen und Ausbildungsstätten werden als Rekrutierungszentralen benutzt. Medizinisches Personal für Kriegszeiten mit vielen Verwundeten geschult. Soldat*innen in Uniform in der Öffentlichkeit und großflächige Werbung gewöhnen uns an einen militarisierten Alltag.


Militarisierung und Sozialabbau gehen Hand in Hand mit der zunehmend autoritären Formierung des Staates. Diese wird von bürgerlichen Parteien vorangetrieben und die faschistische Partei AfD als Teil der Neuen Rechten kann die Lorbeeren ernten, wenn es um eine Übernahme des ausufernden Überwachungsstaats, restriktive Aufenthaltsgesetze oder den Umgang mit Protest geht. Rechte und faschistische Kräfte nehmen dann ihre klassische, vom System zugedachte Rolle ein: das Aufbegehren von Teilen der Bevölkerung und den Zusammenhalt untereinander anzugreifen und zu zerschlagen.


Moderner Faschismus und Autoritarismus


Der moderne Faschismus in Deutschland greift natürlich auf Kontinuitäten zurück, die an den Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts zurückreichen. Die Neue Rechte besteht aus intellektuellen rechtsradikalen Projekten, nationalkonservativen, neoliberalen Ansätzen, gepaart mit völkischen Schlägertrupps und Parteirechten. Rechtsradikale von heute sind gut vernetzt. Hier werden Beziehungen zu den US-amerikanischen Tech-Oligarchen ebenso gepflegt wie jene zu europäischen rechten Parteien oder Gruppierungen. Einen zunehmenden Autoritarismus können wir global feststellen. Nicht verwunderlich, wenn die vorherrschende Wirtschaftsform der kapitalistischen und neoliberalen Ordnung folgt.


Autoritäre Einstellungsmuster, die u.a. auf rassistischer sowie sexistischer Diskriminierung und reaktionären Geschlechterrollen aufbauen, entstehen aus der kapitalistischen Ordnung selbst, werden aber durch Militarisierung sowie dezidiert rechte Propaganda und Gesetzgebungen verschärft. Diese Muster sind in der Gesellschaft bereits angelegte Ideologien und „Lösungsstrategien“ für die Krisen des Kapitalismus. title: Karaköy'den Eminönü'ne kadın zinciri: “Erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulsun”
content:
İstanbul – Karaköy’de iskele önünde zincir oluşturan kadınlar Eminönü’ne yürüyüş gerçekleştirdi. Eminönü’nde iskeleye gelen kadınlar burada, ölümü aydınlatılmamış kadınların hikayelerinden aktarımlarda bulunduktan sonra basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. Açıklamada, “Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

25 Kasım Kadın Platformu öncülüğünde Karaköy'de zincir oluşturuldu, Eminönü'ne bir yürüyüş düzenlendi. Eylemde, 2026-2035 yıllarının iktidar tarafından ‘Aile ve Nüfus On Yılı’ ilan edilmesinin ardından 2026'nın ilk 10 ayında 245 kadının erkekler tarafından katledildiği ve 274 kadının şüpheli şekilde yaşamanı yitirdiğine dikkat çekildi, iktidarın mevcut politikalarına tepki gösterildi.

Eminönü'nde yapılan açıklamada “Kadın cinayetlerinin karşısında yalnızca yas tutmayacağız. Kadınların yaşam hakkını tehdit eden bütün mekanizmaları teşhir edeceğiz. Koruma kararlarının kağıt üzerinde kalmasına, şiddet başvurularının görmezden gelinmesine, faillerin iyi hal ve haksız tahrik indirimleriyle ödüllendirilmesine, şüpheli kadın ölümlerinin karanlıkta bırakılmasına izin vermeyeceğiz. Bir kadının daha öldürülmemesi için erkek şiddetini besleyen cezasızlık düzeni son bulmalı; İstanbul Sözleşmesi yeniden yürürlüğe girmeli, 6284 sayılı Kanun etkin biçimde uygulanmalıdır. Kadınların ekonomik ve toplumsal bağımsızlığını sağlayacak politikalar hayata geçirilmelidir” denildi.

Eylemde son yıllarda hayatını kaybeden kadınlara yönelik bazı saldırılar hakkında da şu bilgiler verildi:

“Fatmanur Çelik, 30 yaşında genç bir kadındı. Kuran'a Hizmet Vakfı'nda sohbetlere katıldığı sırada vakıf çalışanı Ayhan Şengüler tarafından tecavüze uğradı. Ailesi tarafından Ayhan Şengüler ile evlenmeye zorlandı ve evliliği boyunca cinsel şiddete maruz kaldı. Ayhan Şengüler'in kızı Hifa İkra'yı istismar ettiği için yargılandığı davada savcının beraat istemesinin ardından 13 Ocak'ta Anadolu Adliyesi önünde adalet nöbetine başladı. Fatmanur Çelik ve kızı Hifa İkra'nın cansız bedenleri 3 Mart'ta Zeytinburnu Sahili'nde bulundu.

Arya 19 yaşında, TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi İngiliz Dili Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisiydi. 13 Nisan 2026’da kaldığı üniversite yurdunda intihara sürüklendi. Ailesi Arya’ya trans kadın olduğu için şiddet uyguladı, onu onarım terapisine götürdüler. Arya kaldığı yurtta hem yurt yönetimi hem öğrenciler tarafından baskı, dışlanma ve tehditlere maruz kaldı. Arya’nın ölümüne intihar deniyor ama Arya’yı intihara sürükleyen koşulların üstünün örtüldüğünü biliyoruz.

İlayda Zorlu 19 yaşında, Karadeniz Teknik Üniversitesi’nde Uluslararası İlişkiler bölümü öğrencisiydi. Polis, İlayda Zorlu'nun ailesini arayarak 'Kızınız 8 Mart eylemlerine katılıyor, çocuğunuz örgüte katılmış' dedi. Ailesinin baskısına maruz kalan, evde alıkonulduğunu, okutulmayacağını ve evden kaçmak istediğini arkadaşlarına anlatan İlayda, 17 Nisan 2026'da Hatay'ın Kırıkhan ilçesindeki aile evinde, polis olan babasının silahından çıkan kurşunla hayatını kaybetti.

Ayşe Tokyaz, 22 yaşında bir üniversite öğrencisiydi. 2025 yılının temmuz ayında, ihraç polis Cemil Koç tarafından Küçükçekmece’de öldürüldü. Cansız bedeni bir valize konularak katil Cemil Koç’la suç ortaklığı yapan erkekler tarafından yol kenarına bırakıldı. Ayşe’nin ikizi Esra, kardeşini kurtarmak için tek başına mücadele etti. Ayşe yalnızca Cemil Koç tarafından değil, katilin işlerini yapan, cinayetten sonra evi temizleten, Esra’yı oyalayan, sosyal medyadan taciz eden, ifadesini katile sızdıran ve cinayetten sonra çevirmelere takılmaması için katile eşlik eden polis memurunun da aralarında olduğu erkekler tarafından el birliğiyle katledildi.

as someone who has severe sensory issues re: my own hair but who also KNOWS THINGS ABOUT MISOGYNY, I always want to respond to “I shave/wax for sensory reasons” with “me too, but I was encouraged to do that with the hair on my legs, whereas when I removed the hair on my eyelids, eyebrows, and scalp, it got me institutionalized. can you think of any reasons why that might be, bc I have a hypothesis”

people do not like when you say things such as this. i think its a conversation which needs to be had, though!!! like what hair is it considered appropriate and desirable for women to remove? what hair is it considered inappropriate and pathological for women to remove? WE HAVE SOME VERY OBVIOUSLY ANSWERS HERE we just choose not to look at them

“I do it for sensory reasons” is, CHARITABLY, not the end of a conversation. i say charitably because it often is not even fucking relevant. but assuming that it is, ok. and how did those around you react when you began doing this. were you encouraged or discouraged? what would the reaction be if you stopped? what if you removed hair from other areas? what if a man removed his hair for sensory reasons? what would the reaction be? what social pressures might he need to overcome in order to take that action that don’t exist for those of us for whom this is expected?

LET’S GO ON A THOUGHT JOURNEY TOGETHER.

less generously and more straightforwardly because I think many people are missing my point here

“I do it for sensory reasons” is almost never fucking relevant to an existing conversation about the expected removal of body hair in women and is 100% never a relevant response to an existing conversation about SOCIETAL MISOGYNY.

and I would like for those who deploy it as such to do some serious reflecting on why they think it is a reasonable counterpoint in said discussions, rather than a segue into another related discussion about what behaviors are rewarded and encouraged in what people and whether those same behaviors are discouraged and punished in other people. and what someone’s experiences seeing reflected in the world around them might prime them to see certain things as normal (and therefore no big deal to engage in) and others as abnormal (and therefore something that would require an unusually strong individual motivation to engage in)

author: S. Baum
title: Ohio Bill Threatens to Criminalize Drag and Gender Nonconformity, Opponents Warn
content:
Civil liberties and trans rights advocates say the bill has nothing to do with the purported aim of protecting children.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Ohio appears to be on the cusp of passing a drag ban. Transgender Ohioans and their allies are sounding the alarm.

“House Bill 249 seeks to limit drag performances to strip clubs and similar locations, making it a crime to perform in drag in other places where a minor may be present,” an ACLU of Ohio petition to stop the bill reads.

“This bill broadly targets anyone who performs exhibiting a gender identity different than the entertainer’s biological sex at birth. HB 249 also relies on notoriously vague legal standards used to determine whether content is considered obscene and/or ‘harmful to juveniles.’”

Dara Adkison, the executive director of TransOhio, told Erin in the Morning that if this bill becomes law, it would be “the most extreme criminalization of drag and perceived gender nonconformity in the country.”

In addition to traditional drag, HB 249 also specifically targets transgender and gender nonconforming performers. Those found to violate all or part of these measures could be tried for a misdemeanor or felony, which could carry jail time.

Although in theory, the bill applies only to “performances,” not everyday Ohioans, its ambiguity blurs the line between lawful and unlawful; the bill fails to even articulate what constitutes a “performance.”

“If I’m doing my grocery shopping down at Kroger, and I whistle to myself as I’m going down the aisle or hum to the music overhead, has that suddenly become a drag performance in the middle of the Kroger shopping center?” Arienne Childrey, a transgender woman and community activist, asked while being interviewed by Erin in the Morning. She said the bill isn’t about drag performance or protecting children as much as it is about criminalizing gender nonconformity.

Childrey has been following the progression of Ohio’s drag ban for a long while—since 2023, to be exact, when HB 249’s predecessor bill, HB 245, was proposed. That bill was sponsored by Rep. Angie King, Childrey’s own representative in the statehouse. When Childrey and others staged a protest, King responded by mocking demonstrators, arguing they were fighting for the “right to twerk and gyrate in front of your minor children.”

An Ohio drag ban was reintroduced in April of last year. It passed in the House in March 2026 and then stalled for months in the Senate. On Nov. 17, analysts at TransOhio noticed it was put on the legislative calendar for a hearing sometime during the week beginning on Monday, Nov. 23. An exact date and time has not yet been announced.

“What we have right now is vengeance politics playing out in Ohio,” Childrey said, referring to the aftermath of this midterm cycle’s blue wave.

“Their veto-proof supermajority evaporates after the new year,” she continued. “Come January, that disappears. So they know that they are ‘do or die’ this time around; otherwise, they have a two-year legislative cycle where they won’t be able to move something like this through if they were to try.”

The state’s Senate Judiciary Committee must now vote on whether to pass the “sub bill,” or substitution bill, which is an amended version of the text. It will then need to be heard before the full Senate and be reconciled with the House if there are further changes.

However, it is still dripping with the same anti-trans animus and ill intent as before, even if its GOP proponents try to brand it as some sort of middle-of-the-road compromise, activists warned.

For example, the sub bill removed the definitions of “biological sex” that it previously codified, but those were enshrined by HB 96 anyway; the newer version also added a section making it a felony if “the offender previously has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to two or more violations of this section.”

“The vagueness is actually more dangerous now,” Adkison, of TransOhio, told Erin in the Morning. “The sub bill INCREASES the criminal penalties for an offense that previously didn’t exist. Under this bill, gender nonconformity (even among cis people) will be scrutinized, and those who don’t look ‘male’ or ‘female’ enough will face potential prison time.”

“This is so clearly a violation of the First Amendment freedom of expression,” Adkison added.

author: TGEU
title: Joint Statement: Why Portugal’s Self-Determination Act Must Stay
content:
TGEU, IGLYO, OII Europe and ILGA-Europe have submitted joint comments to the Portuguese Parliament on two Bills that would repeal Law 38/2018, the Self-Determination Act, and reinstate the medicalised regime of Law 7/2011: Bill 391/XVII/1, tabled by Chega, and Bill 486/XVII/1, tabled by the PSD. Both parties sit in the ruling government, so together they command the majority needed to pass these Bills into law. We ask Parliament to withdraw both Bills or vote against them in their entirety.


There is no problem to solve.

 The Self-Determination Act works. Between 2018 and 2022, 1,595 people changed their gender marker, more than triple the previous period, and the competent authority, the CIG, reported in 2022 and again in 2026 that it knows of no refusals, no fraud and no misuse. Twelve European countries have self-determination models, some for over a decade; none has repealed them. Where rare problems arose, courts solved them. Legal initiatives that strip people of acquired rights need a demonstrated need, and none exists.


What these Bills would do


Bring back pathologisation and clinical gatekeeping.

 Trans adults would once again have to prove their identity to two multidisciplinary medical teams, undergo years of psychological monitoring and, as drafted, in practice show proof of surgery before the State recognises who they are. The European Court of Human Rights has ruled that no one should have to accept surgery or sterilising treatment to be recognised, and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe has called for procedures based on self-determination. Worse still, Portugal already struggles with a shortage of professionals in trans-specific healthcare: a procedure requiring two teams, years of monitoring and a surgical pathway would make legal gender recognition effectively inaccessible in practice, squandering scarce medical resources on certifying instead of treating or meeting actual health needs. These Bills would put doctors, not trans people, in charge of trans people’s identities.


Exclude 16 and 17 year olds from legal gender recognition

, despite the existing safeguards (legal representatives, a personal hearing and a capacity report) and no recorded refusals, fraud or abuse. The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child requires capacity-based assessment, not fixed age limits. The reality for those affected: every exam, train ride, job application or school registration becomes a forced outing, in a country where nearly three in four LGBTQI students report bullying or insults at school.


Weaken protection of intersex children.

 Portugal made history in 2018 as the second European country to ban non-consensual medical interventions on intersex children. Bill 391 repeals that ban without an adequate replacement; Bill 486’s weakly defined “health exception” could still permit medically unnecessary “normalising” surgeries. Both Bills regress on Recommendation CM/Rec(2025)7, which Portugal helped adopt only very recently in October 2025.


Roll back healthcare and education rights.

 Bill 391 would ban all gender-affirming care for under-18s by statute, overriding the judgment of doctors, parents and the young people themselves, and restrict teaching on gender diversity in schools, an approach the EU Court of Justice has already rejected in its judgment against Hungary. Bill 486 removes the protected ground of gender expression, restricts sports participation by “biological sex”, risks excluding trans and intersex children from youth and school sport, and deletes the right to a social name, which migrants, minors and non-binary people rely on to live as themselves in schools, workplaces and public services.


Rely on outdated, pathologising and stigmatising terminology

 (“gender identity disorder”, “transsexuality”, “hermaphrodites”) that contradicts ICD-11, which Portugal supported, and the human-rights based language that all 46 Council of Europe member States have adopted with CM/Rec(2025)7. Words matter: law that frames people as disorders invites treating them as such.


Not in line with international human rights law


Restricting fundamental rights requires a pressing social need under Article 8(2) ECHR and the Portuguese Constitution. These Bills offer conceptual or hypothetical worries, thinly sourced on Portuguese practice, not demonstrated problems. Rolling back rights people already hold requires full justification and consideration of all alternatives; these Bills …

author: anred
title: 19N: un grito colectivo contra la violencia sexual hacia las niñeces y adolescencias
content:
En el marco del Día Internacional contra las Violencias Sexuales hacia Niñeces y Adolescencias, organizaciones feministas, transfeministas, sobrevivientes y madres protectoras se movilizarán este jueves 19 de noviembre frente al Congreso de la Nación. Bajo la consigna «Yo sí te creo», denunciarán la impunidad judicial, las revinculaciones forzadas con agresores y el desmantelamiento de las políticas públicas de protección. La jornada combinará denuncia, memoria, organización colectiva y un festival para recuperar el espacio público desde el encuentro y la celebración

. Por ANRed


Este 19 de noviembre, el Congreso de la Nación será escenario de una nueva edición del

Grito Global contra las Violencias Sexuales hacia Niñeces y Adolescencias.

 La convocatoria, impulsada por el Colectivo Yo Sí Te Creo junto a organizaciones sociales, feministas y transfeministas, reunirá a sobrevivientes, madres y familiares protectores, profesionales de la salud, docentes y activistas que desde hace años se organizan para denunciar una de las formas más silenciadas de violencia.


La jornada se inscribe en una trayectoria de trece años de lucha y visibilización, que desde 2020 se articula en distintos territorios del país bajo la iniciativa del Grito Global. Su objetivo es romper el silencio, denunciar las responsabilidades institucionales y construir redes colectivas de acompañamiento y protección.


Según los datos citados por las organizaciones convocantes,

una de cada cinco niñas y uno de cada siete niños atraviesan situaciones de violencia sexual

. En Argentina, señalan que cerca del 80 % de estos hechos ocurren en el ámbito intrafamiliar o en entornos de confianza. Estas cifras, advierten, no alcanzan a reflejar la verdadera magnitud del problema, debido a la enorme cantidad de situaciones que nunca llegan a denunciarse.


La violencia sexual contra las infancias no constituye un problema exclusivamente privado o familiar. Las organizaciones denuncian que se encuentra atravesada por relaciones desiguales de poder, condiciones económicas, estructuras patriarcales y prácticas institucionales que muchas veces terminan garantizando la impunidad de los agresores.


Una justicia que revictimiza y desprotege


Uno de los principales ejes de la convocatoria será la denuncia del funcionamiento del Poder Judicial frente a las situaciones de abuso sexual infantil.


El documento cuestiona la utilización del denominado Síndrome de Alienación Parental (SAP) y de argumentos derivados, como las supuestas falsas memorias o los relatos inducidos, para desacreditar las denuncias de niños, niñas, adolescentes y sus entornos protectores.


Las organizaciones advierten que estas prácticas pueden convertirse en herramientas de revictimización y derivar en decisiones judiciales que obligan a las infancias a mantener contacto con personas denunciadas por abuso sexual.


En ese sentido, rechazan las revinculaciones forzadas y exigen el apartamiento de funcionarios judiciales responsables de vulnerar los derechos de las niñeces. También reclaman el regreso de las niñas Arociris, de La Rioja, y Cielo, de Chaco, a sus respectivos entornos protectores.


La criminalización de las madres que denuncian constituye otro de los puntos centrales. Bajo la consigna «No somos obstructoras, somos protectoras», las organizaciones denuncian la persecución judicial de mujeres que intentan proteger a sus hijos e hijas y reclaman la libertad de Flavia Saganías.


A estas situaciones se suman las dificultades materiales para acceder a la justicia: falta de patrocinio jurídico gratuito, investigaciones que se prolongan durante años, ausencia de acompañamiento especializado y desigualdades económicas que condicionan las posibilidades de sostener una denuncia.


Las organizaciones reclaman presupuesto, equipos interdisciplinarios, atención psicológica especializada, acompañamiento a sobrevivientes y condiciones laborales dignas para quienes trabajan en los dispositivos de protección.


En particular, reivindican la implementación efectiva de la Ley Nacional de Educación Sexual Integral, con formación docente y contenidos científicos en todos los niveles educativos, como una herramienta fundamental para que las infancias puedan reconocer situaciones de violencia, identificar sus derechos y acceder a redes de cuidado.


Asimismo, defienden el acceso a la interrupción legal y voluntaria del embarazo y recuperan la consigna «Son niñas, no madres», frente a las maternidades …

title: Businessmen, not battlers, lead the charge for One Nation in NSW
content:
Pauline Hanson’s One Nation pretends to be a party of battlers, standing up for the little guy against the major parties. This narrative has been parroted by the mainstream media and even taken up by Hanson’s opponents. The party’s lead candidates for the March 2027 New South Wales state election paint a very different picture of who the party represents.

Take Mike Newman, newly-appointed NSW leader and candidate for Cessnock, the Hunter Valley seat One Nation considers winnable. Newman’s riches-to-riches story involves growing up in well-heeled Mosman on Sydney’s lower North Shore and attending the elite private school Cranbrook, along with billionaire James Packer. His father, Maurice Newman, was the chair of the Australian Securities Exchange and then of the ABC. 

Son followed father into the world of investment banking. After a long career as a banker in Tokyo, Newman landed a gig in the public service as NSW Senior Trade and Investment Commissioner in Japan. The wasteful inefficiency of the bureaucracy supposedly radicalised Newman and convinced him to go into politics. Curiously, during his three-year stint as commissioner, Newman racked up hundreds of thousands of dollars in expenses (funded by the taxpayer) for flights, five-star hotels and restaurant and bar bills, as was recently revealed by the

Sydney Morning Herald

. This spending included more than $20,000 for an extended stay in a Meriton Suite in Sydney.

Next up is Jeff Bacon, who will be second on One Nation’s ticket for the upper house. Bacon is the managing director of Oceana Precision, a weapons manufacturer based in Tamworth, his north-eastern NSW hometown. He ran as the lower house candidate for Tamworth with the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers party in 2019, then joined the Nationals in 2023 before defecting to One Nation in October 2025. 

In an interview with Tamworth’s local newspaper, the 

Northern Daily Leader,

 in January, Bacon alleged that every single one of Oceania Precision’s rifles was banned in NSW following firearms legislation passed by the state Labor government in the wake of the Bondi Massacre. Bacon would, apparently, be broke in six months if the laws weren’t repealed. Hanson has described him as her “go-to man on the firearms industry”.

Sure, you might struggle to pay grocery or electricity bills, or cover your mortgage or rent. But spare a thought for the owner of a medium-sized weapons manufacturer whose human rights have been trampled on by the Labor government. 

Stuart Bonds, the party’s lead upper house candidate, is more regularly held up as emblematic of the party’s battler credentials.

Bonds, a former Hunter Valley coal miner, won 21 percent of the vote for One Nation in the 2019 federal election. Bonds is critical of both renewable energy and the behaviour of multinational mining companies. He left One Nation in 2021 over its support for the Morrison government's industrial relations legislation that undermined casual workers’ rights.

Bonds, however, is more representative of your average bigot than battler. At an anti-immigration rally in early November, he espoused the far-right Great Replacement conspiracy theory. He told the protesters that, “we are being demographically replaced inside our own nation”, and warned them that this was part of a “socialist plan” to “tear down the fabric of your civilisation”. 

Bonds is also a bigot on other social issues. Many have rightly pointed out the irony of his misogynistic comments when he boasted: “I don’t have a woman boss, and I don’t have a gay boss, and there’s a reason for that”. The only problem for Mr Bonds is that he does indeed have both a woman boss in Hanson and a gay boss in James Ashby, the party director. Irony aside, the comments indicate the rank misogyny and homophobia that aren’t simply personal opinions, but party policy. One Nation boasts about being “pro-life” and is currently campaigning to restrict abortion rights in NSW. 

One Nation’s NSW state election candidates give you a glimpse into the actual character of the party. Rather than being the authentic expression of working-class grievances, the party is a Frankenstein-like combination of bankers, bigots and small business owners. What unites them is not their genuine struggles under the system, but their hostility to the gains made by oppressed groups and minorities, hatred of the left and commitment to a pro-business economic agenda.

author: Bizzi Lavelle
title: Young Women, Pain, Mobility Aids
content:
Stories Contributors Pitch an Idea

To be sick, or have a health condition of any kind is not a moral failing. I know this and I hope that you do too. However, every time I find myself staying in or leaving something early because I’m in pain or I’m fatigued, I can’t help but feel the people around me are disappointed.

People wish they had a friend who could come to their fortnightly event like they said they would. They wish they could book a performer to MC an event without them withdrawing due to spending that week pain ridden in bed. They wish the friend they extended a birthday party invite made it instead of sending through an apologetic message. They wish their friend would be in the room cheering them on at their weekly drag comp or production show.

A common online talking point echoes in my head as I send my latest “I’m sorry” message; you have to inconvenience yourself a little for the sake of your community. You have to be someone’s villager if you want to have a village.

With the weeks or days I spend hidden away, inside, barely leaving the house I often ask myself, do I deserve to be in anyone’s village? Do I deserve my own villagers?

The words to Rina Sawayama’s ‘Bad Friend’ circle my mind as I spend another Saturday night in my pajamas, watching anime in bed: “So don’t ask me where I’ve been, been avoiding everything.”

As I’m lamenting my woes to my notes app and the friends who get it, an article from The Times UK comes across my feed. “Why are young women using walking sticks?” by Katherine Stock. And then another, this time from The Telegraph, “How having a disability became cool” by Poppy Coburn.

The themes of these pieces are misogyny and ableism, with sprinkles of transphobia and ageism.

In both of these pieces, the authors seem to believe that young women in increasing numbers are faking to be disabled for social clout. In the first piece, Stock declares young women using mobility aids and posting about being ill are victims of “social contagion” deems the pain they’re in as “unclear” and therefore “unclear” if these women “really have” disabilities.

It’s wild to me, that in 2026, anyone would partake in such ableist vitriol. Despite what both authors think, there are a wide range of ways to be disabled. Disability and chronic illness don’t always look like a wheelchair user. Sometimes disabilities and chronic illnesses are invisible. Sometimes they’re dynamic. The only criteria to being disabled is having a condition, injury or alike that impedes you and your ability to do day to day tasks.

Disability is the only minority group a person can become part of at a moment’s notice, and is the only minority group we will all be part of at some point in our lives. As my friend, Protect our NDIS rally organiser and activist Oriela says “You will become disabled. That’s a promise not just a threat”.

That one influencer you follow could one day be surfing and the next using a wheelchair or cane. You aren’t able to discern how much pain someone is in by simply looking at them. If that were the case, women wouldn’t be waiting years for their pain to be believed and diagnosed.

For Aboriginal women, seeking medical care has an extra layer of stress. Racial bias in medicine historically saw beliefs that bla(c)k people, particularly women, have a higher pain tolerance than their white counterparts. This, along with classic medical misogyny has led to Aboriginal women being mistreated, ignored or treated as though they’re only ‘drug seeking’.

In Allanah Hunt’s 2024 piece ‘The Good Patient’, she details her experiences of medical racism as she navigates dealing with endometriosis. Despite Allanah’s attempts to present to hospitals as the best and most polite patient, her pain was still disbelieved and she was still treated as a drug seeker. “Because the truth is, no matter how much I’m ‘the good patient’, I will never escape the racial judgement from healthcare providers” Allanah writes.

Similarly, Colleen Lavelle (my mother) discusses her experience of medical racism in her 2017 piece. “Death by racism: bigotry in the health system is harming Indigenous patients’”.

She notes from her own experiences and other First Nations people whose medical experiences she’s listened to that a common thread is wondering if you’ve been overly sensitive.

One memory I have from my teens is when I was at the shops with my mum and younger sister. I went out to the car to put some bags in the car and a man …

author: Agência Diadorim
title: Partido de Trump apostou milhões em propagandas anti trans nas eleições nos EUA — e perdeu
content:
O Partido Republicano dos Estados Unidos apostou — e muito — em campanhas contra os direitos das pessoas trans para tentar conquistar votos nas eleições de meio de mandato no país.

Até 25 de outubro, o partido do presidente Donald Trump havia investido 183 milhões de dólares em anúncios de televisão sobre questões trans, segundo levantamento da AdImpact divulgado pela Associated Press.

 Foram cerca de 217 mil veiculações em todo o país.


O investimento contrasta com as prioridades dos eleitores.

Segundo pesquisa AP-NORC, apenas um em cada dez eleitores registrados considera as questões trans prioritárias. Já oito em cada dez apontam a economia ou o custo de vida como assuntos importantes.


A baixa prioridade atribuída ao tema, porém, não significa que ele seja irrelevante na escolha dos candidatos. Pesquisa do The 19th/YouGov, realizada em setembro com 2.357 adultos, mostra que 45% dos entrevistados afirmam ter maior probabilidade de votar em um candidato favorável à proibição da participação de atletas trans em equipes esportivas femininas.


Por outro lado, na mesma pesquisa, 42% consideram que os políticos não deveriam se concentrar em questões relacionadas às pessoas trans. As opiniões também variam conforme o direito em discussão: 45% são contrários à proibição ou restrição de cuidados de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade, enquanto 38% apoiam essas medidas. Outros 51% acreditam que pessoas trans enfrentam muita discriminação nos Estados Unidos.


A estratégia republicana, utilizada por Donald Trump em 2024, também foi desenhada para pressionar os democratas.

 Segundo a Reuters, enquanto alguns candidatos tentam deslocar o debate para a economia, outros adotam posições mais conservadoras.


Como a

Agência Pública

 mostrou, a tática parece não ter funcionado. Em

entrevista

, a socióloga e cientista política Gisele Agnelli apontou que a promessa central que elegeu Donald Trump em 2024 — a

affordability

, ou recuperação do poder de compra — “não se materializou na percepção de grande parte dos eleitores. Os democratas exploraram essa frustração com uma campanha essencialmente pragmática, concentrada no custo da alimentação, da moradia, dos combustíveis e dos serviços de saúde”, avalia.


Partido republicano utilizou propaganda anti trans para tentar pressionar democratas e conseguir votos nas eleições dos EUA


Da campanha eleitoral às propostas de lei anti trans nos EUA


A mobilização em torno dos direitos trans não se limita à publicidade eleitoral.

No Congresso norte-americano, propostas buscam restringir a participação de meninas e mulheres trans em competições esportivas femininas, o uso de banheiros conforme a identidade de gênero e conteúdos escolares relacionados à transgeneridade.


Uma dessas propostas, o H.R. 28, foi aprovada pela Câmara dos Representantes em janeiro de 2025, mas não se tornou lei. Outras seguem em diferentes etapas de tramitação.


Esporte, educação e acesso a espaços públicos também estão entre os temas de projetos apresentados por parlamentares brasileiros, especialmente ligados ao campo conservador.


A ofensiva anti trans no Brasil


O Partido Liberal (PL), legenda da família Bolsonaro, é apontado pela

Observatória

 como o partido que mais apresenta projetos de lei anti-LGBTQIA+ no Brasil.


Nas eleições deste ano, a sigla elegeu 121 deputados federais e se consolidou como a maior bancada da Câmara. Entre os eleitos estão Nikolas Ferreira (MG) e Lucas Pavanato (SP), ambos com mais de 3 milhões de votos e conhecidos por seus recorrentes discursos transfóbicos.


Entre janeiro de 2019 e maio de 2026, a Observatória identificou, nas Assembleias Legislativas, 81 projetos de censura escolar, incluindo propostas contra a chamada “ideologia de gênero”.


Outros 70 projetos tratam do uso de banheiros, com restrições ao acesso conforme a identidade de gênero. Há ainda 40 propostas que buscam limitar a participação de atletas trans em competições esportivas.


Na área da saúde, foram identificados 39 projetos relacionados ao processo transexualizador, com restrições ao atendimento de menores de idade. Outros 17 tratam da definição de gênero nas políticas públicas.


Na Câmara dos Deputados, foram apresentados outros 20 projetos sobre atletas trans, 19 relacionados ao processo transexualizador, 18 sobre censura escolar, 13 sobre definição de gênero e 12 sobre banheiros.


Ofensiva antitrans
