title: Estados Unidos: Apostillas electorales
content:
Zohran Mamdani, alcalde de Nueva York, Estados Unidos


Por Mario Hernandez


El alcalde Mamdani disfrutó del triunfo de los cuatro candidatos a los que les dio su apoyo para el Congreso


Entre ellos estaban las integrantes del DSA (Socialistas Democráticos de América) Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier, el ex contralor Brad Lander y la gobernadora Kathy Hochul.


La victoria más contundente de la noche fue la de Chevalier, que se quedó con su distrito en el norte de Manhattan y el Bronx con el 87,5 % de los votos. Su rival, el republicano Jomo Williams, apenas arañó un 12 %. Semejante paliza electoral deja bien en claro que las propuestas de Chevalier, que incluyen impuestos a los ricos, salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE, entre otras demandas progresistas, calan profundo en gran parte de sus nuevos votantes. Su triunfo demuestra además que se puede hacer campaña definiéndose abiertamente como socialista, e incluso enfrentar a la policía en las calles, sin miedo a “espantar a los propios”. De hecho, el tono combativo de Darializa y su ya famoso cruce con la policía el día del tiroteo del ICE en el Bronx sin duda le sumaron un buen caudal de votos.


Chevalier cruzó duro al ICE y remarcó la importancia de la vivienda accesible, vistiendo una kufiyya como símbolo de apoyo a Palestina. De todos modos, sorprendió que su discurso hablara muy poco de política internacional: la única mención a Palestina se dio cuando la tribuna empezó a cantar de forma espontánea “Palestina libre”.


Además de Chevalier, el DSA conquistó una segunda banca por el Distrito 7, donde Valdez, que también contaba con el respaldo de Mamdani, logró un triunfo cómodo con más del 83 % de los votos frente a su rival republicano. Valdez, referente del DSA, va a reemplazar a la congresista del establishment demócrata Nydia Velázquez, que se retira en enero. Al igual que Chevalier, Valdez hizo campaña con propuestas de salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE. Un dato clave: a diferencia de Mamdani, ni Valdez ni Chevalier le dieron su apoyo a la gobernadora Hochul ni dijeron que la iban a votar.


Con esto, el DSA pasa a tener tres bancas en el Congreso por Nueva York: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier. Si a eso se le suma el flamante congresista y ex miembro del DSA Brad Lander, a quien Mamdani también apoyó, el alcalde pasa a contar con una bancada importante que representa sus intereses y muchas de sus ideas en el Congreso.


Pero el festejo de Chevalier no fue la única parada de Mamdani esa noche. Antes de subir hacia el Bronx, apenas cerraron las urnas, el alcalde pasó la primera parte de la noche con la gobernadora Kathy Hochul y sus seguidores. En el discurso que dio ahí, Mamdani definió la elección como un “punto de quiebre” para el Partido Demócrata y afirmó que “empezamos el trabajo de transformar a nuestro partido para que vuelva a ser de los trabajadores”.


Su respaldo fue determinante para darle un vuelco a la campaña de Hochul. Hace menos de dos años, parecía que su carrera se había terminado. Todavía golpeada por la ajustada elección de 2022, donde los demócratas de Nueva York perdieron cinco bancas en el Congreso en parte por su incapacidad para movilizar al electorado propio, sus chances de ganar la interna y la reelección parecían bajísimas. Su imagen positiva rozaba apenas el 40 % (al nivel o por debajo de la del presidente Trump), y las encuestas mostraban que un mano a mano en 2026 contra un candidato republicano fuerte podía ser muy parejo.


Pero entonces entró en escena el alcalde Zohran Mamdani. Su meteórico ascenso al poder fue una ola que, al igual que la “ola azul” demócrata, empujó a cuanto candidato llevara la “D” de demócrata en la boleta, y su apoyo temprano y explícito a Hochul le devolvió el aire a la campaña de la gobernadora. Los resultados del martes demostraron la fuerza que tuvo ese espaldarazo. Hochul no solo logró la reelección, sino que aplastó por completo a su rival republicano Bruce Blakeman por más de 20 puntos.


Gran parte de este triunfo se explica por los mismos factores que impulsaron las victorias demócratas en el resto del país: el rechazo a Trump y al Partido Republicano, la bronca con las atrocidades del ICE y la guerra contra Irán, y la frustración por la inflación y el costo de vida. En realidad, el éxito de los demócratas a nivel nacional tuvo más que ver con el odio a Trump que con las propuestas reales de …

author: Arnold Padilla
title: What’s at stake in Trump’s Manila visit?
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump’s upcoming visit to Manila for the ASEAN Summit happens in the wake of intensifying struggle between the U.S. and China for economic, technological, political, and military dominance in Asia. Washington aims to consolidate its strategic position in Southeast Asia, with the Philippines under Ferdinand Marcos Jr. playing an increasingly important role in advancing U.S. imperialist interests.

Trump arrives politically battered. The sweeping Republican defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, which handed both houses of Congress to the Democrats, represents a powerful repudiation of his administration’s policies. Trump’s unpopular U.S. war against Iran and his aggressive tariff policies and their disastrous economic consequences, such as rising living costs, contributed to widespread dissatisfaction among American voters.

The defeat further exposes the political crisis confronting U.S. imperialism. It reflects growing domestic opposition to policies that impose enormous economic and social costs on the American people while sustaining Washington’s aggressive military interventions and global ambitions.

But Trump’s weakened domestic position does not mean that the White House will abandon its imperialist agenda abroad. On the contrary, the administration may seek to demonstrate U.S. power through new military, economic, and diplomatic agreements. Trump could use his visit to Manila to project strength and secure strategic commitments to counter the political setback at home.

The central objective of Washington’s ASEAN agenda is to preserve U.S. supremacy in the face of China’s expanding economic and military power. Southeast Asia occupies a crucial place in this rivalry. It sits astride strategic maritime routes and contains vital manufacturing centers, mineral resources, emerging digital markets, and production networks essential to the world economy.

For U.S. imperialism, maintaining influence over ASEAN means safeguarding its military reach while securing access to markets, technology infrastructure, critical minerals, and industrial supply chains. The U.S. seeks to organize these strategic assets around its own economic and national-security priorities, particularly by reducing dependence on Chinese-controlled production networks.

At the same time, China is expanding its own economic and strategic influence through trade, investment, infrastructure, and military power. This competition between rival great powers seeks to expand their influence over the region’s resources, markets, territory, and political decisions.

Washington’s military agenda was made explicit during the ASEAN defense ministers’ meetings in Cebu in October, when Pete Hegseth, Trump’s so-called Secretary of War, proposed a new framework for U.S.–ASEAN defense cooperation.

Under the language of maritime security and interoperability, Washington seeks to deepen military coordination, intelligence sharing, joint exercises, and naval cooperation with Southeast Asian governments. The proposal complements the expanding network of U.S. military alliances and access arrangements across the Indo-Pacific. It aims to strengthen its First Island Chain strategy to encircle and contain China. On the sidelines of the Cebu meeting, U.S. and Japanese defense officials discussed implementing a more effective denial-defense posture along this chain.

With its geographical location, the Philippines has become a crucial platform for this strategy. Under Marcos Jr., U.S. military access under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) has expanded from five to nine designated Philippine facilities. Washington and Manila are also increasing joint military exercises and deployments of advanced missile and unmanned systems. These arrangements strengthen the capacity of U.S. forces to operate in the South China Sea and potentially respond to a Taiwan Strait conflict.

So far, only two ASEAN countries have formal defense treaties with the U.S., namely the Philippines and Thailand. But all the other members, except for Myanmar, have various forms of extensive defense or military cooperation arrangements with the U.S. However, unlike its Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) and related pacts with the Philippines, not all agreements with other ASEAN countries grant U.S. troops access to military installations, allow combat deployments, or entail an obligation to support U.S. military operations.

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:


It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!


What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.


This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.


Glorification


A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo


Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:


…,

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo


being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…


With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.


The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.


B: In Praise of Theatre Artists:


Zachary J Patterson

title: Trump bombardea Irán en la madrugada de su derrota electoral
content:
Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. A

 nadie escapa que en el telón de fondo del rechazo electoral a Trump se encuentra la guerra contra Irán y sus consecuencias económicas. Pero al referirse al resultado electoral, los principales voceros del partido Demócrata -y también los de la democracia imperialista europea- han ocultado la cuestión de la guerra por abajo el felpudo. Un largo posteo oficial de Obama ni la menciona, después de varias invocaciones a la “unión nacional”. La guerra imperialista en desarrollo, que comenzó bajo el mandato de Biden, está en el horizonte estratégico de republicanos y demócratas.

Para Trump, la continuidad de la guerra con Irán es también un recurso para prevalecer sobre la Unión Europea, en medio del agravamiento de la guerra entre Ucrania y Rusia y los acuerdos por «separado» entre Putin y el propio Trump.

Un escenario de escalada militar, por un lado, y mayor autoritarismo, por el otro, agravará la crisis política y los estallidos populares al interior de los Estados Unidos, en medio de una crisis financiera en ciernes. El eje de la crisis mundial pasa por el corazón del imperialismo.

Por Marcelo Ramal (Política Obrera).


Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. La victoria demócrata, que se consideraba segura en Representantes (diputados), también tuvo lugar en el Senado, donde la composición final sería de 52 o 53 escaños demócratas contra 48 o 47 de los republicanos. Los reveses de Trump abarcaron a estados con un dominio histórico de su partido, como Carolina del Norte y del Sur -en este último caso, ganaron los demócratas después de 25 años de mandatos republicanos; también en el bastión petrolero de Texas, donde se impuso un senador demócrata después de 38 años, y lo mismo en Kansas, después de casi un siglo de hegemonía republicana. En Florida, bastión del exilio derechista cubano y venezolano y corazón del movimiento MAGA, la candidata republicana María Salazar había tomado distancias de Trump para salvar el voto migrante. A pesar de ello, sólo se imponía por una diferencia del 0,1%, en un escrutinio voto a voto. En Michigan, la victoria del candidato de origen musulmán Abdul El Sayed lograba prevalecer después de una furiosa campaña en su contra de Trump y del sionismo.


Significado


Ningún observador reconoce un liderazgo o fisonomía política definida en la victoria demócrata: el hilo conductor del resultado electoral es el golpe asestado a Trump -los electores, que concurrieron masivamente a sufragar en un país donde el voto es voluntario- desplegaron una movilización política en rechazo a la carestía desatada por la guerra, la represión política y el “estado de excepción” impuesto por Trump contra la población migrante. Las redadas del ICE llegaron a convertirse en un factor de desorganización económica, al imponer una zozobra que afecta a una parte de la fuerza laboral del capitalismo americano. La tentativa de “reindustrialización” del país a costa de sanciones comerciales extendidas tuvo pobres resultados y acrecentó la inflación. La carestía fue también estimulada por la instalación de los centros de datos para la oligarquía tecnológica de la IA. En sus campañas electorales, los gobernadores electos de Texas, Ohio, Georgia y Pensilvania hicieron de la oposición a la instalación de estas infraestructuras un eje de campaña. 29 jurisdicciones votaron este martes medidas locales de restricción a estas instalaciones, con apoyo abrumador de la población. La política MAGA, en definitiva, sólo hizo grande a los negocios de la camarilla trumpista y la oligarquía tecnológica. Para la población explotada, sólo trajo inflación, salarios a la baja y mayor zozobra en el empleo.


Entre Mr. Veto y los acuerdos


“Con mi nombre en la boleta, ganábamos en todos lados”. Esto posteó Trump después de la derrota, desconociendo u ocultando que él mismo se había puesto al frente de las elecciones que acababa de perder. Pero la alusión a su figura apunta a lo que viene: la pretensión de erigir un régimen de poder personal, a costa de decretazos y de vetos. Las mayorías cosechadas por los demócratas no tienen la contundencia para desconocer esos vetos -tampoco para hacer avanzar hasta el final un juicio político contra Trump. content:
Number 114

Defying the zio-global dictatorship!


The grim trail of ZIM terror

Why anarchists must confront totalitarian humanism

Acorninfo


1. Defying the zio-global dictatorship

!


by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here


I am sure you don’t need me to tell you that we are heading into a crucial period of history.


Not only is the shadow of a possible world war looming over us, but our freedom is coming under rapidly accelerating assault.


Here in France, for instance, the system started out by simply ignoring schoolkids protesting against the poor condition of their schools and their lives, then went on to

gas

 and

beat

 them,

smear

 their uprising in the media,

team up

 with far-right street gangs to attack the ever-broadening revolt,

ban protests

 in city centres,

pass a law

 to make demonstrators pay for windows they did not break on the basis of some kind of assumed collective responsibility, place protesters under

house arrest

 as “terrorists”, constantly

lie

 about the size of the turn-outs,

manipulate

 social media algorithms so that people did not know about the demos and threaten to pull that communication plug

altogether

.


I should add that there is also the possibility that at least some of the protesters and looters were

agents provocateurs

 working for the system to undermine public support for the youngsters’ cause, although I have not yet seen any hard proof of this.


In an article for

Le Monde diplomatique

 (November 2026 edition), Benoît Bréville describes how politicians were lining up on TV to demand a fascistic response to the protests, with many blaming the left-wing opposition party

La France insoumise

 – president of the French senate Gérard Larcher even suggested the party should be dissolved.


“Others suggested creating thousands of new places in prisons on the model of Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, of removing benefits from the trouble-makers’ families or of hardening the law against minors”.


Bréville notes that curfews were imposed in several cities, policed by drones and helicopters. “Gatherings are banned and in certain neighbourhoods it is even forbidden to walk around with a rucksack or hat”.


He adds that the French railways, SNCF, cancelled trains to prevent some people from attending demos and those arriving by road and rail were subject to police checks.


 “In Paris, the army was mobilised to supervise the demonstrators, along with the brigade of regional intervention, the RAID (

Recherche, assistance, intervention, dissuasion

) and the national gendarmerie’s intervention group (GIGN)”.


But in the face of all that, numbers on the protests across France did not drop away and the uprising is still going strong as I write!


All across Europe protests are

breaking out

 – including against what looks like an attempted

German-backed

 EU

coup d’état

 in Poland – and it seems that policing is increasingly being carried out by

Eurogendfor

 (European Gendarmerie Force), the European mercenary army deployed, as one

X

 user

put it

, “by the EUSSR to crush local uprisings, hijack demonstrations, and stage coups. They have no ties whatsoever to the local population (they don’t even speak the language) and will ruthlessly crush any form of civilian resistance with an iron fist”.


Meanwhile, hitherto unthinkable restrictions are being placed on people’s international travel on the basis of them not being appreciated by the zio-imperialist mafia (ZIM).


Take, for example, the way that veteran anarchist and co-founder of Food not Bombs

Keith McHenry

 was banned from entering Canada essentially on account of the decades of state violence and harassment  he has faced for feeding homeless people (

see below

).


Much of the repression centres, of course, around critics of Israel and its genocidal activities.


Swedish academic Andreas Malm was

refused entry

 to the UK, where he was due to headline an anti-imperialist and pro-Palestinian conference, on the grounds that his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”.


New York journalist Jeremy Loffredo has also

revealed

: “The UK is refusing to let me enter the country to report on and investigate the ongoing crackdown against elderly Palestine supporters because my ‘presence in the UK is not conducive to the public good’”.

author: Shannia Cabuello
title: Molbog community exposes agenda behind land-use projects
content:
They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds.

“They want to take everything so we insisted on coming here to express ourselves. We will embrace our land even if they harass us. We will not give it even if we get hurt.”

Molbog community member Anjilon Flores from Balabac Palawan stressed this point as Molbog indigenous peoples travelled to Metro Manila ahead of US President Donald Trump’s visit.

They aim to amplify their resistance against the Department of Environmental and Natural Resources’ Enhanced National Greening Program (E-NGP) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

Along with multi-sectoral groups and environmental advocates, they exposed the E-NGP and EDCA as tools of imperialist war and resource plunder, threatening the life, livelihood, culture, and ancestral lands of the Molbog people.

Long before Spanish colonial rule, the Molbog community have been the traditional stewards of Balabac island, depending on coconut farming, shifting cultivation, fishing, and harvesting seaweeds for livelihood.

“Palawan is a key biodiversity area and known to be the last ecological frontier of the Philippines,” Bianca Intia of Kalikasan Timog Katagalugan (TK) said at a press conference on October 26.

It shelters several endemic animal and plant species, including Philippine Mouse-deer which are exclusively found in Balabac and nearby islands.

Flores described their fields as prosperous with cassava, banana, corn, peanuts, and rice, making it their community’s main source of income for decades.

For them, lands are sacred that require ancestral permission before undertaking any activities like when entering the land, performing rituals, planting, harvesting, and cutting trees.

Born in Balabac, Flores cannot accept the prohibitions imposed by the E-NGP in using their resources. “They would restrict us from cutting trees which we use for firewood. This is also the livelihood for most of us. What will happen if they forbid us? Our livelihood will also be gone.”

Bangsa Molbog leader Emmanuel San Esteban lamented the encroachment of Balabac Air Base on their homes, sacred prayer grounds, and burial sites in Barangay Catagupan without any consultation with their tribal officials.

“They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds. The mountains where we do our rituals were flattened,” San Esteban said.

The local authorities said that the remains of their ancestors would be transferred to a different location. However, this is against the principles and culture of the Molbog tribe.

The indigenous residents dread the impact of both projects, as it begins to disrupt their peace, routines, and tradition.

They stressed that access to their land has been restricted, limiting the products they could gather from the forest.

According to DENR, the E-NGP was signed to rehabilitate the estimated 1.2 million hectares of the remaining unproductive, denuded, and degraded forestlands by 2022. It also aimed to maintain and protect existing forests.

This was already implemented by the DENR in several areas in Balabac where trees were planted in Barangay Catagupan, Agutayan, and Indalawan.

The communities worried about fines for damaging plants under E-NGP while clearing farmland. Cutting a tree must also be replaced with a hundred more trees and a Php 6,000 ($94) fine.

Kalikasan TK underscored that E-NGP did not aim to benefit communities but only to carbon offset the Ipilan Nickel Corporation’s deforestation and mining operations in Brooke’s Point, Palawan.

The Molbog people also expressed concerns that monocropping and fast-growing plant species under the E-NGP could affect forest biodiversity and native vegetation.

“The E-NGP is within our ancestral domain, for which we had applied for a Certificate on Ancestral Domain Title (CADT),” said San Esteban, questioning how the project progressed faster than their CADT application.

They first filed their CADT application in 2004 but the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) only certified the application in 2019. To expedite the process, the NCIP required them to pay at least Php 1.6 million ($25,092.33). Their CADT remains pending.

San Esteban said that Balabac Air Base in Barangay Catagupan also pushed through because of the NCIP’s manipulation of the Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) process.

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: Esta vez la amenaza de desalojo es a la Lof Cona Torres
content:
Lamentablemente las amenazas de desalojos no paran y es en las provincias del sur donde corren más peligros pareciera. 120


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Kay-Pacha-Lof-.KONA-tORRES-mp3.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Kay-Pacha-Lof-.KONA-tORRES-mp3.mp3


Descargar audio


En este caso se trata de la comunidad mapuche Lof Cona Torres, ubicada en el paraje Colitoro, a 75 kilómetros al noreste de Ingeniero Jacobacci, Provincia de  Río Negro, quien ha denunciado nuevos hechos de hostigamiento en medio de una disputa judicial por su territorio.


El conflicto viene de hace tiempo, ya que  la comunidad recuperó su territorio en 2002, con el acompañamiento del Consejo Asesor Indígena (CAI), para regresar al lugar del que habían sido despojados sus antepasados.


Sin embargo, la disputa por la propiedad se remonta a 2007 y tiene como contraparte a Alfredo Abi Saad, quien reclama esas tierras. Según el relato de la comunidad, la entrega de tierras tuvo lugar bajo la figura de un supuesto préstamo, en un momento que Luis Cona, se encontraba en una situación muy difícil, ya que había perdido a su compañera y quedó a cargo de varios hijos con muy pocos recursos para sostener a la familia.


En ese contexto fue presionado o manipulado para ceder su territorio.  En ese mismo proceso, la familia sufrió el incendio de su vivienda y debió trasladarse a Ingeniero Jacobacci. Ese antecedente de despojo vuelve ahora a poner en riesgo su permanencia territorial.


La amenaza actual se apoya en una orden judicial de desalojo bajo la figura de “desalojo sumarísimo”.


La comunidad señala que el conflicto había quedado suspendido por la Ley 26.160 de Emergencia Territorial Indígena, pero que, tras la derogación de esa norma, el proceso volvió a avanzar. De todas maneras la Lof va a resistir y está acompañada por varias comunidades, que el sábado pasado realizaron una “Jornada anti Desalojos y en Defensa de la Lof Cona”, en donde expresaron su solidaridad y apoyo.


Cabe destacar que esta lucha de resistencia tiene también como protagonista a la Pillan Kuse María Torres Cona, quien a lo largo de su vida se ha destacado por su defensa de los derechos de su comunidad y de su pueblo y desde su lugar vino resistiendo el avance de proyectos mineros en Río Negro e impulsó una de las leyes de avanzada en materia de derechos del pueblo mapuche (Ley 2287 integral del indígena de Río Negro), junto con el Consejo Asesor Indígena.


Además, fue una de las impulsoras de la Coordinadora del Parlamento Mapuche Tewelche de Río Negro, que reúne 180 comunidades y de la cual es hoy la principal referente espiritual.


Esta lucha y protagonismo de María fue reconocido el año pasado por la Facultad de Filosofía y Humanidades de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba, y ahora contamos con su testimonio.


En primer lugar, escuchamos cuando ella habla sobre su historia y vivencias, y luego acompañada por el Lonko Marcos Cona comentan cómo es la situación que están pasando ahora. Agradecemos a las hermanas de Mapuce Kimún Radio y a la Coordinadora Mapuche Tehuelche de Río Negro por este importante material.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense.

author: infolibre
title: Ταξική επίθεση στην στέγη. Αγώνες ενάντια στις εξώσεις, τα funds και την καταστολή. Αυτοοργάνωση και κοινωνική κατοικία.
content:
Το βράδυ της Πέμπτης12/11, πραγματοποιήθηκε

στο χώρο του infolibre εκδήλωση σχετικά με την στεγαστική κρίση

, η οποία αποτελεί ένα από τα βασικά ζητήματα που απασχολεί κοινωνίες και κινήματα σε Ευρώπη και Ελλάδα, ενώ έχουν κινητοποιηθεί διεθνώς εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες άνθρωποι, και έχουν κατέβει στους δρόμους, για να διεκδικήσουν ένα από τα σημαντικότερα αγαθά για την ζωή και την επιβίωση του ανθρώπου, το δικαίωμα στην στέγη, το οποίο βρίσκεται «υπό πολιορκία» από κράτος, κεφάλαιο και διάφορα «κοράκια», κερδοσκόπους ( funds, servicers κτλ.). Η εκδήλωση πραγματοποιήθηκε μπροστά στη διεθνή κρίση και τον αναβρασμό των ευρωπαϊκών κοινωνιών, οι οποίες οργανώνονται και αντιστέκονται απέναντι στην ταξική επίθεση του κεφαλαίου, η οποία γεννάει στεγαστική κρίση, ακρίβεια, πληθωρισμό, χαμηλό επίπεδο διαβίωσης, και εν τέλει τον πόλεμο.


Η εκδήλωση περιλάμβανε

: απευθείας σύνδεση με μέλη της CGT από Βαρκελώνη, ανταπόκριση από Βερολίνο, και τοποθετήσεις από την Συνέλευση Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στη Αθήνα, της Ένωσης Ενοικιαστ(ρι)ών Θεσσαλονίκης και του Συντονιστικού Συλλογικοτήτων κατά των Πλειστηριασμών. Οι ανταποκρίσεις από το εξωτερικό μας μετέφεραν  την κατάσταση γύρω από το ζήτημα της στέγης σε ευρωπαϊκές μητροπόλεις (Βερολίνο, Βαρκελώνη), και τον τρόπο που οι λαοί απαντούν, διεκδικούν και κερδίζουν, ενώ στα «εδώ» έγινε αποτίμηση της σημερινής κατάστασης, τους πρόσφατους αγώνες στην Δυτική και Ανατολική Θεσσαλονίκη, και αναφορά στα εργαλεία που μπορεί να χρησιμοποιήσει το κίνημα απέναντι στο κεφάλαιο, τις εξώσεις και τους πλειστηριασμούς.


Τονίστηκε η αναγκαιότητα

οργάνωσης του αγώνα

 για το δικαίωμα στη στέγη, από τα κάτω, σε γειτονιές και σωματεία. Ενώ αναφέρθηκαν ενέργειες όπως για την υπεράσπιση της λαϊκής κατοικίας, πλαφόν στα ενοίκια, απεργία ενοικίου, παύση πληρωμών, κοινωνικοποίηση εταιρειών και πλαίσιο κοινωνικής κατοικίας έως κατάληψη στέγης.


Συγκεκριμένα, το

μέλος του

CGT

 στην Βαρκελώνη Ειρήνη, ανέφερε πως

το 2023 η κυβέρνηση της Ισπανίας είχε θέσει πλαφόν ενοικίου στις μακροχρόνιες μισθώσεις κατοικιών, αλλά όχι στις βραχυχρόνιες. Στη Βαρκελώνη ισχύει αυτό το πλαφόν, όχι όμως για τις βραχυχρόνιες μισθώσεις. Έτσι, ενοικιάζονται σπίτια για 11 μήνες. Στη Βαρκελώνη δεν υπάρχουν πλέον διαθέσιμα σπίτια. Το ενοίκιο είναι περίπου 1.100-1.200 ευρώ, ενώ ο μισθός δεν ξεπερνά τα 1.400.  ευρώ.Τα συνδικάτα ενώθηκαν ανταποκρινόμενα στο κάλεσμα του Συνδικάτου Ενοικιαστών για την απεργία της 11ης Νοεμβρίου στην Ισπανία.

Το συνδικάτο στέγης θέτει το ζήτημα της παύσης πληρωμής ενοικίων και οργανώνεται στις γειτονιές

, με ταμεία οικονομικής ενίσχυσης και συγκεντρώσεις υποστήριξης ανθρώπων που κινδυνεύουν με έξωση, απέναντι στα funds, με στόχο να αποτραπούν οι εξώσεις.


Η απεργία της 11ης Νοεμβρίου είχε ως αιτήματα την

παύση πληρωμών ενοικίων

 και την

απεργία διαρκείας

. Την υποστήριξαν 200 οργανώσεις. Το επόμενο βήμα θα πρέπει να είναι κάτι πολύ ισχυρό. Από την πλευρά της αστυνομίας έγινε χρήση αλόγιστης βίας, χρησιμοποιήθηκαν  σπρέι πιπεριού και χημικά. Η κυβέρνηση προσπαθεί να κηρύξει παράνομες τις πολιτικές απεργίες, όμως τα συνδικάτα κατάφεραν να διασφαλίσουν τη νομιμότητα της συγκεκριμένης απεργίας. Η συμμετοχή έφτασε το 60% στη Βαρκελώνη και το 80% σε άλλες πόλεις.


Δύο μέλη της

 κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών,

αναφέρθηκαν στην περιοδεία τους, που σχεδιάζεται να γίνει σε Ευρώπη και Ελλάδα, μέχρι τον Μάιο, ενώ αναφέρθηκαν στον χαρακτήρα του εγχειρήματος και στο όσα συνέβησαν πρόσφατα, την απόπειρα διωγμού τους από την πολιτεία και την απεργία πείνας του Αρίστου και της Σούζον

:  Η πρόταση της Κοινότητας για το στεγαστικό είναι η

κατάληψη στέγης

. Τα Προσφυγικά αποτελούν μια μορφή

κοινωνικής κατοικίας

. Από το 2014 λειτουργεί δομή δωρεάν φιλοξενίας ασθενών, σε συνεννόηση με το σωματείο του νοσοκομείου «Άγιος Σάββας».


Αυτό που μας ενδιαφέρει είναι η

οργάνωση από τα κάτω, σε επίπεδο γειτονιάς

. Ο αγώνας της απεργίας πείνας δεν αφορούσε μόνο τα Προσφυγικά, αλλά και την περιοχή των Αμπελοκήπων. Η οργάνωσή μας γίνεται από τα κάτω. Έχουμε 25 δομές. Κύρια στοιχεία μας είναι οι συντροφικές σχέσεις, η εδαφική διάσταση της κοινότητας, τα κτίρια και η ιστορία τους. Για εμάς το στεγαστικό είναι προτεραιότητα και βρισκόμαστε σε επαφή με ισπανικές οργανώσεις

. Αυτό που αναδείχθηκε στην Ελλάδα είναι η απουσία πλαισίου κοινωνικής κατοικίας.

 Μια κοινότητα μπορεί να αποτελέσει βάση και για την κάλυψη βασικών αναγκών. Υπάρχουν προσπάθειες αλλοίωσης του χαρακτήρα της γειτονιάς. Να ξαναζήσουμε μαζί …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI vice-president candidates share ambitions
content:
This story was updated on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 1:26 p.m. ET.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to each of the four candidates running to become one of two vice-presidents at Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. in

its Dec. 14 election

. Here’s what they had to share:


Aaron Aopaloktok Pedersen said three mottos are the heart of his campaign: “Homes we can own, a culture we all share, and money every Inuk can see.”


Pedersen, who is from Cambridge Bay, joined NTI last fall as a housing and homelessness project manager. Since October, he’s served as the chief operating officer of the organization’s

housing corporation, Igluvut

.


Igluvut will own and operate at least 25 affordable fixed rent apartments after they are constructed under a plan to build over 700 homes with the federal and territorial governments.


Pedersen said he wants to create pathways for renters to become homeowners by helping them access down payments.

He also wants to support social and cultural programming aimed at youth and elders and introduce annual reports that disclose how NTI spends its money in each community.


Robert Bourassa, from Pangnirtung, has worked in Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s marine and wildlife division since 2018, where he oversees the implementation of impact benefit agreements from protected areas. 


He also sits on the board of the investment firm Atuqtuarvik Corp., which invests money into Inuit-owned businesses.


“I want to see Inuit prosper,” he told Nunatsiaq News.


He has thought of getting into politics for a long time, he said, mentioning that his grandfather Ipeelee Kilabuk served as a Northwest Territories MLA in the 1970s. 


Bourassa said addressing the housing shortage and improving access to mental health services are his top priorities.


Under the federal budget, Canada pledged $50 billion for Indigenous people over the next decade in sectors like infrastructure, housing and education. Bourassa wants to lobby the government to make sure those funds support housing.


Paul Irngaut, from Igloolik, has been NTI’s vice-president since 2022.


He served as acting president after former NTI president Jeremy Tunraluk went on leave in December 2025. Tunraluk ultimately

resigned

 from the position, triggering a byelection which was held in May. Irngaut threw his hat into the ring to stay in the presidential post, but

lost

 to Gloria Uluqsi.


“I’ve always worked toward the betterment of Inuit, and I think I have a proven track record with the organization,” Irngaut said.


Last year, he helped oversee NTI’s signing of

a

$1.5 billion, 10-year implementation contract

 with the federal government, through which the organization secured $77.6 million per year in funding.


Irngaut wants to strengthen the territory’s fishing industry and create a “marine council” for discussions between Canada’s Department of Fisheries and Oceans and such organizations as the Nunavut Wildlife Management Board and Nunavut Water Board.


“We have to start talking closely with our government before devolution happens,” he said. “It’s important that we have all these things in place so that we can start protecting Inuit rights.”


Adamee Itorcheak serves as the Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s secretary-treasurer, a role he took leave from earlier this year to serve as NTI’s acting vice-president and, for a short time, acting president in the lead up to the May byelection to fill in during Irgnaut’s bid for president.


He also sits on the board of the non-profit Annauma Community Foundation and the Inuit Broadcasting Corp. He was president of Baffin Fisheries.


Itorcheak said he is focused on encouraging NTI to be more transparent about how it spends money, smarter spending, and revitalizing Inuktikut. He wants to continue the work he was doing under NTI’s $4.3-million education program, which aims to open an all-Inuktikut school.


“We need to make some conscious decisions on how we’re going to preserve our language.”


He also said “Inuit have to be front and centre” at talks about projects of national interest, such as the Kivalliq Hydro-Fibre Link and the Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydro Project.


Correction

: This story has been updated to correct information about Igluvut’s role in regards to the 25 affordable fixed rent apartments, as well as information about Aaron Aopaloktok Pedersen’s role in the plan to build over 700 homes with the federal and territorial governments.

author: Unknown
title: Konut fiyatları yıllık yüzde 21,1, yeni kiralar yüzde 24,5 arttı
content:
Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB), 2026 yılı Ekim ayına ilişkin Konut Fiyat Endeksi (KFE) ile Yeni Kiracı Kira Endeksi (YKKE) verilerini yayımladı. Buna göre konut fiyatlarını izleyen KFE, ekim ayında bir önceki aya göre yüzde 0,7 artarak 240,9 seviyesine çıkarken, yıllık bazda nominal olarak yüzde 21,1 oranında yükseldi. Yeni yapılan kira sözleşmelerindeki değişimi ölçen YKKE ise aylık yüzde 0,1 artışla 343,5 değerine ulaşırken, yıllık artış yüzde 24,5 olarak gerçekleşti.

İl ve bölge bazlı dağılımda hem konut satış fiyatlarında hem de yeni kira sözleşmelerinde en yüksek yıllık artış İstanbul'da yaşandı. Konut fiyatlarındaki yıllık artış İstanbul'da yüzde 24,8, deprem bölgesindeki Hatay, Kahramanmaraş ve Osmaniye hattında yüzde 23,7, Ankara'da yüzde 22,7 ve İzmir'de yüzde 17,9 olurken, en düşük yıllık artış yüzde 13,0 ile Edirne, Kırklareli ve Tekirdağ bölgesinde görüldü.

Yeni kiracı kira endeksinde ise yıllık artış İstanbul'da yüzde 31,0, Ankara'da yüzde 26,6 ve İzmir'de yüzde 20,0 seviyesinde gerçekleşirken, en düşük yıllık kira artışı yüzde 16,2 ile Adana ve Mersin bölgesinde kaydedildi.

Üç büyük ildeki aylık konut fiyat endeksi gelişmeleri incelendiğinde, ekim ayında bir önceki aya göre İstanbul'da yüzde 1,1 ve Ankara'da yüzde 1,6 oranında artış yaşanırken, İzmir'de yüzde 0,6 oranında azalış gözlendi. Endeks değerleri ekim ayı itibarıyla Ankara'da 269,2, İstanbul'da 233,1 ve İzmir'de 229,9 olarak hesaplandı. Yıllık bazda ise konut fiyatlarındaki artış hızı İstanbul'da yüzde 24,8 ve Ankara'da yüzde 22,7 ile Türkiye ortalamasının üzerinde seyrederken, İzmir yüzde 17,9 ile ortalamanın altında kaldı.

İstatistiki Bölge Birimleri Sınıflamasına göre bölgelerin yıllık konut fiyat değişimlerinde yüzde 24,8 ile ilk sırada yer alan İstanbul'u, yüzde 23,7 artışla Hatay, Kahramanmaraş ve Osmaniye bölgesi izledi. Artvin, Giresun, Gümüşhane, Ordu, Rize ve Trabzon bölgesi ile Bingöl, Elazığ, Malatya, Tunceli, Van, Bitlis, Hakkari ve Muş bölgesinde yıllık fiyat artışı yüzde 23,3 olarak ölçüldü. Konut fiyatlarının yıllık bazda en düşük oranda arttığı bölgeler ise yüzde 13,0 ile Edirne, Kırklareli ve Tekirdağ; yüzde 15,3 ile Balıkesir ve Çanakkale; yüzde 15,4 ile Adana ve Mersin oldu.

Yeni Kiracı Kira Endeksi verilerine göre ekim ayında üç büyük ilden İstanbul ve İzmir'de aylık bazda sırasıyla yüzde 0,5 ve yüzde 1,3 oranında düşüş yaşanırken, Ankara'da yüzde 1,3 artış kaydedildi. Endeks seviyesi Ankara'da 376,2, İstanbul'da 335,0 ve İzmir'de 333,0 düzeyine ulaştı. Bölgesel sıralamada en yüksek yıllık kira artışı yüzde 31,0 ile İstanbul'da görülürken, bu ili yüzde 27,1 ile Nevşehir, Niğde, Aksaray, Kırıkkale, Kırşehir, Kayseri, Sivas ve Yozgat bölgesi; yüzde 26,6 ile Ankara ve yüzde 25,9 ile Doğu Karadeniz illeri takip etti. En düşük yıllık kira artışları ise yüzde 16,2 ile Adana ve Mersin; yüzde 17,1 ile Edirne, Kırklareli ve Tekirdağ; yüzde 17,9 ile Balıkesir ve Çanakkale bölgelerinde kaydedildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Özgür Özel: Seçimi kazanacak cesarete ve ülkeyi yönetecek maharete sahibiz
content:
YENİ Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel, partisinin Ankara’da düzenlediği 1. Olağan Kurultayı’nda konuştu.


“Türkiye Yenileniyor” sloganıyla toplanan kurultayda Özel, partinin kuruluş sürecini, parti içi demokrasiye ilişkin düzenlemelerini ve ekonomi, adalet, dış politika ile toplumsal barışa yönelik hedeflerini anlattı.


“Müesses nizamın çarkları tepedeki bir azınlık için dönmektedir. İşte biz, o düzenin çarkına çomak sokanlarız” diyen Özel, partisinin “seçimleri kazanacak cesarete ve Türkiye’yi yönetecek maharete sahip olduğunu” söyledi.


YENİ Parti 1. Olağan Kurultayı çalışmalarına başladı


Bugün  13:00


Özel, 24 Temmuz’da kurdukları YENİ Parti’nin siyasi kuruluş sürecini kurultayla tamamlayacaklarını söyledi. Partinin ortaya çıkışını, CHP yönetimine yönelik yargı kararları ve müdahalelerle ilişkilendiren Özel, iktidarın siyasi rekabeti engellediğini savundu.


CHP’nin önceki kurultaylarına ilişkin kararları ve genel merkezine yönelik polis müdahalesini eleştiren Özel, bu gelişmelerin ardından yeni bir parti kurma kararı aldıklarını anlattı.


Özel, konuşmasında tutuklu İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu’na ve cezaevindeki belediye başkanlarına da değindi. Beşiktaş, Beykoz, Şişli, Büyükçekmece, Bayrampaşa, Ataşehir ve Adalar belediye başkanlarının YENİ Parti’ye katıldığını duyurdu.


Tutuklu yedi belediye başkanı YENİ Parti’ye geçti


Bugün  12:00


“Genel başkanı sadece üyelerimiz belirleyecek”


Özel, parti içi demokrasiyi güçlendirmek amacıyla ilçe başkanlarını, il başkanlarını ve genel başkanı doğrudan üyelerin seçmesini sağlayan bir sistem kurduklarını söyledi.


Eylül ayında ilçe, ekim ayında il başkanlığı seçimlerini gerçekleştirdiklerini belirten Özel, 8 Kasım’daki genel başkan ön seçimine ilişkin şu bilgileri verdi:


Tam 2 bin 502 sandıkta, 800 binden fazla üyemizin yüzde 82’sinin rekor katılımıyla Genel Başkan ön seçimini tamamladık.


Özel, mahalle, ilçe ve il meclisleri kuracaklarını, Siyaset Akademisi ve Dijital Katılım Platformu aracılığıyla üyelerin karar süreçlerine katılımını artıracaklarını söyledi.


Parti Meclisi’nin yapısını da değiştirdiklerini anlatan Özel, bu organın Parti Yasama Grubu, Parti Örgütü Grubu ve Politika Geliştirme Grubu olmak üzere üç bölümden oluşacağını açıkladı.


Asgari ücret, emekli aylığı ve sosyal konut vaatleri


Konuşmasının ekonomi bölümünde hayat pahalılığını, gelir dağılımındaki eşitsizliği ve barınma krizini ele alan Özel, YENİ Parti’nin ekonomik vaatlerini sıraladı.


Özel, asgari ücreti açlık sınırının üzerine çıkarmayı, ücret artışının işverenler üzerindeki yükünü devlet desteğiyle hafifletmeyi ve en düşük emekli aylığını asgari ücret düzeyine yükseltmeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi.


Barınma sorununa karşı sosyal konut stokunu artıracaklarını belirten Özel, sosyal konutlarda kira tutarını hane gelirinin yüzde 25’iyle sınırlama vaadinde bulundu.


Vergi politikalarına da değinen Özel, dolaylı vergileri azaltacaklarını, ücretlilerin gelir vergisi yükünü hafifleteceklerini ve vergilendirmede gelir ile serveti esas alacaklarını anlattı.


Tarım politikalarında ise çiftçilere alım garantisi vermeyi, mazottaki vergileri kaldırmayı ve çiftçi borçlarının faizlerini silerek borçları beş yılda yapılandırmayı hedeflediklerini söyledi.


“Bir daha kimsenin ele geçiremeyeceği bir yargı sistemi kuracağız”


Özel, konuşmasında yargı bağımsızlığına ve tutuklama uygulamalarına geniş yer ayırdı. İmamoğlu ve diğer tutuklu siyasetçiler hakkındaki davaların siyasi amaç taşıdığını savunan Özel, tahliye çağrısı yaptı.


“Tutuklama bir ön infaz yöntemi değildir. Son tedbirdir,” diyen Özel, iktidara gelmeleri durumunda yargının bağımsızlığını ve tarafsızlığını güvence altına alacaklarını söyledi.


Özel, “Biz iktidara geldiğimizde yargıyı ele geçirmeye asla çalışmayacağız. Bir daha kimsenin ele geçiremeyeceği bir yargı sistemi kuracağız” dedi.


Gazetecilere yönelik soruşturma ve tutuklamaları da eleştiren Özel, basın ve medya kuruluşlarının siyasi müdahalelerden bağımsız faaliyet yürütmesini sağlayacak bir düzen kurmayı vadetti.


Özel, adalet anlayışlarını dört başlıkta topladıklarını belirterek, “Mahkemede adalet, gelirde adalet, vergide adalet, sosyal hayatta adaleti sağlayacağız” dedi.


Eşit yurttaşlık ve barış çağrısı


Özel, YENİ Parti’nin sosyal demokrat bir parti olduğunu belirterek farklı kimliklerin, inançların ve siyasi görüşlerin eşit haklara sahip olacağı bir düzen hedeflediklerini söyledi.

author: James Crump
title: Spain Caps Rents and Protects Tenants After Four Million Join Protests
content:
Spain’s parliament has approved a package of reforms aimed at making housing more affordable, a day after four million took part in a

nationwide general strike

 over the country’s housing crisis.


The measures, proposed by prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s government, include extending eviction protections for vulnerable tenants and restricting speculative property purchases by preventing companies from buying homes for less than 70% of their assessed value.


Rent increases will also be capped at 2%, while those already above the government’s neighbourhood reference index will be frozen. A 10% tax on flats rented to tourists will also be introduced. 


The conservative Popular Party said it will repeal the reforms if it takes power in the 29 November elections, which were called by Sánchez after his government failed to pass similar housing measures.


“Yesterday, the right to housing won on the street and in workplaces, and I hope it will win again at the ballot box,” said interim housing minister Isabel Rodríguez after the vote on Thursday.


Spain has witnessed weeks of housing protests following the eviction and subsequent death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who was forcibly removed from the flat she had lived in for 70 years in September after she couldn’t afford rent increases.


The country has a deficit of 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to over a million by 2028. The average rental price of a home, €1,176, is equivalent to 98.7% of the average young person’s monthly salary, according to the Youth Council of Spain.


“We won’t stop until we transform this country’s housing model from top to bottom,” said Alicia del Rio of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.


Trade unions reported 90% turnouts among dockworkers and carmakers for the 24-hour strike on Wednesday – Spain’s first general strike in 14 years –

with “total stoppages”

 at Volkswagen’s factory in Navarre and SEAT’s in Barcelona, organisers said.


Around 85% of meat industry workers, 82% of waste collection employees and 75% from the energy sector also took part. In healthcare and ⁠social services roughly 38% went on strike, while 35% of postal service workers also joined.

author: Ming-Yeh T. Rawnsley
title: Making Hope Credible: Puma Shen and the Politics of Access in Taipei
content:
A HOME THAT can be renewed without repeated moves, a cultural allowance that continues into working adulthood, and an exercise service that comes to the neighbourhood: these are tangible reasons to pay attention to Puma Shen’s (沈伯洋) campaign for Taipei mayor. They also offer a way to test the comparison increasingly drawn between Shen and New York mayor Zohran Mamdani. Beyond the excitement surrounding an unexpected challenger, what would make the city more accessible to people with unequal resources?

Shen’s command of municipal policy has helped change how voters see him. Nathan Batto’s account dated September 28 describes how detailed answers helped him reach beyond his established image as a specialist in civil defence and Chinese information warfare. His appeal invites scrutiny of what that expertise could deliver for residents who find existing services difficult to use.

THE COMPARISON reportedly helped shape the contest itself. ETtoday’s Tao Ben-he (³³¥»©M) reported on October 29 that President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) drew inspiration from Mamdani’s unexpected rise when insisting on Shen’s nomination as the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) candidate. The reported connection poses a consequential question: if New York supplied inspiration for choosing a candidate, how much of Mamdani’s challenge to inequality has travelled with it?

Brian Hioe identified the distinction in New Bloom, also on October 29: Mamdani campaigned explicitly against socioeconomic inequality, while Shen has emphasised policy expertise and good governance. The proposals examined here suggest a distinctive contribution: reducing the practical burdens of using public provision. That could bring meaningful improvements, although its redistributive reach remains uneven, particularly where housing assistance depends on ownership.

Mamdani’s promises to freeze rents for rent-stabilised tenants, make buses free and provide universal childcare named household costs that government could reduce. His inaugural address on January 1 also connected childcare to taxing the wealthiest. Taipei need not reproduce those policies to learn from their political clarity: residents should understand whose circumstances will improve, who will contribute and what public authority will do.

Shen has offered a wide range of policy proposals. From that platform, I examine three areas—housing and urban renewal, cultural support for young adults, and neighbourhood exercise services for older residents—to assess how his proposals would change access to public resources. These examples reveal different relationships between administrative reform and inequality; they cannot establish the overall redistributive ambition of his platform.

HOUSING PROVIDES the hardest test. Taipei’s existing approach is not simply to leave residents to negotiate with developers. The city already promotes publicly led renewal and faster review through its urban renewal programmes. It also provides temporary accommodation and describes neighbourhood-based relocation as an objective, including arrangements involving social housing. Shen’s alternative must therefore demonstrate what it changes in practice.

His proposed circular urban renewal scheme (無限都更) changes the sequence of redevelopment. Willing owners would exchange existing property rights for a new home, or rights to use one, before their original site is rebuilt. The city would assemble an initial housing supply and manage the exchange; completed redevelopment would replenish resources for subsequent rounds. The objective is to avoid the familiar sequence of moving into temporary accommodation and moving again after reconstruction.

The scheme recognises disruption as a real cost, especially for older residents whose routines depend on nearby care and social relationships. It could make agreement easier without treating reluctant residents as obstacles. But Shen’s policy acknowledges limited initial supply. Its preference for nearby exchanges needs to be supported by identified sites and a realistic timetable.

Valuation is equally important. Shen’s scheme envisages settling differences between old and new property values, with loan assistance where needed. An older owner with little income may still struggle to bridge that difference. Independent valuations, accessible advice and safeguards against unaffordable debt would determine whether the exchange expands choice or mainly assists households already able to pay.

author: Unknown
title: Incekara: Determination of young people proves that resistance is possible
content:
Protests launched by high school students in Paris against poor educational conditions have had a domino effect, spreading across France and to other countries. What began as a protest over education has developed into broader opposition to the system, encompassing the rising cost of living, declining wages and the housing crisis. These developments have also drawn attention to Turkey, where exploitation and inequality are even more deeply entrenched. University students took to the streets in Istanbul on the anniversary of the establishment of the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), an institution created in the aftermath of the fascist military coup of September 12, 1980. Students protested against the government's increasingly repressive measures. Demonstrations in Beyazıt Square and Beşiktaş were particularly marked by anger over a directive issued by the Ministry of Interior concerning universities in September. Istanbul University student Yasin Incekara spoke to ANF and said, "The determination shown by young people during the March 19 protests demonstrated that it is possible to resist the repressive regime being established in Turkey and showed how these blockades can be broken."


'Young people face similar forms of repression worldwide'


Yasin Incekara, a second-year sociology student at Istanbul University, said that young people taking to the streets across Europe and other parts of the world reflected the problems they share. Incekara emphasized that although Europe is often portrayed as a prosperous society, young people there also struggle with poverty and the problems created by the capitalist system. He said, "Over the past few months, we have seen young people taking to the streets against poverty, the lack of a future and repressive policies, not only in the Middle East but also in Europe, which is presented as prosperous. The youth uprising that has emerged particularly in France shows that young people face similar forms of repression not only in Turkey but in many parts of the world."


'March 19 showed young people's determination to seek freedom'


Incekara said that although resistance in Turkey has been weaker than in other countries, the March 19 protests demonstrated how young people could break through the restrictions being imposed on them. He described the March 19 protests and subsequent developments as evidence of young people's determination to pursue freedom in the face of oppression. Incekara said, "Through their determination to demand freedom against oppression, young people demonstrated during the March 19 protests that it is possible to resist the repressive regime being established in Turkey and showed how these blockades can be broken."


'Repressive directives seek to label revolutionary students as terrorists'


Incekara said that the authorities had intensified repression through various mechanisms in response to the determination shown by young people in their struggle. He pointed to the 17-article directive sent to universities by the Ministry of Interior in September, which he described as fascist, as the latest example. He argued that the directive sought to label students involved in progressive and revolutionary activities at universities as "terrorists." Incekara said: "The directive explicitly refers to providing private security personnel at universities with training similar to that given to police officers, as well as intensifying efforts to recruit informants and pressure students into becoming collaborators. It also opens the way for officers from the Anti-Terrorism Branch to set up information stands at universities under the pretext of awareness-raising and preventive activities, allowing them to conduct intelligence operations. Through these stands, the police aim to criminalize students involved in political struggle in the eyes of newly enrolled students, portraying them as marginal groups associated with terrorism and manipulating newcomers with warnings to 'stay away from them.' Of course, this does not reflect reality. If there is any group seeking to spread terror today, it is the capitalist state and the police themselves."


'Families are also pressured to inform on their children'

author: Rachel Evans
title: Anti-racists counter protest far-right ‘Australia Marches’ rally
content:
About 300 people joined the “No to Racism: Migrants and Refugees Are Welcome” rally at Sydney Town Hall on November 8. It was organised by the Refugee Action Collective Sydney (RAC) to counter the far-right Australian Marches rally against migration.

The far-right rally, which featured speakers from One Nation, Libertarian MP John Ruddick and other right-wing influencers, rallied at the Royal Botanic Garden and drew about 500 people.

Speakers at the counter-protest included Lynda-June Coe, Wiradjuri and Badu Island woman and NSW Greens upper house candidate; Nour Salman from Australia Palestine Advocacy Network; Ishita Chakrabarty from Hindus for Human Rights; Bidjigal/Gweagal activist Jordan Ryan-Hennessy; Ann El Khoury, from University of Sydney Staff for Palestine; Beau Lyon from Action for Public Housing’ and Anisa, a Somali refugee who was held in the Naoero detention centre.

Chakrabarty spoke about the racism faced by Indian migrants and linked One Nation and the Australia Marches rally to the far-right Narendra Modi government in India.

Ian Rintoul from RAC, who chaired the rally, said the United States midterm elections were a huge blow to the racist politics of US President Donald Trump, but said anti-racist campaigners still need to get organised.

“The tragedy is that the racist policies of Australia Marches and One Nation are being fueled by anti-migration and anti-refugee policies of the Labor government,” Rintoul said.

“Labor is linking migration with the housing crisis; cutting the numbers of international students; has introduced fees that will make it harder for refugees to seek asylum in Australia and is implementing an ICE-like compliance force to round up people on temporary visas.”

Lyon said those in power are pushing racism to distract from the real cause of the housing crisis, the for-profit housing system.

“Migrants are not responsible for the housing or cost of living crisis,” Rintoul said.

author: Kieztreffen Pankow

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Lawyers condemn human rights violations vs protesters
content:
The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) condemned the arrest, restricted legal access, and prolonged detention of more than 300 protesters apprehended during demonstrations at Liwasang Bonifacio and Sucat People’s Park ahead of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

During a press conference at the Liwasang Bonifacio on November 17, the lawyers’ group stressed that human rights violations were committed against the detained protesters.

Legal counsels assisting the detainees criticized law enforcement authorities for allegedly delaying their access to clients, filing sweeping criminal complaints, and leaving them in detention over a long non-working holiday period.

Ephraim Cortez, president of NUPL, denounced police authorities for requiring clearance from higher authorities before allowing legal counsels to confer with their detained clients.

He said, “A lawyer’s access to their clients cannot rely upon clearance from higher-ranking officials, as this is our clients’ right to counsel.”

Cortez added that the detention already exceeded the 18 hours allowed by the law. “Those arrested are innocent. They were just protesting. They should be released.”

The protesters were taken into custody during standoffs at the Liwasang Bonifacio and Sucat People’s Park.

Lawyer Mary Jane Real said that arresting demonstrators inside Liwasang Bonifacio violates the law on public assemblies. She stressed that Liwasang Bonifacio is a freedom park. “You cannot be arrested for protesting here, because we have the freedom to protest in this place.”

According to Real, the nine individuals arrested in Manila are facing multiple charges including illegal assemblies, direct assault, resistance and disobedience to a person in authority, tumults and other disturbances of public order, and violations of the Public Assembly Act.

Real also raised alarm over procedural delays caused by the ASEAN Summit work suspension in Metro Manila, noting that even if bail is recommended, detainees remain behind bars since there will be no court personnel to process release orders.

“The inquest concluded yesterday… We are currently awaiting the prosecutor’s decision, but since today is a holiday, no action can be taken until everyone returns to the office on Thursday,” Real said. “Consequently, even posting bail is not possible, as there is no one available to sign the necessary documents.”

On the other hand, lawyer Zoe Caballero of Sentro Para Sa Tunay Na Repormang Agraryo

denounced the reported P9-million cumulative bail required for the detained protesters, most of whom are farmers, workers, and students from the Southern Tagalog region.

“They themselves have nothing to eat, so where are they supposed to get the P9 million? If they actually had P9 million, they wouldn’t have marched all the way to Manila just to make their voices heard,” Caballero said. “Now, we’re being told: ‘Yes, you have the right to speak, but this is the price you must pay to say what needs to be said.’ It turns out you have to be wealthy just to be heard.”

Real urged the public to stand in solidarity with the detained demonstrators, stressing that their protests against Pax Silica are meant to protect ordinary Filipinos from worsening poverty and hunger. “If we don’t oppose this, all we’ll get here in this ‘Pax Silica’ is hunger and poverty. These people, they are the ones making sacrifices so that we may uphold our rights.”

“We have a responsibility toward them; we must help them gain their freedom, because they risked their own lives and peace so that we could be free,” Real said. (AMU, DAA)

author: By  Jo Kimmy, Contributor
title: From Hospitals to Palantir HQ: Protests Across England Over Controversial Healthcare Data Deal
content:
London, England — “We need to take our power back! Our UK government needs to represent the interests of the British public, who elected them into power, not the Zionist entity,” said Taby Khan, a health research scientist protesting outside The Royal London Hospital.


On October 1, doctors, nurses, health care workers and members of the public took to the streets at more than 40 locations across England, demanding an end to the controversial £330 million ($442 million) contract between the National Health Service (NHS) and U.S. technology company Palantir.


The mobilization was organized by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Health Workers for a Free Palestine, Amnesty International, Medact, Keep Our NHS Public, and other groups. They argue that a company known for its work with military and immigration agencies, including the development of AI and surveillance technologies, should not have access to the sensitive health data of

60 million people

 in England.


The protests began outside hospitals across the country, including four locations in London, before culminating in a demonstration outside Palantir’s London headquarters.


Located in central London, Palantir’s London office is the company’s

largest globally

, employing more people than its Silicon Valley headquarters. In front of the building, with its dark, heavily tinted windows and no visible signs identifying it as Palantir’s offices, hundreds of people chanted, held signs and displayed a giant symbolic notice calling for the contract to be terminated.


The demo was largely peaceful, although verbal tensions arose between anti-Palantir protesters and Zionist agitators who were trying to disrupt the demonstration and provoke tensions. Some protesters accused the police of allowing these tensions to develop.


The protest brought together concerns that might otherwise remain separate: the privatization of public services, the security of patient information, the expansion of surveillance technology and Palantir’s involvement in war crimes.


Palantir and the NHS: Who Owns Britain’s Health Data?


The NHS was officially

established

 on July 5, 1948, marking the first time a Western country provided free medical care to its entire population, regardless of status.


The relationship between the NHS and the U.S. tech company

began with an “emergency” contract

 under which Palantir offered to support the vaccination program and data management projects. In 2023, with little consideration for alternative solutions, Palantir was awarded the

contract

 to deliver the

NHS Federated Data Platform (FDP)

.


As the

NHS Data Professionals

 explain: “duplications and local variations prevent smooth linkage across datasets and regions.” The FDP is intended to help NHS organizations connect information held across different systems, making it easier to coordinate services, plan capacity and support operational decisions.


The underlying challenge is real: information can be fragmented across hospitals, general practices and regional services, making it difficult to build a joined-up picture of patient care.


Data analysts have raised concerns about the FDP’s highly centralized structure. Palantir supplies data engineers and manages the underlying infrastructure, which provides limited transparency and leaves NHS organizations with less ability to independently adapt the software to their needs.


From Military Intelligence to Public Healthcare


“Palantir is here to disrupt…and, when it’s necessary, to scare our enemies and, on

occasion, kill them.” –

Alex Karp, Palantir CEO


During the protest in front of Palantir’s London headquarters, a letter written by an anonymous NHS data analyst was read aloud. In it, the analyst described how she had begun to hate her job, working with software developed by a company responsible for the deaths of hundreds of her healthcare colleagues.


Palantir initially focused on government, military and intelligence agencies before expanding into the commercial and wider public sectors. The NHS FDP operates on the Foundry software, which is marketed as a system for the “modern enterprise.” Its other products include Gotham, used for “defense and resilience,” and Apollo, which manages software deployment.


The company’s military business is central to why many healthcare workers oppose its role in the NHS. Its

close involvement in U.S. and Israeli military operations

, alongside accusations of complicity in war …

author: Ariadna Wdowiak
title: El Servicio Penitenciario Federal es responsable directo de las condiciones inhumanas
content:
11 de febrero de 2026: El hombre que ríe acaba de arrastrar más de cincuenta metros a un fotoperiodista enceguecido por el gas pimienta en spray a quemarropas que le echó Gendarmería desde el otro lado de las vallas sobre la cara


Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo no son protagonistas de una zaga de aventuras ni de una serie policial. No son héroes mitológicos. Son dos trabajadores precarizados que militaron y participaron de la cosa pública siempre que pudieron y lo sintieron de esa manera. Pero hoy siguen en prisión preventiva en el penal federal de Marcos Paz por su participación en las protestas del 11 de febrero contra la reforma laboral, frente al Congreso. Tolomeo fue detenido el 15 de febrero. Y Gallo, el 18 de marzo. El Ministerio de Seguridad denunció de terrorismo a los responsables de los incidentes, y el fiscal Carlos Stornelli pidió aplicar el artículo 41 quinquies, que duplica las penas, pero el juez Gonzalo Rúa rechazó ese agravante al dictar la preventiva. Hoy, ambos esperan un juicio oral sin fecha. Desde el 8 de noviembre, Tolomeo hace huelga de hambre en reclamo de su libertad, de agua potable y alimentos, y de mejoras en las condiciones de detención. CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogadas y Abogados piden el cierre de la causa, mientras el Gobierno sostiene que hubo una acción organizada para desestabilizar el orden institucional.


Texto y fotos Andrés Manrique (

ANRed).


 


23 de septiembre de 2026: un Carlston.


El miércoles 11 de febrero, mientras el Senado aprobaba la reforma laboral, una multitud se movilizó frente al Congreso en una marcha convocada por la CGT y distintos sectores sociales y políticos.

El operativo de seguridad, según el Gobierno, terminó con 71 detenidos

. 51 detenciones estuvieron a cargo de fuerzas federales, y 20 las ejecutó la Policía de la Ciudad. La fiscalía fue liberando a la mayoría de los y las detenidas los días siguientes. Entre otros, se detuvieron a personas en situación de calle, a kilómetros de los hechos, sin la más mínima prueba y a más  de un mes de la movilización. Pero quedaron algunos casos por definir. Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo, no fueron apresados ese día, ni cerca del Congreso.


11 de febrero de 2026: reforma laboral


El 11 de febrero, mientras Senadores aprobaba una flexibilización nueva para el trabajo y una forma más radicalizada de precarizarlo, afuera del Congreso

 las fuerzas represivas estuvieron durante más de tres horas

 disparándole a manifestantes, a familias, a vecinos y a fotorreporteros con postas de goma, escopetas Byrna a gas comprimido, dos hidrantes, gas pimienta y granadas de gas lacrimógeno. En ese escenario bélico sostenido por

decisión unilateral del ejecutivo

, unos manifestantes arrojaron unas molotovs del otro lado de las vallas.


Los derechos no se consiguieron pidiendo por favor


La causa


Milton Tolomeo


Milton fue detenido el 15 de febrero en su trabajo

, donde era operario de maestranza. Además, es masajista deportivo, oficio que ejercía por las tardes. Dicho en sus propias palabras, es una «persona que no soporta las injusticias y que siempre creyó que es posible cambiarlas, que siempre hay que involucrarse cuando éstas suceden y no resignarse ni mirar para otro lado», lo que lo llevó a movilizarse contra la reforma laboral el 11 de febrero de 2026.


Entre el 12 y el 13 de febrero, Alejandra Monteoliva -Ministra de Seguridad-, anunció que su cartera denunciaría por terrorismo a los responsables de los incidentes. Dijo que habían realizado una acción organizada para desestabilizar el orden institucional. En esa campaña, el Ministerio difundió un video con cuatro sospechosos y una lista de 17 implicados: Milton Tolomeo no figuraba en el video nu en la lista.

A Monteoliva se la denunció penalmente junto a jefes del operativo por incumplimiento de deberes

. Tolomeo fue detenido a mediados de febrero y el Gobierno lo estigmatizó, difundiendo su cara, con el rótulo de “anarquista de la Molotov”. El domingo 15 de febrero, la ministra salió a celebrar por redes: “Dijimos que lo íbamos a encontrar y lo encontramos” No tenía pruebas suficientes.

title: Faith groups stand with detained protesters
content:
Police arrest protesters, including members of alternative media and student publications, in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, on November 15, 2026. The protesters are part of a delegation who are set to join a protest in Manila against Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump's visit. Photo from Bayan Laguna

“What we are fighting for is engagement and trade grounded in equality, respect for sovereignty, and mutual benefit.”

Ecumenical councils, Christian youth, and Catholic bishops denounce the US-led critical minerals deal and state crackdown ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit.

More than 300 protesters were detained at Camp Bagong Diwa of the Philippine National Police in Taguig City following aggressive police dispersals on November 15. Police dispersed the Southern Tagalog Lakbayan protest caravan in Sucat, Parañaque and Muntinlupa while separate clashes happened at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila.

The protests targeted the proposed signing of the Pax Silica framework during US President Donald Trump’s visit to Manila. Meanwhile, Protestant, ecumenical, and Roman Catholic leaders warned that they will sacrifice Philippine sovereignty, ancestral lands, and public utilities to US geopolitical and corporate interests.

In a pastoral statement issued Nov. 12, 2026, the National Council of Churches in the Philippines (NCCP) condemned both the economic terms of Pax Silica and the Marcos Jr. administration’s suppression of constitutionally guaranteed freedoms. “In a display of servility to the US, the government of Pres. Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is rolling out the red carpet, spending billions of pesos on lavish preparations while ordinary Filipinos struggle with poverty, rising prices, and economic hardship. In true ‘Imeldific’ fashion, authorities are clearing Manila’s streets of vendors and urban poor communities to conceal poverty from visiting dignitaries. Worse, they have imposed a ban on protests, suppressing constitutionally guaranteed freedoms.”

Signed by NCCP Chairperson The Most Rev. Brent Harry W. Alawas and General Secretary Minnie Anne Mata-Calub, the statement warned that Pax Silica’s push for critical minerals, semiconductor supply chains and artificial intelligence data centers places the country squarely in the crosshairs of superpower conflict. “More alarming is the prospect of signing the lopsided Pax Silica agreement during Trump’s visit. Designed to secure US access to critical technology supply chains, including artificial intelligence and critical minerals, the agreement places Philippine resources and sovereignty at the service of US strategic interests amid its rivalry with China. Pax Silica threatens to intensify large-scale mining, resource extraction, and data center development, resulting in environmental destruction and the displacement of Indigenous Peoples and farmers.”

Meanwhile, youth leaders from the United Church of Christ in the Philippines—Middle Luzon Jurisdictional Area Christian Youth Fellowship (UCCP MLJA-CYF) echoed this call in a manifesto titled “Kapayapaang Para sa Sangnilikha, Hindi Para sa Imperyalistang Bansa!” and warned that communities in Central Luzon will bear the brunt of the project’s ecological and social costs. “While we recognize the importance of technological and economic development, such progress must never come at the expense of Philippine sovereignty, the welfare of the people, the protection of creation, the rights of Indigenous Peoples on the margins, and peace not only in Luzon but across the entire Philippines… What we are fighting for is engagement and trade grounded in equality, respect for sovereignty, and mutual benefit—not the domination of a few and entanglement in conflicts that should never become the burden of the Filipino people.”

Caritas Philippines president and San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza said in August that the proposed Tarlac development zone directly threatens Indigenous communities and vital local resources. “The site is not empty land. It is home to Aeta Indigenous families, farmers, and rural communities whose rights and livelihoods must come before corporate and geopolitical interests. Pax Silica must not become another pretext for land conversion, displacement, destructive mining, or the diversion of electricity and water away from public needs.”
