title: Demo 1×1 Flyer für Gen-Z Proteste
content:
Wir haben zu oft gesehen wie Menschen sich filmen, unvermummt Pyro zünden oder ohne Handschuhe Steine auflesen. Daher haben wir einen kleinen Demo 1×1 Flyer geschrieben.


Druckt den Flyer vor den Protesten und verteilt ihn auf den Demos. Ihr könnt auch Einweghandschuhe auf der Demo verteilen (am besten sollten Menschen 2 Paare übereinander ziehen). Animiert und zeigt Menschen auch wie man sich mit einem Tshirts vermummt, wenn es Action gibt.


Wichtig: Ergänzt die lokale Nummer des Ermittlungsausschuss vor dem Drucken. Schreibt denen auch und fragt, ob sie an dem Tag aktiv sind.


Druckt nur in linken Läden und sagt den Menschen vorher, dass ihr solche brisanten Sachen drucken wollt. Am besten Face-to-Face, notfalls mit verschlüsselter Mail anschreiben. Normale Drucker speichern die Text, die mit ihnen gedruckt wurden.


Druckt nur DNA frei. Das bedeutet habt recht frisch gewaschene lange Klamotten an. Kauft neues Papier und neue Tüten zum Transport der Flyer. Vorher nochmal alle Arbeitsutensilien und Unterlagen mit Chlor reinigen. Beim Drucken nicht in Gesicht, Haare oder auf eure Klamotten fassen und Einmalhandschuhe tragen.


Am besten helfen mehrere Menschen beim verteilen auf der Demo. Wenn am Anfang noch nicht alle schwarz angezogen sind, in bunt aber recht unkenntlich die Flyer verteilen. Nur mit Handschuhen verteilen. Möglicherweise auch weitergeben lassen.


Demo 1×1


Redet nur mit Personen über Aktionen, die mitmachen. Ihr wisst nie wer mithört oder sich im schlimmsten Fall verplappert. Redet nur face-to-face ohne Handys.


Seid am besten zu zweit auf der Demo, organisiert euch evtl. in einer größeren Gruppe. Redet vorher über alle möglichen Aktionen und ob ihr die Konsequenzen, wie Knast, ertragen könnt.


Überlegt euch ein Handzeichen und ein Wort (z.B. „Backofen“) das ihr ruft, wenn ihr euch auf der Demo verliert. Ruft auf keinen Fall eure echten Namen.


Nehmt keine Handys oder Smart-Watch mit und macht keine Fotos oder Videos (potenzielle Beweismittel). Solltet ihr euer Handy dabeihaben, schaltet es jetzt aus!


Keine Gespräche über Politik, die Demo oder Straftaten bei An- und Abreise.


Bei Vorkontrollen, nett sagen, dass ihr einkaufen geht. Ansonsten nur angeben: Name, Adresse, Familienstand, Staatsangehörigkeit und Berufsbezeichnung. Keine Arbeitsstelle oder Name eurer Schule oder Uni.


Keine Straftaten ohne Handschuhe und Vermummung, sowie in Klamotten die ihr im Alltag anhabt. Fingerabdrücke, Kleidung und DNA sind Beweismaterial.


Vermummung ist strafbar. Wechselt euer Outfit (nicht nur die Vermummung) nur für die Zeit, in der ihr unerkenntlich sein wollt. Zieht euch nur in Menschenmassen, oder Gebüschen um, wenn ihr nicht gefilmt werdet und geht dann weg.


Cops versuchen während und nach der Demo Menschen festzunehmen. Auch Zivicops ohne Uniform folgen Menschen in der Demo. Wenn euch Menschen folgen, sagt ihnen nett & bestimmt, dass sie gehen sollen.


Cops beklagen, dass (brennende) Barrikaden auf den Straßen ihnen erschweren Menschen mit Autos zu verfolgen und wenn einzelne Streifen von mehreren Menschen angegriffen werden, sie erst mehr Kräfte zusammenzuziehen müssen.


Bei Festnahme: Keine Aussage oder Unterschrift! Du hast das Recht auf einen Anruf – ruf den EA an! Keine Mitarbeitspflicht; also nicht laufen, reden oder vermummen für Videos/Bilder. Grimassen schneiden bei Fotos. Bei DNA-Abnahme Beschluss von Richter*in verlangen. Nach Verhaftung zu Sprechstunde der Roten Hilfe gehen.


Redet niemals über vergangene Straftaten, erst recht nicht mit Handys oder online.


Cops versuchen oft Personen in vermeintlichen Smalltalk zu verwickeln. Am besten einfach ignorieren und nichts sagen, dann könnt ihr euch nicht verplappern.


Nehmt euch Zeit für eine emotionale Nachbesprechung und meldet euch, wenn nötig, bei „Out Of Action“.

Personalausweis, Schlüssel, Bahnkarte, Bargeld, Wasserflasche (still)


Telefonnummer des EA (Ermittlungsausschuss) mit Edding auf den Arm schreiben, dieser kontaktiert solidarische Anwält*innen bei Verhaftungen

Cops filmen; versucht euch so anonym wie möglich zu kleiden (keine Rückschlüsse auf Geschlecht, Tattoos, Körperbau, Körperbehaarung…)

schwarzes Shirt fürs Gesicht (legal bei Anreise, illegal beim Tragen)

author: Charlotte England
title: Mamdani Abolishes Violent Police Protest Unit
content:
Zohran Mamdani is set to disband a controversial New York City police unit known for using excessive force against protesters.


The New York City mayor laid out plans on Monday to scrap the Strategic Response Group (SRG) in favour of a “civilian-led approach” to policing protest that will put “communication, de-escalation” and “coordination” front and centre.


In a joint statement with the city’s police commissioner, Jessica Tisch, Mamdani said his plan would involve replacing 600 SRG officers with a civilian team and a small specialised police unit to handle protests.


Abolishing the SRG – a highly militarised police unit that became notorious for its violent and racist policing of Black Lives Matter protests – was one of Mamdani’s core 2025 campaign pledges.


Under Mamdani’s reforms, the use of tear gas, rifles, painfully loud noises above 90 decibels and kettling – the surrounding and trapping of protesters, usually before mass arrest – will all be banned.


The mayor also endorsed a council bill that would ban the New York Police Department (NYPD) from ever reviving the SRG or its tactics.


The SRG has been subject to countless misconduct claims over the years. In 2020, Human Rights Watch accused the unit – which handles both protests and counter terrorism – of “serious violations of international human rights law” after officers trapped around 300 peaceful protesters in the Bronx neighbourhood of Mott Haven, then beat and arrested them for breaking a curfew they had been prevented from obeying.


More recently, the SRG has been accused of using excessive force against pro-Palestine and anti-ICE protesters, including punching people who are already pinned to the floor, heavy use of tear gas and mass arrests.


In October, Mamdani ordered the NYPD to conduct its first comprehensive review into use of force in more than a decade, and appointed a new chair of the Civilian Complaint Review Board to increase police accountability.


“New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat,” Mamdani said in a statement on Monday. “Protecting New Yorkers’ rights and keeping our communities safe go hand in hand.”


In March, Mamdani created the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety, which he said would strengthen violence prevention, change how the city responds to mental health crises and tackle the root causes of crime. Under the new plans, an unarmed civilian unit within the office, with no powers of arrest, will take the lead in engaging with protesters from 2028.


Within the NYPD, meanwhile, a new First Amendment Support Team (FAST) will respond to protests. Named after the constitutional amendment that protects freedom of speech and the right to peaceful assembly, the team of 30 armed officers will be trained to de-escalate tensions and communicate with demonstrators. They will be backed by a new Patrol Support Division, trained in crowd management, which will either accompany them to protests or be stationed nearby.


Under the new structure, the SRG’s counterterrorism functions will be separated from protest policing and instead consolidated within the NYPD’s Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Protesters condemn state government attacks on Palestine solidarity, free speech
content:
Rallies were held across the country on November 15 to express solidarity with the people of Palestine and oppose repression of speech and protest by all levels of government.

The national day of action against repressive laws was called by Justice for Palestine Magan-djin (JFP) as part of its campaign to repeal the Queensland Liberal National Party government’s laws which criminalise Palestine solidarity slogans including “From the river to the sea” and “Globalise the intifada [uprising]”.

Chris Minns’ NSW Labor government is supporting the Queensland LNP government in the High Court challenge brought by JFP to overturn the laws. Victorian Liberals leader Jess Wilson has vowed to ban the phrase “Globalise the intifada” if elected on November 28.

JFP spokesperson Remah Naji said repression is “uniting our political class” and “thousands of us are united in defending our right to protest genocide”.

“The crimes remain the crime of genocide, the crime of occupation and the crime of apartheid. There is no amount of repression that will distract us from Israel’s crimes or absolve our government from its complicity in them.”

Michael Bradley, from MARQUE Lawyers, which is representing JFP in the High Court Case, said: “Queensland is currently leading the way with its ridiculous law that criminalises mere words, but other states are watching and keen to follow suit.

“It is more critical than ever that a stand is taken — in the courts and on the street — to demand our basic rights: to assemble, to protest and to speak.”

The crack down comes as Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza and the Occupied West Bank, despite the so-called ceasefire. Its strike on the Nasser Hospital on November 12 — the only functioning hospital in Gaza — which killed six people, including surgeon Dr Rizq Shaira and a teenage patient, was condemned by 18 countries for violating international law.

As winter floods, storms and cold descend, many are still left sheltering in tents because of Israel’s restriction of supplies into Gaza. A nine-month-old baby died from hypothermia in Khan Younis in Southern Gaza on November 12 due to exposure to extreme cold.

Israel has killed at least 1610 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire took effect.

Jonathan Strauss reports that 500 people marched in Magan-djin/Brisbane behind a large banner featuring the banned slogan “From the river to the sea”, a frequent chant of the Palestine solidarity movement.

The other banned slogan, “Globalise the intifada”, was not commonly used at Palestine rallies in Magan-djin, but expresses a desire for international support for the Palestinian people.

Anti-Zionist Jewish activist Stephen Heydt told the crowd that “kifah” means “fight” in Arabic. At the end of his speech he and others revealed t-shirts with the “globalise” slogan.

Police soon forcefully intervened, arresting seven people throughout the rally, including Heydt and two women who had carried the lead banner.

Naji said genocide was the real crime, not protesting the complicty of the Queensland and federal government.

The seven arrests add to the 31 previously made under the anti-free speech laws. Some, like Heydt, have now been arrested twice.

JFP is pursuing a High Court challenge to strike down the anti-free speech laws. It is asking for financial support for this and is organising a fundraising event on December 11.

The rally also featured music from a local punk band and a Riff Raff brass contingent.

Pip Hinman reports from Gadigal Country/Sydney that hundreds took to the streets again for Gaza on November 15. They demanded that NSW and federal Labor take action for Palestine, and stop trying to suppress free speech — particularly those speaking up against genocide.

The protest was called to show solidarity with pro-Palestine supporters in Queensland, who are being criminalised for standing up against genocide, and called for the scrapping of bans on phrases which call for rights, dignity, peace and justice for those living between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

Minns wants to bring in similar laws, but is waiting on the outcome of the High Court challenge.

Speakers at the protest included Dr Shamikh Badra, who is from Gaza. He called on the federal government to act for Palestine, and not allow the weapons trade to continue.

Badra condemned the strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza. He said people were still being denied food, medical assistance and other aid, and …

title: Women in Arzoxlî protest against delivery of solar panels
content:
The dispute over the construction of two solar power plants is escalating in the village of Arzoxlî (Turkish: Kervanpınar), in the Sur district of Amed (Diyarbakır). Although an administrative court has temporarily suspended the implementation of the Zenkar-2 project, preparations for the neighboring Zenkar-1 project are continuing. On the 23rd day of a protest vigil against the construction work, trucks delivered solar panels intended for the project to the site.


In response to the delivery, women from Arzoxlî gathered in the village square and marched together toward the construction site. Chanting slogans such as “Excavator operators, get off our grazing land,” “Axa me ava me hebûna me ye” (Our land and water are our existence), “Resistance leads to victory” and “No to companies in Arzoxlî,” they protested against the continuation of the project.


Soldiers block access to construction site


On their way to the project site, the villagers were stopped by Turkish gendarmerie. The soldiers blocked their access and prevented them from proceeding any further. The protesters expressed their anger at the soldiers’ actions.


Residents of Arzoxlî are demanding that construction work on the Zenkar-1 solar power plant also be halted. While a court order has already suspended construction of Zenkar-2, the villagers continue their resistance against the second project through a permanent protest camp.


Women in Arzoxlî continue resistance against solar power project

author: Unknown
title: Families of ill prisoners call for action outside Ministry of Justice
content:
The protest, initiated under the leadership of the Federation of Associations for Legal Solidarity with the Families of Prisoners and Convicts (TUHAD-FED), following a call by DEM Party MPs and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), continued into its third day.


The protest was supported by the families of ill prisoners Newroz Bozkurt, Ömer Güneri, Yakup Akman, Mehmet Ali Taşkın and Selim Çiftçi, members of the Istanbul Peace Mothers’ Assembly, and the Human Rights Association (IHD).


A banner bearing the names of seriously ill prisoners was unfurled, reading: “We are at the gates of justice; we will open the prison gates through resistance. Freedom for sick prisoners.” Protesters chanted slogans including “Release sick prisoners!” and “Revolutionary prisoners are our honour!”


Families said they didn't want their children to die 


Fince Akman, the mother of ill prisoner Yakup Akman, said that their children were not receiving treatment in prison despite suffering from serious illnesses.


“We no longer want our children's coffins to be brought out of prisons. My child and thousands of other ill prisoners are not receiving treatment in prison. We say, ‘Peace’. The PKK has laid down its arms, but the state has taken no steps. The first thing that needs to happen is the release of sick prisoners,” she said.


Hülya Güner Münüklü, the sister of Ömer Güneri, who is held at Elazığ No. 2 Prison, said that her brother had been kept in solitary confinement for four years and had received no treatment for four months despite having a broken leg.


Hülya Güner Münüklü said they had been informed that the hospital was not equipped to perform the necessary surgery. “Why are our sick prisoners not being released? Is this what peace looks like? Is there no justice for Kurds? We have done everything we can; now they must take steps too. Enough is enough,” she said.


Safiye Doğan Ergin, a member of the Istanbul Peace Mothers’ Assembly, also called for the release of Newroz Bozkurt, a prisoner suffering from leukaemia who had been transferred to Etlik City Hospital. “We have come to take Newroz home. We will not leave without Newroz. Newroz is on the brink of death. Why should prisoners have to pay with their lives for their beliefs?” she said.


No new law is needed to release ill prisoners


Özgül Saki, a DEM Party MP for Istanbul, said that there were at least 1,412 sick prisoners in Turkey's prisons, 58 of whom were seriously ill and needed to be released immediately.


Saki stated that ill prisoners' demands for medical treatment and release were already recognised under international conventions and Turkey's domestic legislation, emphasising that preventing prisoners from receiving medical treatment constitutes a crime.


Speaking about the ongoing Peace and Democratic Resolution Process, Saki said that those who had been imprisoned for 20–30 years because of their demands for a democratic resolution should be released. “There is certainly no need for a new law just to release sick prisoners. With a decision by the Ministry of Justice, they could all be reunited with their families tomorrow,” she said.


Saki noted that while no deaths had occurred on the ground following the cessation of armed clashes, sick prisoners continued to lose their lives in prisons. “Turning a blind eye to preventable deaths is a war crime,” she said, reiterating her call for the immediate release of sick prisoners.


The sit-in protest outside the Ministry will resume today, Friday, at 2 p.m.

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Freed Southern Tagalog activists to file counter charges vs police
content:
Photo by Kyle Justin Macabalitao/Bulatlat

This is the spirit of the released delegates of the Lakabayan Southern Tagalog who were violently arrested and detained by the police last November 15 in barangay Sucat, Muntinlupa City. In a press conference on November 19, they announced that they will file counter charges against the officers of the Southern Police District (SPD).

National Union of People’s Lawyers (NUPL) President Ephraim Cortez said the arrest of more than 200 activists and 18 journalists can be considered illegal. Cortez maintained that the police violated the provisions of the Batasang Pambansa Blg. 880 for obstructing or disrupting a peaceful assembly, Article 124 of the Revised Penal Code for arbitrary detention, and Republic Act No. 7438 for the right to counsel.

“The police have already violated their own guidelines and the rights of their arrestees on how they should have been treated during the arrest, not to mention the injuries that they sustained,” said Cortez.

Niezelle Visaya, spokesperson of the Lakbayan Timog Katagalugan, recalled how hundreds of police personnel from the SPD intimidated and harassed the delegates of Lakbayan, from morning until 2 p.m. of November 15 while they were holding a program at Sucat People’s Park.

Visaya said that at around 2:00 a.m. of November 15, hundreds of police from the SPD went to the Sucat People’s Park, intimidating the delegates who were there to rest. The police also started to block the entry and exit points of the delegates.

“They began violently arresting the organizers. Some of us were brought up to the Barangay Police Headquarters, where we were placed in small rooms that don’t have proper ventilation. They continued to bring mothers, Indigenous People, and even children into these rooms,” Viasaya said.

Community journalist Marky Casquite from the Southern Tagalog Exposure also recalled how he was arrested by the police despite his assertion that he is a member of the media.

“I was suddenly picked up and arrested by the police despite showing my media ID,” Casquite said.

“They handcuffed me. They were not even content with that, they also dragged me to the barangay hall leaving me with injuries to my arm from the tightly fastened handcuffs and to my knee from being dragged,” Casquite said, adding that he did not receive first aid even though he was already bleeding.

Lucky Oraller of the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan – Timog Katagalugan (BAYAN-TK) demanded that charges against them and others who were arrested should be junked.

“While Marcos welcomed Trump through the red carpet, his forces dragged, caught, and arrested the ordinary Filipino just to welcome Trump for the ASEAN Summit,” said Oraller.

Oraller also decried how their cellphones and other protest paraphernalia were confiscated, including the vehicle and effigy.

While it was confirmed that the phones were returned to the delegates, the placards, streamer, effigy, and the vehicle along with the bags inside have not been returned, Oraller said.

“We’re not sure what the police could do to our vehicles and bags that are still in Camp Bagong Diwa. [W]e call to the people to monitor the case, as there are threats that they would plant evidence to frame us up,” said Oraller.

title: İzmir'de otizmli çocuklara şiddet soruşturması: Gözaltına alınan 2 kişi tutuklandı
content:
İzmir – Narlıdere ilçesinde, bir spor kulübünde otizmli çocuklara kötü muamele ve şiddet uygulanmasıyla ilgili davada 2 kişi tutuklandı.

Narlıdere ilçesinde 2023- 2025 yılları arasında faaliyet gösteren bir spor kulübünde eğitim gören otizmli çocuklara yönelik kötü muamele ve şiddet uygulandığı yönündeki iddialar üzerine adli soruşturma başlatıldı.

Yapılan incelemelerde birden fazla çocuğun şiddete maruz kaldığı tespit edildi. Soruşturma kapsamında spor kulübünün ortağı olduğu belirlenen şüpheliler F.A. (29) ve Ş.Ö. (28) gözaltına alındı. Emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından adli makamlara sevk edilen 2 şüpheli, çıkarıldıkları mahkemece tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Russian Indigenous Activist Daria Egereva Remains Jailed; Arrested After 2025 U.N. Climate Talks
content:
Human rights and climate groups are calling on Russia to release two prominent activists, Daria Egereva and Natalia Leongardt, who have been held in pretrial detention in Moscow for nearly a year, since December 2025. Egereva, a leading Indigenous rights activist in Russia, was arrested shortly after attending the COP30 United Nations climate summit in Belém, Brazil, where she served as co-chair of the International Indigenous Peoples Forum on Climate Change. Leongardt has worked for decades to support Indigenous rights.


“Right now all we are demanding is the release of Daria and Natalia, because they shouldn’t be in prison. You shouldn’t be arrested for activism,” says Viktor Suliandziga-Bagat, an Indigenous rights activist and representative of the Udege people from the Russian Far East. He is living in exile due to the risk against activists. “I don’t think I can come back to Russia,” he says.

author: anred
title: Cabaret Voltaire, un puente al revisionismo de derecha
content:
Desde hace tiempo, el canal de stream rosarino viene llevando a cabo un cruzada en favor de la derecha peronista a la que no reconoce como tal pero que minimiza en lo que hace al rol de la represión paraestatal previa a la última dictadura militar. En esta oportunidad se despacharon con todo junto a un invitado de lujo: Rodrigo de la Serna.

Por Nicolás Salas.   


El ascenso de la ultraderecha en Argentina abrió un escenario de balances en la militancia en general y dentro del peronismo en particular. El derrotero que implicó el gobierno de

Alberto Fernández

 empoderó a algunos sectores que no sólo habían cuestionado su candidatura sino que además pronosticaron de antemano el fracaso del frente “Todos”. En los últimos años, figuras como

Guillermo Moreno

 supieron legitimarse en esos planteos y ampliar la escena política para la intervención de una tendencia que se mantuvo marginal o minoritaria dentro de lo que fue el auge de la lucha por los derechos humanos a principios del siglo XXI. 


Actualmente nos encontramos con periodistas, comunicadores o divulgadores que recuperaron esas banderas que, a principios del kirchnerismo,

Gerónimo “el momo” Venegas

 y

Hugo Moyano

 supieron agitar casi en soledad cuando nadie prestaba el oído a la exigencia por la reapertura de la causa por el asesinato del secretario general de la CGT,

José Ignacio Rucci

. “

Cabaret Voltaire

” es una versión actualizada, en modo stream, de esta disputa que viene saliendo a la superficie después de años en el subsuelo de la agenda política.  


El 8 de noviembre de 2026, el canal rosarino emitió un programa que contó con la participación del actor y músico Rodrigo de la Serna. La excusa del encuentro fue la presentación de la serie “

Gordon

”, policial basado en la historia de

Aníbal Gordon

, un mercenario de la represión paraestatal, de los servicios de inteligencia y de los centros clandestinos de detención entre las décadas de los 60′ y los 80′. La interacción del artista con Mauricio Vera y Tomás Trapé, conductores del programa, dio lugar a varios debates que trascendieron el abordaje mismo de la producción cinematográfica y pusieron sobre la mesa varias tesis (ponele) sobre la historia argentina moderna. Todas ellas sumergidas en

un revisionismo que pareciera perseguir un único objetivo que es el de deslindar responsabilidades políticas a quienes protagonizaron la represión paraestatal durante el último gobierno de Juan Domingo Perón y de Isabel Martínez de Perón

. Todo parece moverse con muy poca rigurosidad histórica y agitada sobre un balance crítico (y por derecha) de las últimas experiencias progresistas de gobierno.   


Tesis I : A partir de la figura de Rucci, hay que reconciliar a las partes en disputas dentro del peronismo de los 60’/70′


Como lo ha hecho en innumerables programas, Tomás Trapé volvió a referirse a Rucci y se animó a cuestionar una máxima de los organismos de

DD.HH

: “n

uestra responsabilidad histórica no es elegir, porque uno no tiene un muerto en ninguno de los dos bandos, sino que es construir la síntesis y el perdón, y para el perdón se necesita un gesto. Nosotros hemos hecho varios programas sobre Rucci, y lo de Rucci es un gesto para la reconciliación”. 


En la reconstrucción histórica,

organismos como las Madres e Hijos han marcado un hilo conductor entre la represión previa a 1976 y la ejercida posteriormente en la dictadura

. En algunos casos, las consideraciones sobre el personaje en cuestión y su rol con las patotas de ese entonces son muy claras: “

Rucci fue un asesino que mató a montones de pibes y a otros los mandó a la muerte porque los denunció. Que lo hayan matado de ninguna manera es un crímen de lesa humanidad. El crimen de lesa humanidad es cuando interviene el Estado

. La familia de Rucci ahora sale porque la derecha está saliendo», supo denunciar públicamente

Hebe de Bonafini

.


 


Para ir a una órbita ideológica más afín a los mencionados streamers, podemos citar a

Juan Manuel Abal Medina

 en su libro “

Conocer a Perón

” (1). Si bien sus 478 páginas orbitan en una reivindicación constante a la figura de Perón y José Ignacio Rucci, eso no impide que

el autor reconozca y exponga diálogos que corroboran la participación directa del exsecretario general de la CGT en la masacre de Ezeiza (junio de 1973)

, inicio de la contienda entre las diferentes tendencias dentro del peronismo que escalará (sin retorno) con el asesinato del mismo Rucci en septiembre de 1973 …

author: EDRi
title: New report documents authoritarian use of technology across the globe
content:
Privacy International's latest report documents how states are deploying authoritarian technology to stifle dissent, assert control and diminish human rights. The report conveys how surveillance technologies are being expanded and entrenched with the purpose of exerting control over entire populations and/or specific groups of people such as journalists and human rights defenders.

By Privacy International (guest author) · November 19, 2026

EDRi-member Privacy International (PI) have been observing and monitoring an increase in states’ adoption of authoritarian practices and policies. These practices are facilitated by new and emerging technologies or embodied in their very deployment to stifle dissent, assert control and diminish human rights. These digital technologies, such as facial recognition, social media monitoring, spyware, and more, are being deployed — both online and offline — by authoritarian and democratic regimes alike. PI have coined the term ‘authoritarian use of technology’ to describe this global phenomenon.

PI believes that the authoritarian use of technology goes beyond the unlawful use or abuse of technologies by states that the organisation has been monitoring and exposing for years. Authoritarian use of tech results in a systematic undermining of democratic principles, erosion of the rule of law, exertion of significant social and political control, or normalisation of the surveillance of individuals and their communities – particularly those already at risk.

These technologies are being expanded and entrenched with the purpose of exerting control over entire populations and groups of people at risk, such as human rights defenders (HRDs), journalists, lawyers, activists, dissidents and those from minority ethnic, national and religious backgrounds. This is being done to target, persecute or ostracise them. This ultimately creates a ‘chilling effect’, spreading a fear of reprisal, which serves not only to infringe upon the rights of certain individuals, but of whole communities and populations. In turn, this has a corrosive effect on democratic institutions, mechanisms of accountability, oversight and redress, and the fabric of open societies.

In their new report, PI examine the use of five technologies: facial recognition technology, mobile phone extraction, spyware, social media and intelligence monitoring, and mass communications surveillance. The report also provides several cross-cutting themes emerging from the authoritarian use of these technologies on human rights. These include: a systemic interference with the right to privacy, the erosion of and chilling effect on enjoyment of broader fundamental rights and freedoms, the disproportionate or discriminatory targeting of certain groups in society, the absence of clear legal basis, effective safeguards, and independent oversight, and lastly, the lack of accountability of private sector actors.

Facial recognition technology (FRT) is a technology that uses a camera to capture images of people’s faces and then extracts and processes their biometric data to verify an individual or identify a match against an existing image. The report collates examples of how governments and law enforcement are deploying FRT at protests to identify, monitor and track protesters either openly or surreptitiously, and even banning wearing face coverings at protests to facilitate it. The report also features case studies of FRT projects in the UK, Israel and the Occupied Palestinian Territories, and Brazil.

PI’s report includes a chapter on mobile phone extraction, which documents the technology being deployed to gather information and intelligence about activists, journalists, political dissidents, and migrants, which they believe to constitute an authoritarian use of the technology. Our electronic devices, such as our mobile phones and tablets, contain huge amounts of information and sensitive data about our lives. Mobile phone extraction involves extracting data from an individual’s device, or from the cloud services they use, including device information, photos, videos, audio recordings, notes, documents and apps used, as well as the messages, call logs and emails they draft, send and receive.

The report also gathers examples of spyware repeatedly being deployed by both authoritarian and democratic governments to conduct secret, intrusive surveillance of journalists, human rights defenders, opposition politicians, their family members and other …

author: webadmin
title: Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.
content:
Legendary animal liberationist Barry Horne honoured by Northants Sabs.


Just weeks after publishing damning footage of the

Quorn Hunt killing a fox and training hounds

 to attack, saboteurs descended upon their prestigious opening meet – and completely ruined it.


Quorn Killers and Horne Haunts Quorn. Banners proudly displayed by Northants Sabs at the Quorn killers opening meet, 6 November, 2026. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


The day saw violence and abuse by the hunt, and resulted in the arrest of a terrierman who attempted to flee from police.


The day was dedicated to Barry Horne, a legendary activist who made the ultimate sacrifice for animal liberation.


Barry was involved in numerous daring rescue operations, helping to free animals destined for experimentation. He died following a series of hunger strikes intended to pressure Tony Blair’s Labour government over its promise to hold an inquiry into vivisection.


Barry Horne, 17 March 1990, rescuing 82 beagle puppies and 26 rabbits from Harlan Interfauna in Huntingdon. The site is now associated with MBR Acres Ltd, and the long-running Camp Beagle protests against the breeding of dogs for laboratory experiments for the petrochemical, chemical and pharmaceutical industries.


The government reneged on its promise, and animal rights activists reacted with fury in Barry’s name, and thousands more animals, including cats, rabbits and guinea pigs were liberated by activists during his hunger strikes.


Barry was also formerly a member of Northants Hunt Sabs. He died on November 5, 2001. His death radicalised and mobilised countless more animal liberations in his name.

In September 2026 multiple dogs were liberated from the MBR site

.


On Friday 6 November 2026, a day after the 25th anniversary of Barry’s death, the Quorn Hunt held their opening meet at its kennels in Kirby Bellars, Leicestershire.


The day did not quite go as they may have planned.


The Quorn Hunt October 2026, kill a fox and use the body to train the hounds. Notice the huntsman blowing for the kill over the hounds as they tear the body apart. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


On the back of the horrendous footage released only weeks earlier, Northants Hunt Sabs, including personal friends of Barry’s, turned out to stop the Quorn Hunt from killing on their watch.


Part time whipper-in and terrier ‘man’ Mickey Vaughn practising for the regional gurning championship.

Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


Northants Sabs truly smashed the day, hunt tempers flared as sabs arrived at the meet with banners and flags speaking truth about ‘trail hunting’.


Vaughan bravely attacking a woman. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


True to form, the hunters natural default for violence saw sabs attacked and pushed to the ground. Sabs stood their ground following the violent outburst and the hunt was soon put back in their box.


Vaughan being put back into his box. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Sabs stayed on the hunt throughout the day, leaving huntsman Joe Tesseyman struggling to find opportunities to hunt foxes with saboteurs on his case.


Huntsman Joe Tessyman on the run from sabs and police alike. Image Northants Hunt Sabs


Then, near Cream Gorse, the hunter became the hunted.


A Quorn terrierman was spotted leaving the covert on a quad bike, with officers from Leicestershire Police’s Rural Crime Team in hot pursuit.


The hot pursuit began with a terrierman fleeing from police after leaving the covert. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Mickey Vaughan, the terrierman and occasional whipper-in, attempted to slow the pursuing officers down by positioning his horse in the road. Police moved him aside and continued after the terrierman on the quad.


The quad overturned, and the terrierman was spotted running up Pasture Lane with a police officer hot on his tail behind.


You can’t park that there, mate. Image Northants Hunt Saboteurs.


Clearly a runner he was not.


He was promptly caught, cuffed and arrested.


At first I was all like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


We couldn’t possibly comment on what the arrest relates to and will not speculate, but lets hope they throw “obstructing an officer” at him whilst they are at it. Same goes for Vaughan who attempted to prevent the officer from pursuing the masked terrierman.


Then I was like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Meanwhile the mounted field dwindled out, no doubt many of whom left thoroughly embarrassed by the thuggish behaviour of this supposed-prestigious hunt …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 19 November 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Making sense of the Digital Fairness Act, a very unmerry birthday to the Digital Omnibus, and more!

Last week, the European Commission put digital fairness on the menu with a proposal for its long-awaited Digital Fairness Act (DFA) – and we have some food for thought.

This law will strengthen consumer protection against manipulative and exploitative commercial practices, such as fake notifications designed to keep bringing us back to an app, endless scrolling that keeps us online way longer than you intended, and other personalised techniques used by online services that exploit our vulnerabilities. First things first, proposal actually takes some important steps forward by introducing new prohibitions on deceptive design, extending specific protections beyond the biggest online platforms, and recognising the harms associated with addictive digital features. However, we were left wondering – why promise digital fairness yet leave the users to do all the work instead of holding manipulative online services responsible? Read our analysis on Tech Policy Press.

Despite it all, the DFA proposal – something that actually might protect our rights online – is a welcome respite in the current wave of deregulation in the EU. This week, we’re also reckoning with the fact that November 19, 2026 marks one year since the Commission published the proposals for the Digital Omnibus. We, along with many other civil society organisations, had warned that this would be a massive reopening of EU’s core digital protections that would risk dismantling the very foundation of human rights and tech policy in the EU. One year on, it seems like we were granted Apollo’s gift of prophecy. On this unfortunate occasion, we’re standing strong with 100 organisations, experts, academics and more to urge EU lawmakers to not simplify away our rights.

In this edition, you can also explore our extremely thorough guide to the European Parliament’s 1840 amendments to the Digital Omnibus on Data, focusing on what they would mean for privacy, data protection and, ultimately, people’s rights. author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: The death of the word?
content:
Michelangelo,

Cumaean Sibyl

 (c. 1511), Sistine Chapel, Vatican City


This short article was originally published under the title “Morte della parola?” in the Italian newspaper

Paese Sera

 on 8 February 1968. It has been republished in the latest issue of the French magazine

Entétement

, although the original version can be found on the

La Voce di Fiore

 archive website. A Spanish translation of the same can be found at th magazine

Ficción de la razón

.


A book has recently been published in Paris,

Of Grammatology

 (1967), a work destined to cause a stir not only in the field of linguistic studies. Jacques Derrida, one of the most original figures in the new wave of French philosophical criticism, begins with the observation that, today, “through a movement whose necessity we can barely glimpse, everything that, for at least twenty centuries, has tended to be defined under the name of language, is beginning to be summarised under the name of writing”. It does indeed seem that writing—which, according to Rousseau, was nothing more than a complement to speech—is gradually freeing itself from its subordination to the phonetic medium, to the point of reversing its traditional relationship with language: writing would therefore not be a technique in the service of language, but rather, on the contrary, it is language that can be considered a specific case, an aspect, of writing.


To better understand the phenomenon to which Derrida refers when he speaks of writing dissociated from the phonetic element, one need only consider the example of mathematics, whose symbolic notation does not refer to any spoken language. If we consider that today we are witnessing a process of mathematisation across all the sciences, the “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon (readers who have followed recent news regarding the

in vitro

 synthesis of living matter, carried out by certain American scientists, will recall having heard talk of writing and “programmes” even in relation to the most elementary processes of the living cell). The “liberation” of writing described by Derrida becomes an extremely concrete phenomenon.


On the basis of these premises, Derrida deduces the need for a pure science of writing, which considers writing prior to speech and independently of it: this science is, precisely, “grammatology”; and, to define its aims, it suffices to substitute this term for “semiology”, the term Saussure uses to outline the programme of his famous

Course in General Linguistics

: “We shall call it grammatology… and, as it does not yet exist, we cannot say what it will be; but it has a right to exist, and its place is determined in advance”. The age of speech, which began under the creative power of the verb, is drawing to a close before our very eyes; the character of this new age might be summed up in the following formula: “In the beginning was the written word’’.


Whilst it is true that, from this perspective, linguistics must become a mere branch of grammatology, Derrida seems, however, to overlook the fact that a science already exists which considers language not as speech, but as code and writing; consequently, grammatology itself should necessarily be understood as a sub-branch or a section of that science. This is cybernetics, which, from its beginnings in Wiener’s theories, defined its world as a universe of writing and coding. The very idea of grammatology is already fully contained within the notion of “programme”, one of the key concepts of cybernetics. Etymologically, “programme” —pro-grammer— means “to put the letter (that is,

writing

) first”, whilst “prophecy” means, by contrast, “to put the word first”. Indeed, in the programme assigned to an electronic brain, everything that constitutes the living, phonetic element of language is erased to make way for a system of absolute writing that can be deciphered but not pronounced. It is fair to say that, up to now, our civilisation has known two types of language that have gradually diverged: the language of science is, essentially, written language —code, writing—, whilst the language of poetry and philosophical thought is spoken language —breath, word—. Nevertheless, these two domains—which, for convenience’s sake, we might call the “sphere of the programme” and the “sphere of prophecy”—are drawing ever closer together today thanks to cybernetics; through the mathematisation of human phenomena, cybernetics …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Harassment won’t stop a son’s search for his missing father
content:
Marklen Lariosa, son of missing Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) labor organizer William Lariosa, speaks during a rally in Davao City on the first anniversary of his father’s disappearance on April 10, 2025. Photo by Kath Cortez/Davao Today

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through.”

Is it a mistake for a son to demand justice and accountability?

Marklen, son of disappeared labor organizer William Lariosa, raised this question following the recent incident of harassment and surveillance he experienced. Members of his family were alarmed after two unidentified individuals were looking for his residence on the night of October 25.

He told Bulatlat that this was the first time such an event had happened since his father, a labor organizer under Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao, was abducted in Quezon, Bukidnon, on April 10, 2024.

Marklen could not think of other possible reasons, suspecting that the incident may have something to do with his continuing involvement in campaigns and mobilizations that demand the surfacing of Lariosa. “Is it a mistake for a son to search for his missing father?” he further asked.

Read: After 2 years, son laments continuing disappearance of Mindanao labor organizer

Neighbors of the Lariosa family in their hometown in Davao de Oro province were the ones who encountered the two individuals. They reportedly wore helmets and were on board a black motorcycle, introducing themselves as “collectors” when they were asked.

For Marklen, the response and presence of the two raised suspicions. Aside from the fact that they visited the community around 7 p.m., which is outside the regular working hours, Marklen said that he did not apply for any financial loan.

After the incident, he was concerned for the safety of his family, prompting them to lodge a blotter report with the barangay. However, he stood firm that it won’t stop him from continuing his cause.

Desaparecidos, an organization of families and friends of enforced disappearance victims, denounced the incident, urging the government to put an end to this kind of harassment.

“Family members searching for their disappeared loved ones have to endure threats and harassment from state forces on top of the terrible uncertainty and emotional turmoil they are already going through,” JL Burgos, Desaparecidos chairperson, said in a statement.

Rights groups Karapatan and the Center for Trade Union and Human Rights (CTUHR) also expressed strong condemnations about what happened.

Marklen, a member of the National Board of Desaparecidos, has raised a possibility that the two individuals who recently visited their neighborhood might be connected to those who visited their house several times prior to the disappearance of his father.

He said they were visited by individuals who allegedly introduced themselves as state agents once in 2022 and three times in 2023, accusing Lariosa of being involved in communist insurgency. There were warnings, he added, that they would get dragged into it if they would not cooperate.

The series of visits was reportedly the primary reason why Lariosa was forced to take refuge in Bukidnon. Marklen affirmed that his father, who remains missing, had been a labor organizer.

On July 8, the Supreme Court required certain commanders and elements of Philippine Army units to comment on the petition for review on certiorari filed by the family.

Read: Military ordered to reply to missing Mindanao labor organizer’s case

Since 2024, KMU Southern Mindanao has documented 57 cases of human rights violations against its members and organizers.

The labor group released a statement on October 24, presenting the faces of some individuals, including former high-ranking New People’s Army (NPA) member Roberto Rosete Jr., who allegedly harassed KMU’s leaders and members.

Read: Groups decry surveillance of KMU office in Southern Mindanao

Marklen called for an end to any form of harassment and intimidation against families of the disappeared, pointing out that achieving justice is their only goal. (RVO)

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Peasant organizer persists despite surveillance
content:
Jesus Monasterial. (Photo from Photo from Tanggol Magsasaka-TK)

Repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety.

When he was a university student, he questioned the purpose of agricultural education. Now he is organizing landless farmers and fisherfolk.

Jesus Monasterial has spent more than two years working with rural communities in Southern Tagalog. However, his work resulted in repeated surveillance by state forces, peasant groups said.

On October 31, Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan reported that a police intelligence operative identified as “Bruno” had been asking about Monasterial’s whereabouts in Lian, Batangas. The operative was reportedly previously assigned in Nasugbu.

At the time, Monasterial was assisting a protest camp in Barangay San Diego, where farmers, fisherfolk, and residents opposed the possible demolition of several houses.

“I was on my way back to the people’s protest camp in San Diego when news reached us that someone had been asking about my personal information,” he said.

The camp was established by Samahang Mangangawil 1979 and the San Diego Homeowners’ Association, with support from the Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magbubukid sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK) and Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas–Timog Katagalugan (PAMALAKAYA-TK).

The incident prompted fellow organizers to discuss security measures. They also plan to file a complaint before the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).

Monasterial’s involvement in peasant organizing began at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) where he was enrolled in BS Agricultural Biotechnology.

Coming from a family of farmers in Bicol, where his grandparents worked as agricultural tenants, he became increasingly critical of an agricultural education system that he said served the interests of transnational corporations rather than addressing farmers’ lack of land and government support.

Through the League of Filipino Students–UPLB, he became involved in social issues action and joined community immersions with farmers in Tartaria, Silang, Cavite, as well as Mangyan communities in Mindoro and Dumagat communities in Rizal.

These experiences led him to leave his studies and become a full-time organizer. He now serves as deputy secretary-general of KASAMA-TK.

His work involves staying in communities, conducting consultations and political education, and helping establish local farmers and fisherfolk associations.

“Being a full-time organizer means devoting my entire time to the communities and being far from my loved ones,” he said, adding that he had to set aside his plan to finish college.

The October 31 incident was not the first reported surveillance involving Monasterial.

On July 19, 2026, soldiers from the 16th Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army reportedly sought to identify the organizers of KASAMA-TK’s Regional Peasant Consultation in Barangay Malinis, Lemery, Batangas.

On September 21, a man introducing himself as “Del” Dela Cruz reportedly approached a member of Sugarfolks’ Unity for Genuine Agricultural Reform (SUGAR-Batangas), attempting to persuade the member to leave the organization and provide information about its activities.

According to Tanggol Magsasaka–Timog Katagalugan, the man showed footage of a protest outside the Department of Agriculture regional office led by the Alyansa ng Magsasaka para sa Kumpensasyon (AMK), SUGAR-Batangas, KAISAHAN, and KASAMA-TK. He allegedly warned the member against working with Monasterial, claiming that the organizer was “already drawing attention.”

The protest resulted in a dialogue with government representatives to demand agricultural inputs and implements for farmers and farmworkers affected by successive calamities.

The groups also cited previous incidents in Barangay Casile, Laguna; Lupang Ramos and Tartaria, Cavite; and Coron, Palawan.

Monasterial said that the repeated surveillance restricted his movements and caused anxiety over his family’s safety. “Repeated surveillance limits my movements as an organizer and makes me fear returning home to my family because they might also be targeted by the state due to my advocacy.”

Despite the threats, Monasterial said that his work remains rooted in the struggles of farmers and farmworkers.

In Batangas, he witnessed sugarcane cutters and loaders receiving only P350 to P400 for every ton of cane harvested and loaded onto trucks. Their wages are paid at the …

author: dev
title: Habiter au corps d'un âne mort ou le chemin de Nietzsche
content:
Dans la continuité des très nombreux articles que nous avons publiés afin de déchiffrer l'Intelligence artificielle, le monde qu'elle avale, celui qu'elle charrie et celui qu'elle produit, nous partageons cette semaine l'épatante découverte d'Olivier Chiran et Pierre Muzin. La première occurrence de l'expression IA reviendrait au célèbre philosophe Friedrich Nietzsche dans le tout aussi célèbre

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

, un tiret séparait néanmoins les deux voyelles :

« Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit. »


« Donnez-moi du travail, de la fatigue,


de la douleur et de l'enthousiasme. »


George Sand


1.


Pour savoir précisément où nous en sommes, mais aussi faire face à ce qui nous arrive, alors que l'intelligence artificielle étend son emprise sur le monde et les vies, nous avons besoin d'un sémaphore.


2.


On dit que l'expression « intelligence artificielle » a été lancée par John McCarthy, en 1956, lors de la conférence de Dartmouth, coup d'envoi du programme de recherche consacré à la reproduction algorithmique de la pensée humaine. Soixante-douze ans plus tôt, en 1884, Friedrich Nietzsche, le célèbre philosophe allemand, rédige son grand poème philosophique :

Ainsi parlait Zarathoustra

. Dans la troisième partie de cet ouvrage (trouvée « sous le ciel alcyonien de Nice », dira-t-il), il écrit : « Braire à tout propos I-A, c'est ce qu'apprennent les ânes et ceux qui en ont l'esprit

 [

1

]

. » Première apparition de ces deux lettres, longtemps avant Dartmouth. Évidence de leur rapprochement – en même temps que, d'un simple tiret, de leur mise à distance. On pourrait s'étonner que les traducteurs français (Henri Albert en 1903, Geneviève Bianquis en 1969) aient fait le choix, au lieu du « hi-han » conventionnel, de les conserver telles quelles. Mais le texte allemand dit bien : «

Immer I-A sagen – das lernte allein der Esel, und wer seines Geistes ist

 ! » – Nietzche ayant délibérément fait tomber le

h

 de «

iah

 », braiment de l'âne dans la langue de Goethe. Nous dirons donc, quant à nous, que l'histoire de l'I-A commence à la fin du xixe siècle, lorsqu'un philosophe visionnaire, cheminant à flanc de montagne, a compris qu'on pouvait arracher au cri de l'âne sa puissance d'exclamation intempestive – et qu'il y avait là, pour nous, un grand danger

 [

2

]

.


3.


C'est qu'il y a deux ânes. Gilles Deleuze, commentant les propos de Nietzsche : « On aurait pu croire que l'âne, l'animal qui dit I-A, était l'animal dionysiaque par excellence. En fait, il n'en est rien ; son apparence est dionysiaque, mais toute sa réalité est chrétienne

 [

3

]

. » Le braiment sans son ou ses

h

, c'est cette manière qu'a l'âne de dire toujours oui – mais un faux oui, une fausse affirmation qui ne sait pas dire non, qui ne sait qu'acquiescer face à ce qui est. Bêtise. Démission de la pensée. Obscurantisme. Post-vérité. Positivisme logique. (Margaret Thatcher : «

There is no alternative

 » → TINA : « I-A ! I-A ! ») Toutes choses contre lesquelles, justement, la philosophie s'évertue à lutter. « Le réel tel qu'il est, conclut Deleuze, c'est une idée d'âne. »


4.


Il arrive aussi, on le sait, que l'âne se cabre. L'I-A approbatif que dénoncent les philosophes est la forme mutilée de ce « hi-han ! » qui est à la fois refus catégorique et cri pour l'autonomie et la liberté. Entre les deux, il y a toute la différence entre l'âne vivant (dionysiaque) et l'âne mort (chrétien) – entre l'appel à la révolte et le bourdon béat de la fanfare. (« Si l'âne contribue peu à l'harmonie durant sa vie, écrivait-on au milieu du xixe siècle, il la sert généreusement après sa mort, lui fournissant les meilleures peaux qui existent pour les grosses caisses et les meilleurs tibias pour fabriquer des clarinettes

 [

4

]

. »)


5.


Dans

L'Âne

, de Lucius de Patras, le narrateur voit une magicienne se transformer en oiseau après s'être frotté le corps avec un onguent

 [

5

]

. Ayant voulu l'imiter, il se retrouve, quant à lui, métamorphosé en âne. Séquestré par une bande de brigands, il tente de leur échapper en emportant avec lui, dans sa fuite, une jeune prisonnière. Par malchance, les brigands retrouvent les fuyard

·

e

·

s, les renvoient à leur geôle et imaginent comment les punir avec toute la sévérité requise. « Écoutez une rare et nouvelle invention, qui vous plaira, ou je me trompe fort, dit l'un d'eux à ses comparses ; l'âne doit mourir, c'est la justice …

author: Bahar Sheikh
title: Lieblingsstreberin: Paula Saunders
content:
In der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ gerät Tatiana Maslany als geschiedene Mutter in einen Scam aus Cybersex, Erpressung und Verschwörung.

Geschiedene Soccer Mom, gewissenhafte Fact-Checkerin, falsch Verdächtigte? Paula Saunders (Tatiana Maslany), Protagonistin der Apple-TV-Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“, lässt sich auf kein Label festlegen. Sie jongliert mit einem Sorgerechtsstreit und einem schlecht bezahlten Medien-Vollzeitjob – worüber sie sich beim Online-Sexarbeiter Trevor ausheult, der ihr empathisch zuhört, solange sie ihn bezahlt. Bis Trevor plötzlich bei ihrer Camsex-Session entführt wird. Kurze Zeit später kriegt sie einen Anruf, dass sie 15.000 Dollar zahlen soll, um ihn freizukaufen. Von der Polizei wird sie mit dem Hinweis, dass das sicher Betrug ist, abgewimmelt. Als sie nicht zahlt, wird sie mit Cybersex-Aufnahmen erpresst. Da das Sorgerecht für ihre Tochter auf dem Spiel steht, nimmt sie die Sache selbst in die Hand und spürt anhand von ein paar wackeligen Screenshots und einer Überweisung die Erpresser*innen auf. Sie beherrscht alle Techniken der Open-Source-Recherche, ist kreativ und fokussiert, wenn es darum geht, die Fakten herauszufinden. Bis die Frage aufkommt: Wer sind eigentlich die Scammer hinter Trevor? Während die Darstellung von Online-Sexarbeiter*innen als „Scammer“ klischeehaft ausfällt, finden sich alle menschlichen Ambivalenzen in Paulas Charakter wieder, was sicher auch Tatiana Maslanys schauspielerischem Können zu verdanken ist. Paula wird von einer Mischung aus Erpressung, Gewalt und Tatendrang weiter in den Scam hineingezogen, bis sie der ziemlich nutzlosen Polizei immer verdächtiger erscheint. Dabei will Paula nach eigenen Angaben nur eine gute Mutter sein und legt sich dafür regelmäßig mit ihrem Ex-Mann Karl (Jake Johnson) an. Neben all dem coacht sie die Fußballmannschaft ihrer Tochter bis zum Gewinn und scheint immer kurz vor einer Beförderung zu stehen. Wenn sie nur ihre Unschuld beweisen und die große Verschwörung aufdecken könnte, die sie in die Situation gebracht hat … Die Serie „Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed“ ist auf Apple TV verfügbar, eine zweite Staffel ist geplant. author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

ABD Savunma Bakanlığı (Pentagon) yetkilisi Arthur Miller, ABD'nin İran'la savaşının maliyetinin 13 Kasım itibarıyla 48,3 milyar dolara ulaştığını açıkladı.

ABD Senatosu Silahlı Hizmetler Komitesi'ndeki oturuma katılan Donanma Müsteşar Yardımcısı adayı ve Pentagon'un mali kontrolör yardımcısı Miller, açıkladığı rakamın mühimmat harcamaları, teçhizat yenileme maliyetleri ve operasyon giderlerini içerdiğini kaydetti.

Öte yandan Miller, Senatör Richard Blumenthal'ın sorularına yanıt olarak söz konusu rakamın, İran'ın saldırıları sonucu hasar gören Ortadoğu'daki ABD tesislerinin onarım maliyetlerini içermediğini belirtti.

author: Gabriel Aguirre
title: Work For Peace, In Berlin / Trabajos por la Paz en Berlín
content:
Culture of Peace, Europe, Latin America, South America

By Gabriel Aguirre, World BEYOND War, November 19, 2026

Berlin has historically been a city where peace occupies a central place in the public discourse of its inhabitants. The historical events—from the Second World War to the fall of the Berlin Wall—speak for themselves.

For this and other reasons, organizations such as the International Peace Bureau (IPB) have their headquarters there—a space that has served to promote the vision of a different kind of world. During the second week of October, Gabriel Aguirre, the Latin America organizer for World BEYOND War (WBW), had the opportunity to visit these offices as part of a working tour that included several European countries.

During the visit, meetings were held with the International Peace Bureau team, alongside discussions and interviews with various organizations within the German peace movement. The situation in Latin America and its processes of resistance sparked great interest among the participants. Furthermore, the two organizations discussed joint projects currently underway between World BEYOND War and the IPB—most notably the Peace Wave, an initiative that has established itself in recent years as a key platform for the mobilization and coordination of peace advocates worldwide.

Naturally, a stay in the German capital would not be complete without a visit to the Anti-War Café (*Anti-Kriegs-Café*), located near the bustling Alexanderplatz area. It is a must-visit spot for anyone in Berlin who speaks out against war. There, visitors are welcomed by Heinrich, the coordinator of the WBW Berlin chapter—a man who has long been deeply active in, and supportive of, various global struggles for peace. Beyond enjoying a German beer, visitors can learn about historical instances of solidarity and anti-war activism from around the world.

Gabriel Aguirre, Un Mundo Más Allá de la Guerra, 19 de noviembre de 2026

Berlín ha sido históricamente una ciudad donde la paz ocupa un lugar central en el debate público de sus habitantes. Los acontecimientos históricos hablan por sí solos, desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial hasta la caída del Muro de Berlín.

Por este y otros motivos, organizaciones como el Buró Internacional de la Paz (IPB, por sus siglas en inglés) tienen allí su sede central, un espacio que ha servido para proyectar la idea de un mundo diferente. Durante la segunda semana de octubre, el organizador para América Latina de World BEYOND War (WBW), Gabriel Aguirre, tuvo la oportunidad de visitar estas oficinas en el marco de una gira de trabajo que incluyó varios países de Europa.

Durante la visita, se llevaron a cabo reuniones con el equipo del Buró Internacional de la Paz, así como encuentros y entrevistas con diversas organizaciones del movimiento pacifista en Alemania. La situación de América Latina y sus procesos de resistencia despertaron un gran interés entre los participantes. Asimismo, se abordaron proyectos conjuntos que actualmente se desarrollan entre World BEYOND War y el IPB, entre los que destaca la V Ola de la Paz, una iniciativa que en los últimos años se ha consolidado como un espacio clave de movilización y articulación para los defensores de la paz en todo el mundo.

Por supuesto, la estadía en la capital alemana exigía visitar el Café Antibélico (Anti-Kriegs-Café), ubicado en las cercanías de la concurrida zona de Alexanderplatz. Es un lugar de parada obligatoria para quienes visitan Berlín y alzan su voz contra la guerra. Allí los visitantes son recibidos por Heinrich, coordinador del capítulo de WBW en Berlín, quien durante muchos años se ha mantenido muy activo y solidario con las distintas luchas globales por la paz, donde además de tomarte una cerveza alemana, podrás aprender sobre las experiencias históricas de solidaridad y contra la guerra en el mundo.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
content:
We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary

Birds of War

, which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the

BBC

, and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence.


The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions.


“Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.”


Birds of War

 premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

Dennoch ist es vor allem die Juso, die medial in Erscheinung tritt; sie war es auch, die im Sommer auf nationaler Ebene entschied, sich dem internationalen Aufruf zu einem «Youth Strike» in ganz Europa anzuschliessen.
