author: Unknown
title: Carl Ahlteen - Josef Hillström
content:
Författare

: Carl Ahlteen

Titel

: Josef Hillström

Undertitel

: (1 års minne)

Källa

: Allarm november 1916


 Ett år har nu gått till ända sedan den tiden då vi ännu hade vår präktige kamrat i livet.


 Vi alla, som i fjor i slutet av oktober och b örjan av november månad tillhörde organisationen, minns allt för väl med vilken spänning vi emotsågo den dagen då Hillström skulle återfå friheten.


 Få av oss kunde trots allt tro att den

kristna statsliga

 mordlusten skulle ta ett sådant uttryck som detta: mörda en människa, endast därför att hans hjärta klappade för proletariatets frigörelse. Han, denne präktige kamrat anklagades för mord av en f. d. polisman, handlare, där tyckte man sig finna bevis nog. Hur hade det varit om det endast hade varit en handlande, ej en f. d. polisman? Å på det sätt den kristna staten gick tillväga mot Josef Hillström kunde de utan vidare anklaga en som fanns i New York eller någon annan avlägsen stad, för brottet i Salt Lake, Utah. Man behövde ej det ringaste bevis i fallet Josef Hillström därför skulle det givetvis ej behövas i det andra fallet heller.


 En sak var det som var nog: Josef Hillström diktade arbetarsånger av sådan art att gamla och unga rycktes med för dess känslighet och sanningsrika manande innehåll.


 Hade Hillström diktat kristna sånger, hade han levat den dag som i dag är, och varit omgjordad med lyx och överflöd. Hade Bruno ljugit lika fräckt som de kristna prästerna i Rom hade han ej blivit bränd på bål.


..Å du förbannade kristna rättvisa, du mördar ädla män och sanningssökare. Hitintills har du undgått straffet, men det väntar dig! Lederna tätna!


 Den kristna fräcka råheten har förmått att hålla sig vid liv en rätt lång tid, men den tidens längd som återstår är nog snart räknad. Över hela jorden höres hoten av starka män, och lederna tätna. Det bådar domsdagar för förtrycket.


 Strax efter Hillströms häktning erhöll jag brev från honom vart han omtalade hur det kom sig att han var i fängelset. Han själv ansåg det hela som en komedi, och kunde givetvis aldrig tro att man i en tidsålder som denna kunde begå ett sådant brott mot honom som blev gjort.


 Regelbundet hade jag brev och vykort från honom, och regelbundet sände jag honom tidningar, vilka han fick mottaga ända tills i juni månad 1915. Han bad mig då sända dem till en kvinnlig kamrat som personligen gav honom dem. Inom kort blev detta också omöjligt.


 Hela tiden hade vår präktige kamrat hoppet framme, alltid framhöll han att snart skola de väl i alla fall inse sitt brott mot mig och frigiva mig. Efter möjligheterna att få läsa böcker och tidningar blevo stängda, förstod vår kamrat vad saken gällde, han förstod att det kristna packet ej kunde tillfredsställas med mindre än att se hans huvud på ett fat.


 Han förstod att endast en räddning återstod för honom, det var att massorna organiserade sig och ryckte honom ur mördarhordens händer. Rättvisan genom borgarnas lag trodde han berättigat nog ej mera på.


 Över hela Amerika hölls "Joe Hill" möten, över hela Amerika talade man sympatiskt, och i form av kontanter lade man sin tribut. Man gjorde allt man kunde sade man.


 Ja man gjorde allt man kunde fredligt - vad som var tillåtet av Hillströms mördare - men var det nog? Tänk än en gång efter arbetare om det var nog. Vi ha tre kamrater nu sittande väntande på samma som "Joe Hill" kamraterna på "Messeba Range". Skall man även i detta fall hålla sig inom ramen av borgarnas lag? Skall man efter den blodiga rättvisan fullbordat sitt verk med dem säga: vi gjorde allt vi kunde.

vad är rätt för borgaren och borgarens stat?


Jo! att fylla sitt eget behov, göra vad som passar deras intresse. Om detta blir gjort inom eller utom ramen av den s. k. rättvisan, eller med eller mot slavarnas vilja bekymrar ej dem det minsta. Slavarna de måste innan de handla ha reda på om det är rätt, och i sin stora enfald gå de till sina dödssvurne fiender och fråga om det är rätt.


Idiotiskt handlingssätt, utfört av slavar och viljelösa, och av dem endast.


 Borgarna ha, på grund av slavarnas feghet

makt

 och detta är nog för dem att få rätt.


 Slavarna uraktläto att organisera sig och med makt uttaga Hillström.

Den 19 november kom, och hydran frossade av det unga, flytande, varma, kamratblodet.

 Några minuters blodflöde och hon var tillfredsställd. Han låg där nu dödad denne vår präktige kamrat. Hans ädla hjärta hade upphört att slå, hans hand kunde ej mera föra den penna som på en kort tid sände ut så många …

author: rezgar2
title: نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات
content:
إن المعركة حول التكنولوجيا هي أيضاً معركة حول الملكية والسلطة والوعي ومستقبل البشرية. ومع اتساع دور الفضاء الرقمي بوصفه إحدى الساحات الرئيسية للصراع الطبقي، يمكن للأممية اليسارية الرقمية أن تصبح نقطة انطلاق لتجديد العمل الأممي عموماً. ويتمثل التحدي اليوم في البناء على التشخيص بأدوات جماعية للمواجهة، وفي تطوير التعاون العملي القائم بين قوى اليسار وتوسيعه، ليكمل المواقف والبيانات التضامنية بعمل مشترك أكثر تنظيماً واستمرارية، وفي التوجه التدريجي من منصات الاحتكارات إلى بدائل مستقلة وديمقراطية. وبذلك يمكن أن تتحول إمكانات الثورة الرقمية من امتياز تستأثر به حفنة من الشركات والدول الكبرى إلى مكسب عام يخدم الإنسان وتحرره.

صدر حديثاً كتاب «نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات» نصوص ودراسات وبرنامج عمل حول اليسار الرقمي والأممية اليسارية الرقمية، من إعدادي وتأليفي، وهو متاح إلكترونياً ومجاناً.

يشهد العالم ثورة رقمية متسارعة تعيد تشكيل الاقتصاد والعمل والسياسة والوعي الإنساني. وفي الوقت الذي تفتح فيه هذه الثورة إمكانات هائلة للتقدم والتحرر البشري وتجاوز الفقر والأمراض، تتركز ملكية أدواتها ومواردها الأساسية في أيدي حفنة من الاحتكارات الرأسمالية المدعومة من الدول الكبرى. وفي المقابل، تتسع الاحتجاجات الجماهيرية والشبابية في كثير من بلدان العالم، مستفيدة من الأدوات الرقمية في التنظيم والتعبئة، ومؤكدة أن الظروف الموضوعية لتجاوز الرأسمالية قائمة.

ومن هذا التناقض تنبع الحاجة إلى مسار متكامل يبدأ بفهم الرأسمالية الرقمية، ويمر بإغناء تجربة اليسار فكرياً وتنظيمياً بما يواكب التطورات الراهنة، وصولاً إلى بناء أممية يسارية رقمية قادرة على التأثير.

تتيح الثورة الرقمية تقليص ساعات العمل، وتطوير الخدمات الصحية والتعليمية، وتحرير الإنسان من الأعمال المرهقة والمتكررة. غير أن هذه الإمكانات تتطور في إطار علاقات إنتاج رأسمالية، تستحوذ فيها الاحتكارات على القسم الأكبر من مكاسب التقدم التكنولوجي.

فالخوارزميات والمنصات الرقمية ليست محايدة اجتماعياً أو طبقياً، إذ تتأثر بعلاقات الملكية والتمويل والإدارة. وتتجاوز هذه الهيمنة حدود الاقتصاد إلى تشكيل الوعي وتوسيع المراقبة وتوظيف التكنولوجيا في القتل والحروب، ويزيد تقارب بعض قوى اليمين المتطرف مع الاحتكارات التكنولوجية من مخاطر الفاشية الرقمية.

وأمام هذا الواقع، يبرز السؤال الجوهري: كيف يقاوم اليسار الرأسمالية في طورها الرقمي المتقدم، ويفتح الطريق نحو بديل اشتراكي إنساني أكثر عدلاً، محلياً وعالمياً؟ وكيف يجدد نفسه ويطورها ليكون قادراً على ذلك؟

فقد أصبحت الرأسمالية الرقمية قوة عابرة للحدود، بينما يبقى جزء كبير من العمل اليساري الرقمي محصوراً داخل الأطر الوطنية، ويعاني ضعف التنسيق الرقمي الأممي. وتكشف التجارب الحديثة حجم الخطر الذي يواجهه اليسار في هذا الميدان.

ففي البرازيل، وخلال سباق رئاسي بالغ التقارب عام 2026 بين لولا دا سيلفا ومرشح اليمين المتطرف فلافيو بولسونارو، اتهم لولا وحزبه شركة ميتا بتقليص انتشار منشوراته لمصلحة خصمه. وتدخلت المحكمة الانتخابية العليا وألزمت الشركة بتقديم توضيحات، ونشرت صحيفة «فولها دي ساو باولو» مراسلات داخلية يقر فيها موظفون في الشركة بأن قيود المنصة أضرت بحسابات لولا، فيما تحدثت ميتا عن «أعطال تقنية». ورغم ذلك، حسمت التعبئة الجماهيرية جولة الإعادة لصالح لولا.

وفي ألمانيا، وظّف إيلون ماسك منصته «إكس» لدعم حزب «البديل من أجل ألمانيا» اليميني المتطرف قبيل انتخابات فبراير 2025، عبر مقالات التأييد وبثّ حوار مباشر مع زعيمته أليس فايدل، فيما رصدت دراسات انحياز خوارزميات المنصة لصالح محتوى الحزب. وفي كولومبيا، وبعد جولة إعادة حسمت لمرشح اليمين المتطرف بفارق نحو نقطة مئوية واحدة، اتهم الرئيس غوستافو بيترو شركة سايبر إسرائيلية بنشر نصف مليون حساب آلي زائف للتلاعب بالناخبين، وطعن في سلامة برمجيات الفرز وانحياز المنصات الرقمية لليمين المتطرف. ومهما انتهى إليه التحقيق، فإن انتقال الطعن في انتخابات بلد بأكمله إلى ميدان الخوارزميات والحسابات الآلية يكشف طبيعة المرحلة التي نعيشها.

أما المثال الأوضح فجاء من المحكمة الجنائية الدولية. فبعد أن أصدر قضاتها مذكرات توقيف بحق مسؤولين إسرائيليين بتهم ارتكاب جرائم حرب في غزة، فرضت الإدارة الأمريكية عقوبات على عدد من قضاتها ومسؤوليها، فأغلقت شركات أمريكية حساباتهم المصرفية والرقمية. وإذا كانت الرأسمالية مستعدة لفعل ذلك بمحكمة دولية تضم أكثر من مئة وعشرين دولة عضواً، فماذا ستفعل بمشروع يساري يصبح مؤثراً ويسعى إلى كسر هيمنتها، ويتجاوز الخطوط الحمراء التي رسمتها؟

وتمتد هذه الهيمنة إلى الحياة اليومية للناشطات والناشطين، عبر عقوبات رقمية تفرضها المنصات على من يفضح جرائم الحرب الإسرائيلية وانتهاكات دول أخرى، أو يطرح خطاباً يسارياً جذرياً. وتبدأ هذه العقوبات بالتضييق وتقليص الانتشار والتهميش، وتصل إلى حذف المحتوى وإغلاق الحسابات. وقد وثقت منظمات حقوق الإنسان الدولية هذه الممارسات وأدانتها، ومنها تقرير «هيومن رايتس ووتش» عن الرقابة الممنهجة على المحتوى الفلسطيني في منصات ميتا. ويدفع هذا القمع الرقمي كثيراً من الناشطات والناشطين إلى رقابة ذاتية طوعية، فيعدلون خطابهم ويتجنبون قضايا بعينها خوفاً من الحظر …

OLIVIER BESANCENOT ET MICHAËL LÖWY ont publié un ouvrage intitulé Affinités révolutionnaires, Nos étoiles rouges et noires, qui entend mettre en relief les « alliances et solidarités agissantes entre les deux mouvements ». Les deux auteurs veulent, disent-ils, « éclairer ce versant ignoré, souvent délibérément, qui révèle la fraternité de leurs combats ». Cela me paraît une excellente idée[1].

Le présent ouvrage n’est cependant pas à strictement parler une réponse à Affinités révolutionnaires : en effet, le mode d’exposition de leurs idées choisi par Besancenot & Löwy, au moins dans la partie historique, ne permet pas de répondre, parce que leur argumentation est trop allusive et vague, fondée sur un exposé extrêmement approximatif des faits. C’est pourquoi, plutôt que de répondre, j’ai simplement choisi d’aborder les mêmes faits, les mêmes questions, mais à notre manière : le lecteur se fera lui-même une idée.

Il peut déjà se faire une idée de la conception qu’ont Besancenot & Löwy des « affinités révolutionnaires » en constatant la présence d’un portrait pleine page de Marx, mais aucun portrait de Proudhon, Bakounine, Kropotkine.

author: Unknown
title: Bir yarış oyunundan kültürel fenomene: Grand Theft Auto'nun ortaya çıkış hikâyesi
content:
Video oyunları dünyasının en çok beklenen yapımlarından Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), 13 yıllık bekleyişin, ertelemelerin ve sızıntıların ardından oyuncularla buluştu.

Bugün milyonlarca insanın merakla beklediği serinin temelleri, 1997 yılında İskoçya'nın Dundee kentinde, DMA Design adlı görece küçük bir oyun stüdyosunda atılmıştı.

Bulmaca oyunu Lemmings ile başarı kazanan stüdyo, başlangıçta Race'n'Chase adını taşıyan bir yarış oyunu geliştirmeyi planlıyordu. Ancak ekibin geleneksel yarış oyunlarından farklı bir deneyim yaratma arayışı, video oyunları tarihini değiştirecek bir fikrin ortaya çıkmasını sağladı.

Serinin yaratıcılarından Dave Jones, dönemin oyunlarından farklılaşmak için geliştirdikleri en önemli özelliğin, oyuncuların kullandıkları otomobillerden inebilmesi olduğunu anlatıyor.

Oyuncuların araç değiştirebilmesi, otomobil çalabilmesi ve şehirde yaya olarak dolaşabilmesi, farklı oyun türlerinin bir araya gelmesine olanak tanıdı.

Geliştirme ekibi başlangıçta oyuncuların hem suçlu hem de polis memuru olarak oynayabileceği bir oyun tasarlamıştı. Ancak polis karakterini yönetmenin oyunculara getireceği kurallar ve sınırlamalar nedeniyle bu fikirden vazgeçildi.

Jones, o dönemde aldıkları kararı, "Bir noktada, 'Biliyor musunuz, kötü adamı oynamak çok daha eğlenceli' dedik, bu yüzden oyunun konusu da bu oldu" sözleriyle anlatıyor.

İlk GTA'nın satışları, stüdyonun önceki başarısı Lemmings'e kıyasla yavaş ilerledi. Jones'a göre bunun nedenlerinden biri, oyunun sunduğu yeniliklerin ancak oynandığında anlaşılabilmesiydi.

İlk oyunun senaryosunu yazan ve tanıtımından sorumlu olan Brian Baglow ise oyunun yıl boyunca satışlarını sürdürdüğünü, oyuncuların birbirlerine tavsiye etmesiyle giderek daha geniş bir kitleye ulaştığını belirtiyor.

Suç ve şiddet temaları nedeniyle İngiltere Parlamentosunda da tartışma konusu olan GTA'nın yasaklanması yönünde çağrılar yapıldı. Oyunun yayıncısı BMG Interactive'in bu tartışmaları bir pazarlama stratejisi olarak kullandığı daha sonra ortaya çıktı.

Kuşbakışı kamera açısı ve iki boyutlu grafikleriyle bugünkü GTA oyunlarından oldukça farklı görünen ilk yapım, serinin kendine özgü mizah anlayışının da temellerini attı.

The Guardian'ın video oyunları editörü Keza MacDonald'a göre GTA'nın Amerikan şehirlerini abartılı biçimde tasvir etmesinde, geliştiricilerinin İskoçya'dan gelen gözlem gücünün önemli bir payı vardı.

MacDonald, "Bu son derece hiciv dolu bir oyun. ABD'nin aşırı bireyci ve aşırı kapitalist yapısını doğrudan hedef alıyor" diyor.

İlk oyunun sınırlı bütçesi ve gerçek markaların lisanslarını kullanmanın maliyeti, geliştiricileri kurgusal markalar yaratmaya yöneltti. Hayali radyo istasyonları, reklamlar ve işletme isimleri zamanla serinin karakteristik özellikleri arasına girdi.

Başlangıçta ekonomik zorunluluklardan doğan bu tercihler, oyuncuların içinde bulunduğu şehrin kendine ait bir kültürü ve gündelik hayatı olduğu hissini güçlendirdi.

Baglow, yaklaşık 30 yıl sonra ilk oyuna ilişkin en fazla gurur duyduğu özelliğin bu kurgusal dünyanın inşası olduğunu söylüyor.

2013 yılında piyasaya sürülen GTA 5, üç gün içinde 1 milyar dolar gelir elde ederek eğlence sektöründe o güne kadarki en hızlı gelir elde eden ürün oldu.

Serinin etkisi yıllar içinde video oyunlarının sınırlarını da aştı. GTA'nın adı sinema filmlerinde ve gündelik konuşmalarda kullanılan bir kültürel referansa dönüştü.

MacDonald, serinin ilk dönemlerinde sinemadan yoğun biçimde beslendiğini, bugün ise sinemanın GTA'dan ne ölçüde etkilendiğinin tartışıldığını belirtiyor.

Jones'a göre serinin bu kadar geniş bir kitleye ulaşmasının nedenlerinden biri, oyuncuların aşina oldukları bir dünyada geçmesi. Fantastik veya bilim kurgu evrenlerinin aksine GTA, oyunculardan yeni bir dünyanın kurallarını öğrenmelerini beklemiyor.

Serinin yeni oyununun hem kapsam hem de gelir bakımından GTA 5'i geride bırakması bekleniyor.

PlayStation ve Xbox, GTA 6'nın kendi dijital mağazalarının tarihinde en fazla ön sipariş verilen oyun olduğunu açıkladı. Oyunun 212 gigabaytlık boyutunun da oyuncuların ön sipariş vererek indirme işlemini önceden tamamlamak istemelerinde etkili olduğu değerlendiriliyor.

Oyuna yönelik ilgi, reklam kampanyalarıyla şehirlerin gündelik hayatına da taşındı. Londra'daki Selfridges mağazasında oyunun kurgusal şehri Vice City temalı bir alan oluşturulurken Miami'de GTA evrenindeki hayali markaların reklamları yayımlandı.

Video oyunları sektörüne yeni bir ekonomik ivme kazandırması beklenen GTA 6'nın …

title: Gram altın 6 bin liranın altına geriledi
content:
Küresel piyasalardaki gelişmeler ve ABD merkezli makroekonomik beklentiler, altın fiyatlarında sert düşüşe yol açtı. Ons altın son günlerde yaşadığı kayıplarla 14 ayın en düşük seviyesine inerken, gram altın da kritik eşik olan 6 bin liranın altına geriledi.

20 Kasım işlemlerinde 3.550 dolara kadar inen ons altın, bugün TSİ 07.26 itibarıyla 3 bin 532 dolar seviyesinde işlem gördü. Gram altın ise 5 bin 716 liraya kadar geriledikten sonra sabah seansında TSİ 07.26 itibarıyla 5 bin 735 lira bandında hareket etti.

Altın fiyatları üzerindeki baskıda doların güçlenmesi belirleyici unsurlar arasında yer aldı. Dolar endeksinin 104 seviyesine dayanması, dolar cinsinden fiyatlanan altını diğer para birimlerini kullanan yatırımcılar açısından daha pahalı hale getirerek uluslararası talebi zayıflattı.

Düşüşte, ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) aralık ayında faiz artıracağı yönündeki beklentiler ve Fed cephesinden gelen "daha sıkı adımların gerekebileceğine" dair mesajlar etkili oldu. Öte yandan ABD tahvil piyasasında yükselen getiriler de altının cazibesini azalttı; ABD'nin 10 yıllık tahvil getirisi yüzde 5'in üzerinde seyrederken, 10 yıllık enflasyondan arındırılmış reel getiri yüzde 2,85-2,90 bandına dayandı. Getirisi bulunmayan altın karşısında tahvillerin öne çıkması, değerli metal üzerindeki satış baskısını artırdı.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Groups decry abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist in Davao City
content:
Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas answers questions from members of the media during a candle-lighting activity at Freedom Park in Davao City on the 2nd death anniversary of New Bataan 5 on February 24, 2024. Photo from Panalipdan Youth Davao’s Facebook page

Progressive groups condemned the alleged abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas in Davao City.

The Hands Off Mindanao Youth Activists (HOMYA) Network reported that around 10 to 12 individuals wearing all-black clothing and caps allegedly pursued the 24-year-old youth activist along Upper Madapo Hills, Barangay 8-A, on November 17 while he was on his way home.

“[They] tried to corner him and said, ‘This is him. Do not run’,” the network stated in its alert released on November 19.

Pangadas who belongs to the Indigenous Manobo reportedly was able to escape. He lost his phone and slippers and sustained injuries after he tripped and fell down during the pursuit which reportedly lasted for three hours.

The HOMYA network said that this incident reflects the continuing attacks and harassment faced by activists. “These acts of intimidation inflict serious mental, emotional, and psychological distress not only on Mawing, the direct target of these fascist attacks, but also on his family and loved ones who are forced to live under constant fear and anxiety.”

Read: Groups slam PNP official’s apology after tagging Mindanao activists as ‘wanted persons’

Lara Felescoso, spokesperson for Resist! Campaign, a human rights advocacy initiative, also considered the abduction attempt as an attack against Lumad youth and Indigenous community members who fight for their ancestral lands and fundamental rights.

Pangadas, who hails in Talaingod, Davao del Norte, was a former student of the Salugpongan Ta Tanu Igkanogon Community Learning Center, a now-defunct alternative school teaching Indigenous children in the Davao region. He was a relative of the late Manobo leader Bai Bibyaon Ligkayan Bigkay.

Fifty-five Salugpongan schools across the region were shut down in 2019 for allegedly violating Department of Education (DepEd) regulations and for training children to become members of the New People’s Army (NPA), an accusation that has been debunked by the school administration and human rights organizations.

Read: Groups urge gov’t to prioritize reopening of Lumad schools in Mindanao

During a protest in Davao City for the State of the Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in 2022, Pangadas and his older brother Ismael were arrested by the police and faced criminal charges for alleged human trafficking. They were acquitted from these cases.

Read: Court acquits Lumad brothers, 3 teachers from human trafficking charges

Pangadas serves as the education and research officer of the environmental advocacy group Panalipdan Youth Davao and convenor of HOMYA, a network that has been established due to continuing attacks and harassment against activists in Mindanao.

With such circumstances, the HOMYA network did not rule out the possibility that the alleged abduction attempt might be state-perpetrated, raising suspicion that it is linked to the government’s counterinsurgency operations.

Various progressive groups and youth-led organizations demanded an immediate and impartial investigation to identify the perpetrators and hold them accountable. (DAA)

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Lakbayan Southern Tagalog children finally released
content:
Released Lakbayani children. (Photo from Salinlahi Facebook page)

The children were denied their rights to counsel.

The 15 minors arrested in barangay Sucat, Muntinlupa City on November 15 have been released four days later (November 19).

This follows the order issued by the Muntinlupa City Office of the Prosecutor on November 18 for the release of all those arrested.

The minors aged 14 to 17 were part of the Lakbayan Southern Tagalog that started their march from the University of the Philippines Los Baños on November 12 to join the protest on the arrival of US President Donald Trump.

The 15 minors were the last to be released from being held in Bahay Pag-asa in Muntinlupa City. There were a total of 20 minors among the participants of Lakbayan Southern Tagalog, who were arrested on November 15 during the police’s violent dispersal in barangay Sucat.

The five minors aged 15 below were already released on November 17 as they were found to have no criminal liability.

The more than 200 adults who were part of the Lakbayan were earlier released on the night of November 18.

This contradicted the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) claim on November 18, that all 236 delegates of Southern Tagalog were released. The 15 minors were only released in the afternoon of November 19.

“Despite days of delaying tactics and bureaucratic processes that kept the minors detained for four days after illegal arrest and parents waiting in distress – returning everyday and waiting outside overnight – with the pressure of child rights advocates, lawyers, and church organizations, the children are now free,” Salinlahi Alliance for Children’s Concerns said.

“As we celebrate this collective victory, we also continue to demand for the immediate release of the nine illegally arrested and detained protesters at the Liwasang Bonifacio last November 15. One of them is a minor and currently remains at the Manila Youth Reception Center (MYRC),” the group said in their social media page.

According to Salinlahi, the children were denied their rights to counsel as the Bahay Pag-asa Head blocked the lawyers and paralegals from talking to them.

Salinlahi stressed that these children suffered police brutality and their longer detention only makes their violations of their rights extend much further.

“Bahay Pag-asa is mandated to protect and rehabilitate children—not become an instrument for prolonging their detention and suppressing their rights,” Salinlahi said in a statement.

For the National Union of People’s Lawyer (NUPL) the Philippine National Police (PNP) must be held accountable for their brutality against activists who are only exercising their right to protest. “These findings expose the fundamental weakness of the PNP’s case. Having arrested and charged hundreds of individuals in one sweeping operation, the police could not even sufficiently distinguish the alleged acts of one respondent from another.”

Meanwhile, three students of the University of Makati (UMak) were also released on November 19.

The Taguig City Prosecutor’s Office dismissed the cases that were filed against the students. These are alarm and scandal under Article 155 of the Revised Penal Code and resistance and disobedience to an agent of a person in authority under Article 151 of the same code.

The Taguig City Prosecutor’s Office said in its resolution, “The evidence on record shows that the actions of (three students), were made specifically to voice out certain political and social grievances and not the purpose of causing general disturbance or public disorder.”

Lawyer Jose Topacio of the Alliance of Nationalist and Genuine Labor Organizations-Kilusang Mayo Uno (ANGLO-KMU) meanwhile pointed out that the three students were released only after six days of continuous confinement at the Taguig City Police Station, way past the time periods prescribed by Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code.

“We are also alarmed at the brazen displays of intimidation by the police, where the detainees were repeatedly told that the police intended to hold them for six days, that detailed files about them were being compiled since the Grand Hyatt protest on 10 September, and that their arrest should serve as a ‘lesson’ to them,” Topacio told Bulatlat in a message.

Topacio also noted how Taguig City police shouted at the visiting relatives of the students and repeatedly asked to move away from the station to other parts of the Taguig City Hall complex while conferring with counsel …

title: Majority of reported ‘serious’ injuries to Indigenous children in Manitoba tied to sexual assault
content:
Warning: this story discusses child abuse and suicide


Manitoba’s youth advocate says more than half of serious injury reports involving kids are linked to sexual assault, and that 71 per cent of victims are Indigenous children.


“It’s pretty telling,” said Sherry Gott, the executive director of

Manitoba Advocate for Children and Youth (MACY)

. “The numbers are pretty high, 53 per cent of our reports are a result of sexual assault or sexual exploitation, and the majority of those are Indigenous children.”


MACY is a non-partisan advocacy organization funded by the provincial government.


Alongside investigative work, it provides advocacy and social services to youth and families, which can result in safety plans, placements and post-release mental health and addictions support for children and young adults (aged 18 to 20).


Since 2000, her office has published annual reports which summarize trends, data and updates with respect to youth in Manitoba, as well as the organization’s recommendations to the province.


In 2023, the organization created its Serious Injuries Reviews and Investigations program, in response to a recommendation from the provincial

Phoenix Sinclair Inquiry

, created to examine the circumstances surrounding the neglect, physical abuse and

eventual murder

 of the five-year-old girl in Fisher River Cree Nation almost a decade prior.


The inquiry resulted in amendments to provincial law, which aim to improve child welfare and investigations surrounding children both in and out of foster care.


According to the report, MACY received 506 referrals from April 2025 to March 2026. Only 300 of the referrals were able to be reviewed, according to the legal definition of a serious injury, according to the report. Five of the reviews were closed before completion because the youth died.


The report noted that the number of referrals received by MACY has been steadily growing over the last three years. The 2023-2024 report recorded 184, and 2024-2025 recorded 273.


Because of the demand, only 135 of the 300 referrals legally eligible for review have ended with complete serious injury reports, as of writing. Only 99 were assessed for potential investigation, and 36 of those assessments were reviewed further.


Just one case is currently being investigated.


Gott told APTN News that MACY doesn’t have the resources to keep up with the demand.


“There is a backlog, and we’ve actually redeployed some of our staff [from other departments] to do the work,” she said.


According to MACY, 53 per cent (71/135) of the injuries that received a report were a result of sexual assault, while 55 per cent of secondary injuries were also linked to the same cause.


Additionally, 25 per cent of cases involved drugs or alcohol; 22 per cent were linked to self-harm or attempted suicide; 20 per cent were bodily injuries, such as broken or fractured bones; 19 per cent involved gunshot or stab wounds; 15 per cent were head injuries; and accidental and “severe neglect” cases accounted for four per cent each.


Forty per cent of the injuries resulted in a hospital visit, and 35 per cent “were deemed life-threatening,” the annual report continued, and 71 per cent of all cases involved a youth who was First Nations, Inuit or Métis.


The report stated that, based on MACY’s data, 62 per cent of kids involved in serious injury reports have “experienced victimization in their lives.


“This fact alone highlights the importance of a targeted response and intervention by social services following any form of child victimization,” the report continued.


Additionally, “60 per cent experienced mental health concerns that were co-occurring, or combined with, substance use and suicidality.”


Gott recommended that the province should also pay attention to how many of the serious injuries occurred to a child in care.


“Either at the hands of caregivers, or foster parents, or their own families, so we need to highlight that quickly and implement some sort of strategy to support those children,” she said.


MACY also reviews and investigates the deaths of children, based on information received from the

Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (OCME)

 every time a death occurs.


In 2025-26, the OCME recorded 238 official child deaths; 195 of which involved children 17 and younger, and 43 involved young adults (18 to 20).


Almost half of the deaths were natural (44 per cent), and 36 per cent were undetermined. In most cases, the …

author: The Canadian Press
title: Gitxsan Huwilp Government in B.C. wants train hauling stopped in territory after latest derailment
content:
The

Gitxsan Huwilp Government

 in British Columbia said lives and food security are at risk after two recent rail accidents on the 103-year-old track along the Skeena River.


The First Nation said in a statement that the latest derailment has reignited its call for the “immediate stop to all train hauling” in its traditional territories and fishing waterways, calling the practice dangerous.


Several railcars jumped the tracks on Tuesday, spilling diesel and sending some cars loaded with forest products into the Skeena River about 15 kilometres west of Terrace.


CN Rail announced the track had been repaired and train traffic resumed on Thursday, while the two crew members who were injured in the derailment have been released from hospital.


The company said environmental protection measures are in place in the river and specialized environmental response teams remain at the site, working to contain and recover spilled diesel fuel and removing derailed equipment.


The First Nation said it is the second such incident in eight months, after a mudslide derailed grain cars travelling along the river south of Prince Rupert in March, resulting in a spill of nearly 8,000 litres of diesel.


Hereditary Chief Toby Howard said the latest accident demonstrates the continuing risks posed by freight transportation through Gitxsan territory.


“A 103-year-old track has created dangerous conditions for the rail system in our territory,” he said in the statement.


CN Rail did not immediately respond to a request for a response to the nation’s calls to halt train hauling in the territory.


Howard said the nation’s hereditary chiefs have offered the provincial government assistance in identifying “the areas of most vulnerability on the line” but the Transportation Ministry has dismissed the offer.


“The hauling of any materials — dangerous, human or otherwise — must stop immediately until CN Rail can guarantee the rail line is safe,” he said.


The derailment is also “well within the reach of ocean tides, jeopardizing an entire ecosystem,” the First Nation’s statement said.


“We must ensure that every inch of the railway from Burns Lake to Prince Rupert is inspected, otherwise our Gitxsan people are not safe,” Howards said.


Read more:


Derailment in Gitxsan territory has the hereditary chief calling for a halt to all rail traffic


CN Rail said it appears a rock slide caused Tuesday’s derailment, which involved two locomotives and five railcars.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Nunavut child advocate considered suing territorial government over child welfare stonewalling
content:
Nunavut’s child advocate says she was ready to take the territory’s Department of Family Services to court because of what she characterized as the DFS stonewalling her office’s access to information pertaining to Nunavummiut children in care. 


Jane Bates told Nunavut’s legislative assembly in September that despite an information-sharing protocol, the department was deciding for itself whether, and when, her office should be involved in assessing its conduct.


“This situation has become so serious,” the Representative for Children and Youth (RCYO) told legislators, “that earlier this year I advised the deputy minister that, unless the underlying issue concerning the RCYO’s statutory authority and the department’s corresponding obligations could be resolved, I was prepared to withdraw from the GN–RCYO Protocol and seek the assistance of the Nunavut Court of Justice to ensure that our office could carry out its statutory mandate.


“If significant limits, safeguards and independent oversight are not put in place, the department will continue to operate in the same manner with the same results.”


These details are from notes shared with APTN News of Bates’s presentation on the crisis in Nunavut’s child-welfare system delivered on Sept. 24 and 25 to the territory’s Legislative Assembly’s Standing Committee on Oversight of Government Operations and Public Accounts.


Legislative Assembly of Nunavut. Photo: APTN


In the presentation notes, Bates said the DFS has made no significant progress in four years on recommendations to address serious concerns about the safety and well-being of children in care, foster care in the territory, and concerns of families and guardians.

 


Furthermore, the presentation noted that the department is not formally answerable to any authority, leaving no one to force DFS to carry out improvements to its quality of care.

 


Government services, Bates wrote, “Are NOT meeting the needs of Nunavummiut, they are causing harm and, in some cases, serious harm.”

 


Significant power and authority

 


According to the presentation in the legislature, Bates’s office has been contacted by members of the RCMP, public prosecutors, legal aid and out-of-territory facilities, who have each expressed concerns for the treatment of Nunavummiut children in the foster care system.


Those who raised concerns, Bates noted, felt they had not been heard and saw no change in the way the system worked.

 


“I can state unequivocally,” Bates wrote, “The state of child welfare is one of the most critical issues facing children, youth and families in Nunavut today. I am not referring simply to the prevalence of child maltreatment or to the number of families in need of supports and services. I am talking about the way those services are currently being delivered.”

 


Bates argued that the DFS operates according to “an authority based approach, where decisions are made for people rather than with them.”

 


She said that her office continued to identify circumstances where the rights of children, youth and families were not upheld, where children who were supposed to be protected were not, and where the DFS failed to deliver care, supervision, planning and supports to children whom the Department was supposed to protect and care for.


Jane Bates, Child and Youth Representative for Nunavut, has been in her position since July, 2019. Photo: APTN


At the same time, Bates noted, the DFS has significant power and authority over all aspects of the child-welfare system. She said her office has seen “this power and authority exercised in ways that do not ensure the delivery of ethical, equitable and consistent services” and that may even “result in further harm to the very children and families the system is intended to serve.”

 


“In practical terms,” wrote Bates, “the department is currently writing the test, marking the test, and assigning itself a passing grade.

 


“What ties many of these issues together is an approach in which the department determines what it believes is best. The views of children and youth are not considered, and the knowledge of families and caregivers is not sought.”

 


A public face of service, a private face of failure

 


Bates identified what she called a significant difference between how the government describes the child-welfare system and how her office and others see the DFS operating in practice.

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: Canada commits $6.2M to 2028 North American Indigenous Games
content:
The federal government is increasing its investment in the 2028 North American Indigenous Games by $1.3 million, bringing its total contribution to $6.2 million. 


According to the government, the money is intended to expand Indigenous participation in sport and strengthen opportunities for First Nations, Inuit and Métis athletes across the country.


Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden announced the funding Thursday during the official launch of the 2028 Games, which will bring an estimated 5,250 participants representing as many as 700 Indigenous nations to Winnipeg and communities across Manitoba from July 9 to 23, 2028.


The federal government says the host province is expected to match its $6.2-million investment in the 2028 Games. 


The investments come as the federal government faces the broader challenge of addressing barriers to sport participation in Indigenous communities, where access to culturally relevant programming, facilities, coaching and competitive opportunities remains central to developing sustainable pathways for Indigenous athletes.


Van Koeverden said the investments are intended to advance reconciliation while creating opportunities for Indigenous youth to participate, compete and pursue athletic excellence.


“We’re investing in Indigenous sport and youth and promoting participation, competition and the pursuit of excellence.”


For Indigenous communities, however, the significance of the games extends beyond the financial commitments and the competition itself.


The North American Indigenous Games (NAIG) are among the largest Indigenous multisport and cultural gatherings in North America, bringing together Indigenous youth to represent their communities while celebrating their respective cultures, traditions and identities.


The event provides a high-profile platform for Indigenous athletes while creating opportunities for cultural exchange, community connections and the development of future leaders.


Rick Brant, president of the North American Indigenous Games Council, said the announcement represents an important step toward welcoming Indigenous athletes to Manitoba in 2028.


“Together, we will deliver a games experience where athletes can compete with pride, celebrate their cultures and build connections that last a lifetime,” Brant said.


Norway House Cree Nation and the Southern Chiefs’ Organization are leading the hosting effort. 


The 2028 event also marks a return to Winnipeg, which previously hosted the North American Indigenous Games in 2002.


North American Indigenous Games in Halifax 2023. Photo by: APTN


Beyond the podium: Building Indigenous sport pathways


While the additional investment in the 2028 NAIG represents the most immediate announcement, the federal government’s broader funding commitments signal an effort to strengthen Indigenous sport development beyond a single international event.


Budget 2026 proposes $16 million over four years to expand access to culturally relevant sport programming for Indigenous Peoples and strengthen Indigenous sport leadership across Canada.


The proposal is particularly significant because Indigenous sport development involves more than creating opportunities for athletes to compete at elite levels.


The federal government’s

Sport for Social Development in Indigenous Communities (SSDIC)

 program is designed to support that work through funding for Indigenous nations and organizations delivering sport and recreation initiatives within their communities.


Rob Newman, president of the Aboriginal Sport Circle, said the impact of the NAIG extends well beyond the athletes who compete.


“Behind every team are years of work by Indigenous sport bodies and communities helping young people get there,” Newman said.


He said the launch and confirmed funding build on the work already being undertaken by Indigenous sport organizations and communities.


“It gives Indigenous youth the chance to represent their people and carry home a stronger belief in themselves and what they can achieve,” Newman said.

title: Yazidi women’s organizations call for international search for missing persons
content:
Twelve years after the genocide committed by the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) against the Yazidis in Shengal, the fate of around 3,000 people remains unknown. The Free Yazidi Women’s Movement (TAJÊ) and the Umbrella Organization of Yazidi Women’s Councils (SMJÊ) have issued a joint appeal to 54 state and international institutions and political officials, calling for the establishment of an international search and rescue commission to locate abducted women and children in particular and secure their release.


The letter is titled “We demand freedom and justice for those abducted during the genocide of August 3, 2014.” The organizations recall that around 6,000 Yazidis were abducted during the ISIS attack on Shengal, and numerous families are still waiting for news of their loved ones although twelve years have passed since. “Every family whose loved ones are missing has the right to know the truth. Every person who remains in captivity has the right to freedom. And every victim of the genocide has the right to justice,” the letter reads.


Uncertain fate following the dismantling of al-Hol camp


The women’s organizations expressed particular concern about the situation in Syria. They said numerous abducted Yazidis were held in Idlib and other regions in the past, and the ongoing political and military instability is making it difficult to search for them. Another concern was the dismantling of al-Hol camp during the Syrian offensive against the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria at the beginning of this year. According to TAJÊ and SMJÊ, Yazidi women who had been unable to reveal their identities for fear of threats and reprisals were also among those held there.


Since the dismantling of the camp, TAJÊ and SMJÊ said, it has remained unknown where these women were taken and under what conditions they are currently living. The fate of other abducted Yazidis in Iraq and Turkey must also be clarified, they said and, in this context, referred to their campaign “For Justice and Freedom – Become a Voice for Those Abducted During the Genocide.” The campaign aims to prevent the crimes committed against the Yazidis and the suffering of their families from being forgotten as time passes.


Four demands to the international community


The letter focuses on four specific demands. First, TAJÊ and SMJÊ call for the establishment of a specialized international team involving the relevant states, international organizations, and other responsible bodies. The team would systematically search for those abducted, determine their whereabouts, and organize their release. Second, the women’s organizations demand that ISIS perpetrators be brought to trial not only for terrorist offenses but explicitly for genocide and crimes against humanity. They demand that the crimes committed against the Yazidis be prosecuted in accordance with international law.


As a third measure, they propose an international commission to investigate cases of missing persons. Scientific investigations, identity registries, and DNA analyses would be used to identify and locate abducted and missing persons and reunite them with their families. Finally, the organizations demand that states that have officially recognized the genocide against the Yazidis take practical steps to give effect to that recognition.


These include searching for missing persons, rescuing those abducted, protecting the rights of survivors, and prosecuting those responsible. “Recognition of the genocide is not merely a political and moral stance. It also entails far-reaching obligations,” TAJÊ and SMJÊ emphasized.


Letter sent to parliaments, governments, and UN institutions


The appeal was sent to a total of 54 government bodies, international organizations, and political officials. The recipients include the German Bundestag, the Federal Foreign Office, and the German Institute for Human Rights, as well as parliaments, ministries, and human rights institutions in Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria, Sweden, Luxembourg, Portugal, and Armenia.


Institutions in Australia, Canada, Ireland, and the United States, as well as the European Commission, the European Parliament, and several United Nations human rights bodies, were also contacted. Among the officials personally addressed was European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

title: YRK reports Iranian drone and artillery attacks on Serdeşt region
content:
Iranian regime forces attacked areas in Serdeşt district in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) with artillery and drones on Wednesday. According to the Press and Communication Center of the Eastern Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK), the attacks were concentrated particularly on the Mirava region.


According to the YRK, the shelling on November 18 lasted from 11 am to noon and was part of the Islamic Republic’s ongoing artillery and drone attacks on the region. The attacks reportedly caused damage to the natural environment and landscape. They also significantly disrupted the daily lives of local residents.


YRK underlined that the repeated attacks were fueling insecurity and concern among residents and making their living conditions and daily activities more difficult. The YRK reported that their forces had suffered no casualties or damage in the attacks.


Most recently, the Iranian regime carried out massive attacks on Serdeşt last week. In the ensuing clashes between the Revolutionary Guards and YRK units, guerrilla fighter Dersim Behar lost his life.


The YRK reported on Tuesday, November 17, that their units carried out two actions in the cities of Bane and Serdeşt regions.


According to the statement, specialized and professional YRK teams targeted a base of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in central Serdeşt on November 15. The base commander and one Revolutionary Guard were killed, while two other Revolutionary Guards were wounded.


On the other hand, another YRK unit killed an officer affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in Bane on November 16.


The YRK stated that both actions had been carried out to honor Dersim Behar’s memory and avenge her death.

title: Four lawyers remanded in custody in Izmir
content:
The police and prosecutorial procedures concerning the six lawyers, who were detained following raids on their homes on the morning of 17 November in Izmir, have been completed.


The six lawyers, including members of the Izmir Branch of the Progressive Lawyers Association (ÇHD), were transferred to the İzmir Bayraklı Courthouse. Following their statements to the prosecutor, they were brought before the Criminal Judgeship of Peace on duty, with prosecutors requesting their arrest.


Following their hearings, the court ordered the arrest of ÇHD Izmir Branch Secretary and lawyer Veysi Çetin, ÇHD members and lawyers Yemen Cankan and Erdoğan Akdoğdu, and lawyer Bahattin Özdemir.


Meanwhile, ÇHD member and lawyer Emrah Kanbay and lawyer Göksel Akbaba, who appeared before the court as part of the same investigation, were released subject to judicial control measures.

title: DEM Party to visit Abdullah Öcalan
content:
The Imrali delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) will travel to the Turkish prison island of Imrali again in the coming days to meet with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. The delegation consists of members of parliament Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, as well as lawyer Faik Özgür Erol.


The delegation last visited Öcalan on September 13. More than two months have passed since that meeting. An exact date for the upcoming visit has not yet been announced.


The announcement comes just days after new information emerged about Öcalan’s detention and working conditions. DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan stated during his party’s parliamentary group meeting on November 17 that Öcalan had been moved to a residential area specially built for him on Imrali. Accordingly, his working conditions have also changed following the relocation. In addition, his secretarial support has been increased to enable him to work more quickly and effectively, Bakırhan stated.


The changes are linked to the ongoing peace and democratization process. In his speech, Bakırhan emphasized that, following the cessation of armed hostilities and the initiation of dialogue, the focus must now be on establishing the legal and political foundations and opening up space for democratic politics.

title: Hatimoğulları calls for strengthening local democracy in Adana
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları has accused the Turkish government of neglecting Adana’s economic development and weakening local self-government. At a meeting with neighborhood and village heads (muhtars) as part of the campaign “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice,” she criticized the shifting of state investment incentives and agricultural policies that are accelerating the decline in agricultural production.


Hatimoğulları explained that muhtars were often the first point of contact for people affected by poverty, unemployment, and social exclusion. She remarked that women, unemployed young people, people with disabilities, and those without adequate access to social benefits, in particular, turned to them with their problems.


“Adana has lost its industrial base”


Hatimoğulları recalled that Adana had once been a major industrial and agricultural center that attracted workers from across Turkey. “The fertile lands of Çukurova provided a livelihood for many people. Industry was much stronger. But because investment incentives were shifted to other cities, Adana has lost its industrial base. Agricultural policies have also deprived the city of its agriculture. The plains of Çukurova, Harran, and Konya have the potential to meet the country’s food needs. Instead of utilizing this potential, however, the government is pursuing policies that undermine agricultural production,” Hatimoğulları said.


Elected mayors must be reinstated


Addressing government interventions in Adana’s municipal administrations, Hatimoğulları called for the reinstatement of elected mayors. She stressed that the arrests and removals from office not only disrupted the work of municipalities but also made it more difficult for muhtars to convey concerns from their neighborhoods to the relevant authorities.


The DEM Party Co-Chair continued: “The people of Adana elected Zeydan Karalar, but he is no longer at the head of the city administration. Although he was released from detention, he has not been reinstated. The elected mayor of Ceyhan, Kadir Aydar, was also released but has not been reinstated. Seyhan Mayor Oya Tekin is in prison. Following the operation against the Çukurova municipal administration, Emrah Kozay and other officials remain in detention. Can we still speak of local self-government and democracy under these circumstances?”


Hatimoğulları demanded that the affected mayors and municipal officials be allowed to stand trial without being held in detention and be reinstated in their positions. She also called for expanding the powers of municipalities and muhtars. “In the face of growing social hardship, they are often barely able to respond to the population’s requests for assistance. Real democracy does not emerge when everything is governed from Ankara. Real democracy emerges through the strengthening of local self-government.”


“Peace must not become an election campaign tool”


Regarding the peace and democratization process, Hatimoğulları described the absence of further news of deaths among Kurdish and Turkish young people as the most important achievement of the past two years. “This is enormous progress for us. We all know how much suffering and devastation each death caused among those affected. The fact that we no longer have to experience this is a major gain.” At the same time, she criticized the antidemocratic measures, police operations, arrests, and detentions for placing a strain on the process. She said the issue was the democratic and peaceful resolution of a century-old question which must not be subordinated to the interests of individual parties.


“Whoever tries to sacrifice this process for their narrow party-political interests, whoever fails to approach it sincerely and seeks to turn it into an election campaign tool, will be mistaken. No matter who they are. Because we regard this process as a genuine peace process. We want it to succeed, to ensure there is no turning back, and to prevent us from ending up where we started.” Hatimoğulları emphasized that the DEM Party had never viewed the process as an opportunity to gain partisan political advantages. She said this position applied equally to the governing parties and the opposition.


“We want the deaths to stop permanently. That is why we support this process. No party should reduce it to its own interests. We say this to both the governing parties and the opposition,” she stated.

title: HPG releases names of seven fallen guerrillas from Merîwan
content:
The Press Center of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) has released the identities of seven guerrilla fighters from the Eastern Kurdish city of Merîwan who lost their lives in various areas of Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq) between 2011 and 2024. In a statement, the HPG paid tribute to their commitment to the Kurdish freedom struggle and extended their condolences to the families of the martyrs.


The HPG statement said:


“We remember our comrades Rênas Botan, Kawa Hewraman, Sîrwan Qendîl, Hewrê Kemanger, Sîrwan Zirêbar, Serxwebûn Hewraman, and Serkeft Hewramî, who fought as steadfast militants committed to the Apoist principle of self-sacrifice, with respect, love, and gratitude.


Our comrades Rênas Botan, Kawa Hewraman, Sîrwan Qendîl, Hewrê Kemanger, Sîrwan Zirêbar, Serxwebûn Hewraman, and Serkeft Hewramî took up the struggle for freedom against the centuries-long oppression of our people and joined the struggle without hesitation, guided by the Apoist principle of self-sacrifice. They rejected colonial borders and the order that denies the existence of our people, and assumed a leading role in the struggle in the mountains of Kurdistan.


Despite the advanced military technology of our time, they relied solely on the strength of human will, consciousness, and conviction, setting an extraordinary example of courage and determination. They fought fearlessly to defend the existence of our people and, through their selfless commitment, embodied the unyielding will to resist colonialism.


Through their actions and unwavering commitment to the freedom struggle, they became an embodiment of the determination on which our resistance is founded. Our fallen comrades, who have secured a permanent place in the hearts of our people, have thus become guides toward a free future, an expression of our struggle, and a guarantee of its success. We extend our condolences to the esteemed families of our martyrs and to the entire patriotic Kurdish people. We pledge to remain faithful to their memory under all circumstances and to resolutely achieve the goals for which they fought.”

title: DEM Party calls for timetable for parliamentary monitoring commission
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) is calling for a binding timetable for the establishment of a parliamentary monitoring commission as part of the peace and democratization process. At a press conference at the party’s headquarters, spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan criticized the fact that it remained unclear when the commission would begin its work despite talks between Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş and the political parties.


Following the talks last week, Kurtulmuş had announced that the commission would be established “in the coming days.” Doğan described this statement as insufficient: “Instead of vague statements, a timetable should have been presented long ago. What are they waiting for to complete the preparations? Why is there a delay? There is nothing left to wait for.”


The DEM Party spokesperson demanded that the commission’s working procedures, responsibilities, and roadmap be made public. She also said it was necessary to clarify the political framework under which the parties would cooperate within the commission. She noted that the delays were also affecting coordination between the legislative and executive branches.


Call for the participation of all parties


Doğan emphasized that all parliamentary groups must be represented on the monitoring commission, and that broad political participation was essential to the success of the peace process. In this context, she criticized the decision by Yeni Party Chair Özgür Özel not to nominate any members to the commission. During the work of the National Commission for Solidarity, Brotherhood and Democracy, he had declined to participate in the delegation visiting Abdullah Öcalan. This was compounded by votes against the framework law.


“Now comes the decision not to participate in the monitoring commission either. It creates the impression that they want to avoid being perceived as supporters of the process at all costs. This does not reflect well on them,” Doğan stated. She stressed that the demand for democratization was legitimate and necessary but must not lead political forces to distance themselves from the peace process. Peace and democratization were inseparably linked, she underlined.


Doğan warned that the Yeni Party’s stance could widen the gap between the party and the Kurdish people. “The debate must not be reduced to party-political majorities and tactical calculations. We are in a process that must rise above such calculations and in which potential pitfalls must be identified in time. To end this war that has lasted for 50 years, everyone must be at the table. We call for the participation of all parties.”


“Sick prisoners must not be left to die”


Another major focus of the press conference was the situation of seriously ill prisoners. Doğan expressed her support for the indefinite vigil outside the Turkish Ministry of Justice, which is demanding the release of sick prisoners and guaranteed access to medical care.


She recalled the recent death of political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam and criticized the fact that applications for release from prison and suspension of sentence had gone unanswered. “If it is possible to save a person’s life but a decision is made not to do so, then that is a political decision,” Doğan said. She also cited the cases of Evin Zapsu, who is imprisoned in Kayseri-Bünyan Women’s Prison and has stage IV cancer, and Newroz Bozkurt, who is being held in Sincan Women’s Prison and suffers from chronic leukemia.


“The imprisonment of seriously ill people under prison conditions must end. We will not allow the right to life to be subjected to arbitrary administrative decisions, political calculations, and arbitrary practices. We support the sit-in protest and will stand in solidarity with the families until the very end. For us, this is a matter of rights and justice.”


Criticism of appointed trustees and political bans


Doğan also condemned an appeals court’s decision to uphold the 19-year-and-six-month prison sentence imposed on Sıddık Akış, the co-mayor of Hakkari. She pointed out that the ruling had been issued at a time when the legal foundations of the peace process were under discussion. The continued arrest and prosecution of Kurdish politicians, she argued, contradicted the stated goal of democratic reform. According to Doğan, what is needed is an expansion of the space for democratic politics rather than further restrictions.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Garbage truck fire caused by ‘suspected’ lithium-ion battery
content:
A garbage truck fire believed to have been caused by a lithium-ion battery prompted the City of Iqaluit to remind residents to take care when sorting their garbage.


The truck was on its regular route Wednesday when it caught fire while collecting waste on Joamie Court near Tundra Buddies Daycare,  a public service announcement issued later that day said.


“Crews responded quickly by unloading the waste onto the roadway to prevent the situation from escalating,” the announcement said.


While the fire’s cause has not been confirmed, officials suspect it was related to the improper disposal of lithium-ion, or rechargeable, batteries.


Lithium-ion batteries can spark fires when crushed, punctured or overheated, sometimes leading to explosions that can ignite nearby paper, cardboard and or debris, the announcement said.


The city issued a

similar reminder

 in July after a fire at the city’s landfill. As well, in August 2024, a fire

caused

 by a laptop left overheating on a bed caused damage to a Rankin Inlet home.


Iqaluit residents are advised to discard lithium-ion batteries at the safe disposal site at the city’s landfill.


The city is also creating plans for additional drop-off locations for hazardous waste, Coun. Kyle Sheppard said Wednesday in a Facebook post.

author: Chris Walker
title: Jeffries Staffer Created AI Program to Monitor Democratic Caucus Members
content:
The House Democratic Party leader’s office denies that Jeffries knew about the AI program.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A staffer for House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) custom-designed an artificial intelligence (AI) program to monitor the public communications of lawmakers and different factions within the party’s caucus.

According to reporting from The Washington Sun, which unearthed the source code for the program in a public GitHub software repository, the staffer asked the AI tool to monitor statements and social media posts of House Democrats in an effort to improve messaging strategies for Jeffries.

The program, which the staffer called Caucus Pulse, was produced using Anthropic’s AI agent Claude. To help the program, the staffer, whose identity is not yet known, fed it tens of thousands of posts from Democratic lawmakers purchased through the social media site X.

The program itself explains its purpose as being an assistant to the staffer, describing them as a “research analyst in the House Democratic Leader’s research and writing shop.”

The Washington Sun reached out to Jeffries’s office, with the Democratic leader’s spokesperson Christie Stephenson assuring the publication that Jeffries (who is the presumptive next Speaker of the House) wasn’t himself aware of Caucus Pulse.

“A staffer in this office conducted a short-lived experiment with AI in a personal capacity, without the involvement of the Office of the Democratic Leader,” Stephenson said. “No official resources were used, and we’re addressing this matter internally.”

In public statements, Jeffries has spoken out about the rapid and unregulated expansion of AI.

“The explosive growth of artificial intelligence and the challenges that are therein presented — that’s not a hoax,” Jeffries said in September, referencing comments from President Donald Trump that described fears about AI as hoaxes conjured by the media or by Democrats. In that same statement, Jeffries called for “immediate” and “decisive” action on the issue.

The regulations Jeffries will push for if he becomes Speaker of the House, however, are yet to be determined. Notably, Jeffries has received significant backing from many AI industry leaders, including $150,000 from executives at Anduril, an AI-weapons company that contracts with the federal government, and $44,300 from Mehdi Allhassani, an executive at the AI surveillance company Palantir, among other tech-based campaign donations this past election cycle.

House lawmakers also formed a bipartisan “AI Safety and Innovation Caucus” this week, which will be charged with balancing AI safeguards while also “ensuring the United States remains a global leader in innovative AI technologies,” the group announced.

The regulation of AI and data centers was one of the top issues among voters in the midterm elections. According to exit polling data, 56 percent of voters described those two issues as a “crucial or major factor” in determining how they cast their ballots.

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we must raise $16,000 before midnight. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference.

title: Bursa Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri kayyım ve siyasi yasaklara karşı eylem yaptı: Bıçak kemiğe dayandı
content:
Bursa – Bursa Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri, Sözcü TV'ye kayyım atanması ve CHP'nin 38. Olağan Kurultayı'na ilişkin ceza davasında Yeni Parti Bursa İl Başkanı Nihat Yeşiltaş ile Osmangazi Belediye Başkanı Erkan Aydın'a verilen 2 yıl 1 ay hapis ve siyasi yasak kararını Fomara Meydanı'nda yaptığı basın açıklaması ile protesto etti.

Bursa Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri adına konuşan Derviş Erdem, "AKP iktidarı, eleştirel sesleri susturmaya ve toplumun haber alma kanallarını denetim altına almaya yönelik politikalarını sürdürüyor. Sözcü TV’ye yönelik müdahale, basın özgürlüğüne, halkın haber alma hakkına ve farklı görüşlerin kamuoyuna ulaşabilmesine yönelik kabul edilemez bir müdahaledir. Bizler özgür basının ve halkın doğru bilgiye ulaşma hakkının savunucusu olmaya devam edeceğiz. Sansüre ve baskıya karşı Sözcü TV emekçileriyle dayanışmamızı sürdüreceğiz. Kamu yararını, halkın haber alma hakkını, gazetecilik mesleğini hedef alan, Türkiye’de demokrasiyi yerle bir eden, anayasal hakları yok sayan otoriter tek adam rejimi adım adım tahkim etmeye dönük yapıldığı malum olan uygulamaların hayata geçirilmesi kabul edilemez. Foncu hırsızlar, yağmacılar gönüllü iadelerle işledikleri suçtan yırtarak veya aflarını isteyerek halk arasında serbestçe dolaşırken sesini çıkaranın, itiraz edenin gerçekleri, doğruları kamu adına yayınlayanların sabaha karşı kapısına dayanan bu düzende hiçbir hakkımızın güvence altında olmadığını kamuoyunun bilgisine sunarız. Artık bıçak kemiğe dayandığı, sözün bittiği yerdeyiz" dedi.

Daha sonra konuşan ÇGD Bursa Yürütme Kurulu üyesi Hatice Nur Derya, "Halk TV’nin ardından Sözcü’ye de kayyum atanması, Türkiye’de medya ikliminin kara kışa döndüğünü gösteriyor. Kayyum kararının gerekçesi, gözaltıların hukuki dayanağı ve TMSF’ye verilen yetkilerin sınırları gecikmeden açıklanmalıdır. Hangi haberin yayımlanacağına, hangi sorunun sorulacağına ve kime söz verileceğine gazeteciler karar vermelidir. Haber kaynaklarının gizliliği, çalışanların iş güvencesi ve haber merkezlerinin editoryal bağımsızlığı korunmalıdır. Yetkilileri kayyum kararını kaldırmaya çağırıyoruz. Sözcü çalışanlarıyla dayanışma içindeyiz. Bu günler de geçer. O gün geldiğinde, bugün gerçeğin peşinden giden gazeteciler de halkın o gerçeği öğrenmesini engelleyen kararlar da hatırlanacak" dedi.

Eylemde konuşan KESK Genel Sekreteri Sevgi Yılmaz, "Halk düşmanı, emek düşmanı, otoriter rejimler halkın haber alma hakkından korkarlar. Onun için de basın otoriter rejimlerde her zaman tehdit altındadır. Her zaman gazetecileri susturmaya çalışırlar. Türkiye Cumhuriyeti tarihinde de aslında hiç iç açıcı bir tablo yok. Bu baskıları niye yapıyorlar çünkü fon vurgununun yazılmasından rahatsızlar. Bu ülkenin Milli Eğitim Bakanı bizim çocuklarımızı MESEM'lerde ölüme gönderiyor bunun haber yapılmasından rahatsız. Bizim en temel meseleler hakkında bilgi sahibi olmamızdan rahatsız. Haber alme hakkımız, seçme ve seçilme hakkımız ve bütçe hakkımız için birleşmekten başka çaremiz yok. DİSK, KESK, TMMOB ve TTB olarak bu haklarımız için 12 Aralık'ta Ankara'dayız" dedi.

CHP'nin 38. Olağan Kurultayı'na ilişkin ceza davasında 2 yıl 1 ay hapis ve siyasi yasak cezası alan Yeni Parti Bursa İl Başkanı Nihat Yeşiltaş ise şunları söyledi, "İktidarın TELE1 Halk TV ve Sözcü TV’den rahatsız olduğunu ve bu nedenle kayyum atadı. Bunun tek bir sebebi var. O da halkın haber alma özgürlüğünü engellemektir. Çünkü bu iktidar foncuların, talancıların, rantçıların düzeni, bu düzenin içinde kurdukları bütün yapıları deşifre olmasın, halk öğrenmesin, millet öğrenmesin diye kendilerine muhalif olan sadece ve sadece gerçekleri yazan basını susturmaya çalışıyorlar. Hepimize bir görev düşüyor. Biz basına sahip çıkacağız."

Hakkında verilen hukuksuz karara ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulunan Yeşiltaş, “Dün Ankara'da bir hukuk garabeti yaşandı. Delil yok. Kanıt yok. Dosyanın içi bomboş ve biz savunma yaparken saat 10.00'dan saat 17.00'a kadar sadece bizi dinleyen merak edip hiçbir soru bile sorulmayan ve daha önceden artık kararı bile verilmiş, sonuçları bile belli olmuş bir hukuk tiyatrosuyla karşılaştık. Burada hukukun nasıl siyasallaştığını orada gördük. Bugün aynı dosyadan aynı ithamlarla yargılandığımız birlikte yargılandığımız kişilerin İzmir'e ihanet eden İzmir'in iradesini satan Cemil Tugay beraat etti. Ve bizler siyasi yasak aldık. İktidara karşı direnenlerin, onurlu bir mücadele ortaya koyanların ve yapılan haksızlıklara karşı yoksulluğa, açlığa, sefalete karşı bir direnci bir itirazı ortaya …

title: Şenzen'e Berlin'den yanıt: “Yeni Yalta'ya hayır, Avrupa masada olacak"
content:
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin ve Şi Cinping'in 19 Kasım Şenzen zirvesi ve zirveden çıkan bildiriye en kapsamlı siyasi karşılık Berlin'den geldi. Almanya Başbakanı Friedrich Merz, Ukrayna'yı destekleyen ülkeler toplantısında “Yalta formatında bir düzenleme barış getirmez” dedi: “Yalta'da Avrupa bölündü, paylaşıldı. Bunun yeniden olmasına izin vermeyeceğiz.”


Berlin: "Odada Ukrayna olmadan Ukrayna, Avrupa olmadan Avrupa konuşulamaz"


Berlin'deki buluşma, Fransa ve Britanya'nın öncülüğünde Mart 2025'te oluşturulan “Gönüllüler Koalisyonu”nun (Coalition of the Willing) zirvesiydi. Berlin'deki zirvenin Şenzen'le aynı güne denk gelmesi tesadüf değildi. Financial Times'ın Alman hükümet yetkililerine dayandırdığı bilgiye göre, Gönüllüler Koalisyonu'nun toplantısı, Trump, Putin ve Şi'nin görüşmesine hızlı, ortaklaşa ve hazırlıklı bir yanıt verebilmek amacıyla özellikle bu tarihe planlanmıştı.


Ukrayna'nın güvenliğini desteklemek ve olası bir ateşkesin uygulanmasına yönelik güvenceler geliştirmek amacıyla kurulan koalisyon, Türkiye de dahil olmak üzere 36 ülkeyi kapsıyor. Adı, 2003'te ABD öncülüğündeki Irak işgaline katılan ülkeler için kullanılan “Coalition of the Willing” ifadesini çağrıştırsa da iki oluşumun amaçları ve siyasi bağlamları farklı. Berlin toplantısı, Şenzen Bildirisi'ne verilen yanıtın yalnızca birkaç Avrupa başkentinden değil, önceden örgütlenmiş uluslararası bir diplomatik girişimden geldiğini de gösterdi.


Fransa, Almanya, Britanya'nın ortak açıklaması


Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron ise Şenzen bildirisinin başlı başına yeni bir dünya düzeni getirdiği yorumuna katılmadı:


“Bunun dünyanın yeniden düzenlenmesi anlamına geldiğini sanmıyorum.”


Macron Avrupa güvenliği kapsamında Berlin toplantısını öne çıkardı.


Britanya Başbakanı Andy Burnham da ilkeyi açıkça ifade etti:


“Ukrayna odada olmadan Ukrayna hakkında, Avrupa temsil edilmeden Avrupa güvenliği hakkında karar alınamaz.”


Berlin yalnızca tepki açıklamakla kalmadı. Almanya, Fransa, Britanya ve Ukrayna liderlerinin ortak bildirisinde, Rusya'nın saldırıları kınandı; ateşkes sonrasında Ukrayna'ya hukuken bağlayıcı güvenlik güvenceleri, Avrupa öncülüğünde çokuluslu bir güç ve ABD ile eşgüdüm içinde ateşkesin denetlenmesi seçenekleri sıralandı. Rusya'ya ekonomik baskının sürdürülmesi ve enerji ateşkesi istendi.


Görünürdeki farklılıklara karşın, Berlin Bildirisi bir Washington–Avrupa kopuşunu haber vermiyor. Berlin zirvesine katılan Trump'ın özel temsilcileri Jared Kushner ve Steve Witkoff da Avrupalıların görüşme masasında yer almasını desteklediler. Kushner Berlin bildirisiyle aynı doğrultuda konuştu: 


“Avrupa'nın masada olmasının adil, uzun vadeli ve kalıcı barış için zorunlu olduğuna inanıyoruz”


Putin de Şenzen'de Avrupa'nın Ukrayna müzakerelerine katılmasına karşı olmadığını, ancak bunun koşullarını önce Moskova'da görüşmek istediğini söyledi.


“Avrupalılar olmadan Avrupa'nın güvenliğini tartışmanın anlamsız olduğunu biliyoruz.”


Ardından da şunu ekledi:


“Avrupa'nın bu görüşmelere ne getireceğini anlamamız gerekiyor.”


Avrupa'da farklı görüşler 


NATO Genel Sekreteri Mark Rutte, nükleer güçlerin görüşmesini olağan bulduğunu ve yeni bir Yalta'dan endişelenmediğini söyledi.


Litvanya Cumhurbaşkanı Gitanas Nausėda ise zirveyi dünyanın yeniden paylaşılması olarak yorumlamaktan kaçındı, ama Çin ve Rusya'nın veto yetkisini sürekli korurken BM reformunun öncülüğüne soyunmasını sorguladı.


Polonya Başbakanı Donald Tusk da Trump'ın Putin'e “dostum” demesine  “Tanrı bizi böyle dostlardan korusun” diye karşılık verdi. 


BM reformu: 3 daimi üye, 193 ülke adına konuşabilir mi?


Şenzen bildirisinin ilk maddesi BM'nin “küresel sorunlara daha etkin yanıt verebilmesi” için reform sözü veriyor. Ancak Konsey'in genişlemesi, veto hakkı ve bölgelerin temsili hakkında somut bir çneri içermiyor. 


Oysa zaten masada somut reform önerileri var. Brezilya, Almanya, Hindistan ve Japonya'dan oluşan G4 grubu eylülde daimi ve geçici üye sayısının artırılmasını istemişti. Afrika ülkelerinin ortak talebi: Kıtaya 2 daimi ve 5 geçici üyelik verilmesi, veto korunacaksa Afrika'nın da bu hakka sahip olması. Şenzen bildirisi çoktandır gündemde olan bu talepleri yanıtsız bırakırken reform konusu ilk kez Trump, Putin ve Şi tarafından gündeme getirilmişçesine kaleme alınmıştı. r.

title: Musk Says He’s Not MAGA After Spending Nearly Half a Billion Backing Republicans
content:
After years of promoting Trump’s far right agenda, Musk claimed that he is actually “quite moderate.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

After years of promoting Donald Trump’s “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) agenda, Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he no longer considers himself part of the pro-Trump movement.

Speaking remotely at The New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk attempted to suggest that he had never harbored such viewpoints — despite his stint as the head of the Trump administration’s so-called “Department of Government Efficiency,” or DOGE.

“I’m not MAGA. … I’m not sure what MAGA means, but I don’t think I’m — like, if it means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that,” the multi-billionaire said.

Musk further claimed that he prefers “checks and balances” in government, and described himself as “quite moderate.”

Musk added that he felt “pretty foolish for how much money I spent in the midterms” in support of MAGA-aligned Republicans.

Elon Musk claims he’s “not MAGA” pic.twitter.com/3hZZQgSPaN

Musk’s rejection of MAGA on Wednesday is a stark departure from his attitude over the past two years. In fact, Musk embraced MAGA while campaigning for Trump in 2024, describing himself as “dark MAGA” while wearing a black version of the red hat often donned by the president.

Musk didn’t just make speeches in support of the movement — he jubilantly championed MAGA, jumping wildly on campaign stages in rockstar fashion, with then-candidate Donald Trump alongside him.

His “dark MAGA” persona continued into 2025, when he wore the black cap during appearances at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) and in Oval Office meetings while discussing his work with DOGE.

Musk’s comments come as he has been trying to distance himself from the Trump administration in recent months, even going so far as to say he got “carried away” with the major funding cuts to international programs that he implemented as head of DOGE. Those cuts, experts have noted, could lead to the deaths of 14 million people worldwide, including 4.5 million children, by 2030.

Despite those comments, Musk still spent almost half a billion dollars in support of MAGA-aligned Republicans during the midterms, including an anti-trans ad blitz across multiple states.

Musk may be attempting to distance himself from MAGA with hopes that doing so will prompt Democrats to back away from their promised investigations into his work at DOGE and his companies’ many lucrative contracts with the government — though some Democrats have already publicly told the billionaire that won’t happen.

Musk’s attempts to rebrand himself as anti-MAGA could also stem from his recognition that the movement has run its course. Indeed, recent polling indicates that most Americans are tired of MAGA.

A Quinnipiac University poll in September, for example, found that only 32 percent of Americans remain dedicated to the movement, with 65 percent rejecting it. That poll also found that candidates describing themselves as MAGA did so at their own peril, with 51 percent of voters saying the label made them less likely to vote for a candidate and only 18 percent saying it made them more likely to do so.

A post-midterm poll from Politico also found that nearly one in two MAGA supporters recognize that their movement is dwindling, with 45 percent of those identifying with MAGA agreeing with the idea that they were “losers” in the elections held earlier this month.
