Perpustakaan Anarkis (Indonesia)

The cat is out of the bag now that Lonely Planet knows that Bandung, Indonesia, is a hot spot for punk rock. Over the years, I have discussed my research with different people from all over the world, and many are surprised that punk still exists. Punk is not dead; in fact, it is alive and thriving in the urban centers of Indonesia and has been for some time.

If you are tuned in to the visual cues of punk, it is difficult to wander around Bandung, Jakarta, Denpasar, or any other major city in the country without seeing markers of the scene. Early in my fieldwork, I bumped into some teenagers in the Dago area of Bandung, and one of them was extremely excited that the band shirt I was wearing and the back patch on his jacket were both representing the same obscure punk band from Portland, Oregon. Indeed, the punks in Indonesia are numerous and, as the kid’s fandom exemplified, plugged into the broader global punk rock scene. While punk takes different forms in Indonesia today, I focus on Bandung’s anarcho-punk scene and the global connections they maintain that are predicated on do-it-yourself (DIY) or anarchist principles. This group is redrawing sociopolitical and cultural borders, which is particularly noteworthy in a post-authoritarian nation with an emerging democracy.

Bandung is a sprawling and densely populated city in West Java, situated approximately 90 miles southeast of Jakarta. The city proper has nearly three million inhabitants, while the metropolitan area has nine million residents. Physical remnants of Dutch colonialism in the form of broad boulevards and European architecture have earned the city the moniker “Paris of Java.” Bisected by the Cikapundung River, Bandung sits in a valley surrounded by volcanic peaks. Like all cities in Indonesia, Bandung’s profound income inequalities are hard to miss; corrugated metal shacks bunched together form sprawling communities nestled up alongside opulent malls and high-rise buildings. Bandung is known as something of a college town, as it is home to several major universities, both secular and Islamic. This has attracted people from different backgrounds to Bandung creating a “hip” and cosmopolitan atmosphere against its abject poverty. The Bandung rock scene is embedded in this setting of striking juxtaposition of rich and poor. Although the city is associated with a rapidly evolving youth pop culture, the punk scene has been thriving for some time and well-known bands have been playing for over 20 years.

Anarchist punk does not exist in a vacuum, and punk’s lived realities are complicated by familial, financial, and social expectations. Band members have children and jobs and are situated in complex global power dynamics.

It would be inaccurate to discuss the Bandung punk scene as though it is a cohesive and well-delineated group. From a purely logistical standpoint, Bandung is too large a …

author: Stephen Prager
title: ICJ Finds Myanmar Guilty of Committing Genocide Against Rohingya Muslims
content:
The International Court of Justice for the first time in its 80-year history has found a state responsible for genocide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In a historic ruling, the International Court of Justice on Thursday found Myanmar’s government responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority during its brutal military campaign in 2017.

It is the first time in the ICJ’s 80-year history that it has found a state responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention, with the court ruling in a 9-6 vote that “the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar’s actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part” of the Rohingya population.

ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said the court found that during Myanmar’s military campaign that began in northern Rakhine State in August 2017, “security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers.”

NEWS: @CIJ_ICJ determines Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the 2017 clearance operations in northern Rakhine State.@antonioguterres calls the judgement a demonstration of international justice.https://t.co/1RCbI9g5hb pic.twitter.com/E51EwzIIDf

In the case brought by the West African nation of The Gambia, the court found that the evidence supported UN investigators’ estimate that at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, including women and children. It also showed soldiers committed widespread rape and sexual violence. The ICJ additionally found that Rohingya villages were systematically burned and destroyed while neighboring villages belonging to other ethnic groups were spared. In all, more than 700,000 Rohingya were forced to flee into neighboring Bangladesh.

The court ordered Myanmar to investigate, prosecute, and punish suspects, and enact laws implementing the Genocide Convention to prevent future violations. It also ordered the country to facilitate the voluntary return of displaced Rohingya, help locate missing people, return or replace lost or damaged property, provide rehabilitation for victims, and ensure protection against discrimination. Myanmar must also compensate the Rohingya for harm done with an amount to be determined later, the ICJ said.

The ruling was celebrated by human rights advocates. Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnes Callamard called it “a historic and authoritative recognition of the atrocities committed against the Rohingya and a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families.”

Genocide. The international Court of Justice is fully convinced that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. Complex and well presented lines of arguments on genocidal intent. Many implications for jurisprudence and future trials. Well evidenced and well argued…

She said the ruling “must serve as a wake-up call to the international community” and “must not simply be ignored,” especially since those who committed the atrocities are still in positions of power.

“The man who oversaw a campaign of crimes against humanity and other crimes under international law against the Rohingya, the former head of the armed forces, Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, is now Myanmar’s president following engineered elections,” she said. “Governments should not welcome him on the international stage, especially as grave violations continue unchecked inside Myanmar. Instead, they should stop any transfer of all weapons, security and surveillance equipment, and military and security assistance to Myanmar.”

Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch, said that in addition to being a “long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military,” it also “provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.”

Nimer Sultany, a law professor at the University of London’s School of Oriental and African Studies, said the ruling had massive implications for the December 2023 genocide case brought before the ICJ against Israel over its military campaign in Gaza.

author: David Swanson
title: WBW Takes Part in Annual Conference of Doctors Against Genocide in Washington, D.C.
content:
Asia, Immorality, North America, Videos

By John Reuwer, World BEYOND War, November 19, 2026

Doctors Against Genocide was founded in 2023 by Palestinian American doctors whose family members had long been attacked and displaced in their homeland, and were now being systematically killed by the Israeli invasion of Gaza. They have worked relentlessly since then to alert the medical profession and the public of this grave health and humanitarian crisis. They have been joined by thousands of health care workers and supporters to monitor, document, educate, and advocate for an end to the horror of genocide not only in Palestine, but in Lebanon, Sudan, Congo, Myanmar, and other areas of intense conflict.

We gathered at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C., for three days of reports, analyses, and networking across a broad range of related topics. Here are a few highlights that I witnessed. To view any part of the full, incredibly rich conference, here are the recordings for Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3.

Co-founder and pediatric neurologist Karameh Kuemmerle describes the need for a medical definition of genocide for governments and medical associations to use in order to protect health care workers in areas of violent conflict.

Dr. Mazen Al-Rantisi spoke from the West Bank about his 128 day detention without charges in an Israeli prison. Known in Ramallah as the “doctor of the poor” for his 40 years treating people without regard for their ability to pay, he was abducted from his home at 3:00am and kept in a 2 x 6 meter cell with 10 other inmates sharing one toilet with almost no toilet paper or soap. He describes disturbances day and night, random beatings, and denial of medical care despite serious medical problems and pervasive scabies. The guards seemed to competer with one another to see who could be most cruel. My two days imprisoned on an Israeli floating concentration camp this summer left me no doubt about his testimony.

I led a conversation with two medical colleagues who have been on the front lines challenging ICE agents in the streets and their hospital at considerable cost to their health and careers. This led to making the connections between U.S. government support of Israel in its genocide, and its bringing the techniques of population control for use on its own citizens.

Anthropologist and artist Dana Walrath tells about her study of ten genocides, the latest of which is against the Palestinians. The common beginning is always dehumanization of the target group. Gaza is the first time the horror has been lifestreamed in real time to the screens of anyone paying attention. What does that mean for humanity? Dana expressed her studied impression that there is no evidence for war in most of human prehistory nor an inevitable part of the human condition.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Judge Nominee Won’t Say If He Can Run for President a Third Time
content:
James Sullivan, who refused to say if Trump could run for president again, is currently a Texas Supreme Court justice.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Wednesday, a nominee to a federal judgeship struggled to recall and then refused to answer basic questions about the 22nd Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which stipulates that a person cannot run for a third presidential term if they’ve previously been elected president twice.

James P. Sullivan, who is presently a Texas state Supreme Court justice, lost his reelection bid earlier this month when the state saw a “blue wave” in the midterm elections. Days after his loss, President Donald Trump nominated Sullivan to become a federal judge within the state.

Although Sullivan’s time as a judge was limited — he was appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott (R-Texas) in early 2025 and served just under two years on Texas’s high court after a vacancy occurred — he has a strong legal background rooted in conservatism, having previously served as general counsel to the governor from 2018 to 2025. Sullivan is also a member of the far right Federalist Society.

During his nomination hearing in the Senate on Wednesday, Sullivan refused to answer queries regarding basic constitutional theory and recent history.

When Sen. Chris Coons (D-Delaware) asked him to explain the meaning of the 22nd Amendment, Sullivan appeared to struggle, at one point closing his eyes tightly, as if to focus. After several seconds, Coons gave him a hint: “No person shall be elected…” he began, prompting Sullivan to recall that the amendment bars people from running for a third presidential term.

Coons then asked Sullivan if Trump could run for a third term, citing numerous remarks by the president suggesting he might try to do so. Sullivan refused to answer the question.

“As a nominee for a federal district court, it would be a violation, I believe, of Canon 5 for me to opine on something like that,” Sullivan responded, citing American Bar Association (ABA) standards for nominees for judgeships. He then described the issue as something that “seems like it’s the sort of thing that is the subject of ongoing political debate.”

Coons disagreed, stating that it seems clear that the amendment — and Trump’s suggestions that he could run again — are contradictory.

“The question of whether someone can serve a third term as president of the United States, I think, is only unresolved in the mind of President Trump, who has repeatedly said that he’s thinking he might run for a third time,” Coons explained.

“I don’t believe it is the subject of political debate,” he added.

After the two continued a short back-and-forth on the matter, Coons reiterated his disbelief in Sullivan’s non-answer.

“The amendment is bracingly clear: ‘No person shall be elected to the office of the president more than twice,’” he said. “There is no debate about this, in my view.”

OMG — Trump judicial nominee James P Sullivan (a Texas Supreme Court justice!) reveals he doesn't know what the 22nd amendment says, but then after Chris Coons explains it to him, he refuses to say it'd be illegal for Trump to serve an illegal third term 🤦 pic.twitter.com/YwkDcVa70C

The ABA’s Canon 5 rule does contain a subsection prohibiting “a candidate for judicial office from making statements that commit the candidate regarding cases, controversies or issues likely to come before the court.” However, there is a caveat to that rule that Sullivan appeared to ignore: “As a corollary, a candidate should emphasize in any public statement the candidate’s duty to uphold the law regardless of his or her personal views.”

Had Sullivan responded to Coons’s question on the 22nd Amendment by correctly pointing out that the law forbids Trump from running again, he likely wouldn’t have been in violation of the standard he cited.

Later during the hearing, multiple nominees were asked by Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Connecticut) to recall the events of January 6, 2021, when a mob of loyalists to Trump sought to violently disrupt the proceedings of Congress following Joe Biden’s victory in the 2020 presidential race.

Blumenthal sought to discern whether any of the nominees were “willing to say the Capitol was attacked” on that date. The nominees, including Sullivan, did not respond.

“Nobody? It’s a sad day,” Blumenthal said.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Biden Told Netanyahu He Loved Him in Final Call From White House
content:
Former US president Joe Biden told Benjamin Netanyahu that he loved him on his last call to the Israeli prime minister before leaving office. 


“I still love you, pal”, a transcript of the 15 January 2025 call,

published by the Jerusalem Post,

quotes Biden as saying. “You’re a good man,” he added. “I admire you.”


Biden acted as a key supporter of Israel’s genocide in Gaza while in office, lending direct military, politcal and diplomatic support and overseeing the

transfer of billions of dollars worth of weapons

 to the country. 


In the wake of the 7 October attacks in 2023, Biden repeated false Israeli claims that Hamas had beheaded children, which was seen to bolster Israeli propaganda efforts to justify its massive escalation of war crimes against Gaza’s civilians. 


“I never really thought that I would see, have confirmed, pictures of terrorists beheading children,” Biden said at the time, only for a White House spokesperson to later confirm he had “not seen pictures or confirmed such reports independently”. 


In the January 2025 call, Biden told Netanyahu: “You’ve been through hell. I can’t tell you how much I appreciate you and what you’ve been through,” adding: “I know we’ve disagreed on occasion but, you know… I still love you, pal.”


He added: “I don’t know how you’ve done it all… Next time I think I have a tough job, I’ll think of you… you’re a good man… I admire you. It took a lot of courage to do what you did.”


The transcript stands in contrast to Biden’s comments on Netanyahu in his new memoir, Promise Me, America, which describes the Israeli leader as a “Trump-like” figure “bending democratic institutions to serve his personal needs.”

author: Unknown
title: 8 dicembre-marcia popolare Notav. Contro gli sprechi e per la difesa dei territori
content:
Sono passati

ventun anni

 da quell’

8 dicembre 2005

, quando migliaia di persone tornarono a

Venaus

 per riprendersi i terreni sottratti dopo lo sgombero e l’occupazione militare dei giorni precedenti. Una giornata rimasta impressa nella memoria della Valle di Susa e che ha segnato una

tappa fondamentale nella storia del Movimento No Tav

.


Da Notav Info


Nel corso di tutti questi anni, la questione della

Torino-Lione

 ha assunto una portata che va ben oltre la realizzazione di una linea ferroviaria. Ha mostrato cosa significa imporre un

modello di sviluppo

 che concentra enormi risorse nelle

grandi opere

, consuma territori e risorse e affida al continuo aumento delle infrastrutture e della circolazione delle merci la propria idea di progresso. Una visione che oggi si confronta con una realtà fatta di

impoverimento, precarietà e servizi pubblici sempre più in difficoltà

.


È una contraddizione che attraversa il nostro presente.


Mentre il

carovita

 erode salari e pensioni, il

lavoro precario

 rende sempre più difficile costruire prospettive di vita e

l’accesso alla casa e ai servizi essenziali

 diventa un problema per fasce sempre più ampie della popolazione, si continuano a presentare come inevitabili i

tagli e la mancanza di fondi per sanità, scuola, trasporti e welfare

. Allo stesso tempo, crescono gli

investimenti nel riarmo e nella produzione bellica

, alimentando un’economia che individua nella guerra e nella sua preparazione nuovi settori di espansione.


Non è una questione di risorse che mancano, ma di come vengono distribuite

 e degli interessi a cui vengono destinate. La Torino-Lione è una delle espressioni di queste priorità: un’enorme concentrazione di

denaro pubblico

 per un’opera che sacrifica territori e comunità, mentre rimangono inevase necessità ben più urgenti. Un’opera ormai priva di qualsiasi giustificazione, che si cerca oggi di legittimare riconducendola alle esigenze della

mobilità militare

.


Difendere i territori

 significa allora anche mettere in discussione questo modello, rivendicando un diverso uso delle risorse collettive, riconoscendo come prioritarie la

cura delle persone, dei luoghi, dei beni comuni e rifiutando la guerra

.


La storia della Valle di Susa dimostra che opporsi a questo modello

non è soltanto necessario, ma possibile

. In questi anni abbiamo costruito relazioni, mobilitazioni e forme di partecipazione che hanno saputo andare oltre i confini della nostra Valle. Oggi più che mai davanti a un mondo in fiamme e alle piazze piene sappiamo che questa lotta si innesta nella volontà ampiamente condivisa di

cambiare un sistema ingiusto

 nella distribuzione delle risorse e spietato nella

repressione del dissenso

.


L’8 dicembre torniamo a camminare insieme

, a ventun anni da Venaus, consapevoli che le ragioni di questa lotta continuano a parlare al presente e che la difesa dei territori è parte di una

battaglia più ampia per un futuro diverso

.


Ci vediamo in marcia, contro gli sprechi e per la difesa dei territori!

title: Betriebsratswahlen 2026 vom 1. März bis 31. Mai – warfen braune Schatten voraus
content:
Dossier


„

Von März bis Mai 2026 finden die nächsten Betriebsratswahlen statt. Während in kleineren Betrieben sich die Frage stellt, ob es überhaupt Kandidat:innen gibt, stellt sich in Großbetrieben die Frage, wieviel Listen antreten und wie hoch die Wahlbeteiligung ist. Nur noch 37% der Beschäftigten in Betriebe mit fünf und mehr Mitgliedern haben einen Betriebsrat. (…) Die Entpolitisierung der Gewerkschaften und ihre Anpassung an das kapitalistische Profit- und Konkurrenzsystem haben dazu geführt, dass sich die meisten Betriebsräte als Co-Manager betrachten. In der Krise führte das dazu, dass sie bereit sind, erkämpfte Errungenschaften über Betriebsvereinbarungen – meist völlig undemokratisch ohne Diskussion und Zustimmung der Belegschaft – zu opfern. (…) Die Gefahr besteht, dass sich der Unmut in der Belegschaft bei VW über die von IGM und Betriebsräten mitgetragene Arbeitsplatzvernichtung mit zusätzlichem Lohnverzicht teilweise in Stimmen für das „Zentrum Automobil“ bei den Betriebsratswahlen 2026 ausdrückt

Analyse vom 27. August 2025 bei der Vernetzung für kämpferische Gewerkschaften

Offen bleibt damit, wie betriebliche Konflikte, ökonomische Rahmenbedingungen und gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen die Wahlkampfführung prägen und welche Strategien betriebliche Akteurinnen zur Mobilisierung und Repräsentation der Beschäftigten entwickeln. (…) Was wurde getan, um die Wahlen zu nutzen, um die demokratische Verankerung und die Repräsentant:innen betrieblicher Interessenvertretungen zu stärken? Welche Probleme traten auf und wie wurde Union Busting sowie Zentrum- und AfD-Propaganda begegnet? Was folgte daraus in Bezug auf Strategien einer langfristigen und nachhaltigen Entwicklung von Mitbestimmung und gewerkschaftlicher Interessenvertretung im Betrieb?.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya, UN’s Top Court Rules
content:
Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during a scorched-earth military campaign in Rakhine state, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled. 


Judges at the UN’s highest court reached the historic verdict on Thursday, with nine voting in favour and six voting against. They also ruled by ten votes to five that Myanmar must adopt “measures of restitution”. 


It is the first time the court has ruled that a state is fully responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention.


Myanmar’s military launched what it claimed were “clearance operations” against the Muslim minority group in 2017, razing entire villages to the ground while committing mass killings and gang rapes. 


Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya were forced across the border to Bangladesh, where they remain confined to camps in squalid conditions. 


Authorities in Myanmar have blocked investigations and carried out “extensive destruction of evidence” crimes by burning and disposing of bodies, Judge Iwasawa said during the ruling. The case was initiated by The Gambia in 2019. 


Crowds of people celebrated at one refugee camp on Thursday as they watched the verdict being delivered on a small screen, the BBC reported.


But Nay San Lwin, a prominent Rohingya activist,

told Al Jazeera

 that a court verdict alone would not bring “meaningful justice”, which required “recognition of our identity, restoration of our rights, justice for every victim and the opportunity to return to our homeland safely, rebuild our lives, and live in peace and dignity.”


Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch, said: “The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.


“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.” 


The UK government last month

hosted representatives of Myanmar’s dictatorship

, which critics said would give the military junta an opportunity to launder its image. 


“The British government has been gradually softening its approach towards the Myanmar military regime, but hopefully this will stiffen their spines,” Mark Farmaner, director of the Burma Campaign UK pressure group, told Novara Media. 


“There have been no new sanctions rounds for two years,” he added, “and aid to the Rohingya has fallen… Myanmar has been pretty much forgotten.”

author: Mag
title: Automobilarbeiter:innen in China: Den Blick vom internationalen Konkurrenzkampf der Autoindustrie auf die Situation der Beschäftigten richten
content:
Dossier


„

Arbeitsbedingte Muskel-Skelett-Erkrankungen sind zu einem der größten Gesundheitsprobleme am Arbeitsplatz geworden. Viele Automobilarbeiter in China sind WMSDs  [Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs)] ausgesetzt. (…) Hondas chinesisches Joint Venture entlässt 900 Leiharbeiter (…) „Fabrikjobs werden oft mit den ‚drei D’s‘ assoziiert – „dirty, dangerous and demeaning“ (schmutzig, gefährlich und entwürdigend) (…) Jüngere Chinesen empfinden es als erniedrigend“, sagte sie. „Sich wie eine Maschine zu fühlen, ist für sie nicht sinnvoll.“ (…) Im Februar hängten Arbeiter bei WM Motor Transparente auf, beriefen sich auf das chinesische Arbeitsrecht und forderten eine wirtschaftliche Entschädigung für ihre Entlassungen. Im April protestierten die Beschäftigten von Tianji Motors gegen nicht gezahlte Löhne und Sozialversicherungsbeiträge, und im Juli protestierten die Beschäftigten von Baoneng Motors gegen Lohnrückstände

…“

Überblick vom 12.3.2024 im Forum Arbeitswelten


 mit Fotos und zum Thema:


Entlassungen bei Automobilzulieferer Xingyu Automotive in China: Neue Wege des Widerstands in globalen Lieferketten


„

Im August 2026 geriet die Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems Company (im Folgenden »Xingyu«), ein führender chinesischer Zulieferbetrieb für die globale


Autoindustrie, in den Mittelpunkt einer heftigen öffentlichen Kontroverse: Das Unternehmen hatte die Arbeitsverträge von 107 Hochschulabsolvent:innen aufgelöst, nur wenige Wochen, nachdem diese ihre Stellen angetreten hatten. Aus dem betriebsinternen Arbeitskonflikt wurde rasch eine umfassende Debatte in der chinesischen Öffentlichkeit über Unternehmensführung und die Einhaltung von Vorschriften und Standards in der Lieferkette. International erhielt die Auseinandersetzung Beachtung, als Volkswagen eine Untersuchung des Falls ankündigte. Er steht damit exemplarisch für das Zusammenspiel von angespanntem chinesischem Arbeitsmarkt, Kapitalmarktkontrolle in globalen Produktionsnetzwerken, unternehmerischem Kostendruck, Arbeitnehmerrechten und der Forderung nach Regelkonformität in globalen Lieferketten. Der Fall zeigt auch, dass Arbeitsplatzabbau und Entlassungen in der Automobilindustrie nicht nur in Ländern des westlichen Kapitalismus, sondern in globalem Maßstab stattfinden, und China trotz seiner wachsenden Exportstärke keineswegs eine Ausnahme ist. Der folgende Bericht untersucht den Fall Xingyu entlang dieser miteinander verflochtenen Dimensionen

…“

Artikel von Hugo Lobpreis

express – Zeitung für sozialistische Betriebs- und Gewerkschaftsarbeit

Die Automobilarbeiter in China bleiben kämpferisch: Erneuter Streik für höhere Löhne im BYD-Werk in Changsha


„Eine unscheinbare Kurzmeldung im China Labour Bulletin: „Die Streiks im BYD-Werk in Changsha im Jahr 2023 wegen niedriger Löhne und gekürzter Überstunden sind ein Muster, das sich mit ähnlichen Aktionen in den Jahren 2024 und 2025 fortsetzt. Die wiederholten Kürzungen von Überstunden bei BYD lösen immer wieder Widerstand aus. Am 20.4.2025: Arbeiter legen kollektiv die Arbeit nieder, um höhere Löhne in einer BYD-Fabrik in Changsha in der Porovinz Hunan zu fordern.“ Es ist interessant zu erfahren, daß es im Werk Changsha bereits eine Tradition an Arbeitskampfen gibt und die Unruhe unter den Beschäftigten in der chinesischen Autoindustrie nicht beendet ist. Die Mehrheit der Arbeitskämpfe in China werden von einbehaltenen Löhnen, Entlassungen und nicht ausgezahlten Abfindungen ausgelöst, doch in dem Arbeitskampf bei BYD Changsha geht es um die Höhe der Löhne.“


Meldung und Übersetzung von Karsten vom 2. Mai 2025 im forum arbeitswelten

author: Unknown
title: Riflessioni di alcune giovani italiane sullo sciopero generale dell’11 di novembre a Barcellona
content:
Riceviamo e pubblichiamo un racconto sulla giornata di sciopero a Barcellona da parte di alcune compagne che vivono lì.


Mezzanotte dell’11 di novembre, qualche secondo dopo l’inizio dello sciopero generale per la casa. Nel cielo di Barcellona compaiono fuochi d’artificio da vari punti della città, seguiti da cori e canti, per festeggiare l’inizio della giornata. 


La libertá è quando comincia l’alba in una giornata di sciopero generale

 dice una strofa di una poesia di Joan Margarit, che circola nei giorni precedenti.  Qualche ora dopo, verso le 3.30/4, escono di casa lə primə compagnə per raggiungere a piedi i primi blocchi stradali delle principali arterie viarie della Catalogna. 

A Barcellona i principali obiettivi sono le varie 

ronde

, tangenziali con una funzione simile al raccordo anulare romano, che abbracciano tutta la cittá. Il livello di tensione con lə conduttricə di moto e macchine, determinatə a raggiungere i propri posti di lavoro, sono delle piú variegate. Nella 

ronda del mig

 a Lesseps tutto procede senza particolari problemi; ad uno dei tagli della 

ronda litoral

lə manifestantə, bardatə, si stendono sull’asfalto per dormire e recuperare le poche ore di sonno. In vari punti della Catalogna le macchine investono lə scioperanti procurando feritə; molte sono lə manifestantə che, visto il grande numero di persone, si autogesticono e separano per bloccare altre uscite o entrate della stessa arteria. Le reazioni sono delle piú diverse, tra chi tira fuori la sdraio felice di non andare a lavorare a chi ha un crollo psicotico quasi gritando tra le lacrime: “E il mio diritto di andare a lavorare dov’è? Io muoio se non vado a lavorare!”. Rispettando una buona tradizione catalana, quella de 

elfoc i la rauxa

, i primi fuochi della giornata riempono l’aria periferica barcellonina, bloccando persino l’entrata di zone logistiche strategiche come quella di Mercabarna e del porto di Barcellona.


L’adesione allo sciopero è storica, l’84% secondo le principali sigle sindacali. In Spagna non si vedeva uno sciopero generale cosí da almeno quattordici anni. 

Nonostante il tempo passato, si nota la tradizione 

vaguista

 della città con un programma giá ben collaudato: blocchi stradali a prime ore dell’alba, poi, mentre alcuni di questi si mantengono fino all’ora di pranzo come a Lesseps, iniziano i picchetti informativi (e meno informativi) per i vari quartieri. È evidente una differenza molto grande tra gli scioperi italiani e quelli di Barcellona. Qui la storia sindacale è molto differente. Mentre in Italia una delle tradizioni politiche piú forti, quelle dell’autonomia, nasce propriamente come movimento extraparlamentare e contro i principali sindacati (basta pensare alla ben nota cacciata di Lama alla Sapienza), qui sindacati come la CNT hanno avuto un ruolo centrale giá dalla resistenza antifranchista nel ‘36 . Oggi rilevante è soprattutto il ruolo della CGT, nata da una scissione della CNT, che mantiene viva la tradizione di sindacalismo anarchico e combattivo.


Se negli scioperi di dimensioni minori, come quelli per la Palestina, l’obiettivo dei 

cercavila

 di quartiere erano le filiali delle note multinazionali pro-israele, nella giornata dell’11 sono stati segnalati tutti i negozi aperti al grido di 

esquirol

 (crumiro). 


A Gràcia, quartiere ribelle fino a 10 anni fa ed oggi mangiato dagli expats e svuotato della maggior parte delle sue occupazioni, ci sono tre diversi picchetti che si muovono avanti e indietro per le strade principali, costringendo a chiudere piú o meno gentilmente ogni serranda. Piano piano gli animi si vanno scaldando e la fantasia cresce: piante ornamentali di hotel tirate per terra, farina sulle casse dei supermercati, immondizia all’entrata dei negozi, scritte, manifesti e pressioni in ogni porta illuminata o aperta. I lavoratori lasciano le proprie attivitá con piú o meno buona volontá, la maggior parte chiudono poco prima che arrivi la piccola manifestazione, alcuni si nascodono al buio mentre altri litigano e si confrontano con lə manifestantə, a cui viene tirata farina, uova e costretto con la forza a chiudere il negozio. Vengono risparmiate farmacie e altri servizi minimi, particolare accanimento avviene contro i negozi piú gentrificatori. Un lavoratore, mentre trasporta un pallet di prodotti a un supermercato, scappa alla vista del picchetto e i prodotti vengono distribuiti tra tuttə, dal succo ai pannolini. In altri quartieri il confronto è piú violento …

title: Autozulieferer GKN schliesst Florentiner Werk und setzt 450 Familien auf die Strasse – nun besetzt für Eigenproduktion
content:
Dossier


“

GKN, ein britisches multinationales Unternehmen, das Achswellen für mehrere Automobilhersteller produziert, hat heute Freitag, den 9. Juli 2021 die Arbeiter*innen über die sofortige Schliessung des Standorts Campi Bisenzio in der Provinz Florenz informiert. 450 Arbeiter*innen verlieren somit von einem Tag auf den anderen ihren Job. Die Kommunikation über die Betriebsschliessung erfolgte über eine interne E-Mail an die Arbeiter*innen; die Öffentlichkeit konnte in einem Facebook-Post der Metallarbeiter*innengewerkschaft FIOM darüber lesen. (…) Die Massenentlassung bei GKN ist ein weiterer Fall von Kündigungen, die unmittelbar nach Abschluss der Vereinbarung zwischen Regierung, Gewerkschaften und Unternehmensverband Confindustria Ende Juni 2021 erfolgt..

.” Aus dem Beitrag von Maurizio Coppola vom 9.7.2021 – wir danken! Siehe den Volltext ganz unten und weitere Informationen zur nachfolgenden Fabrikbesetzung und Selbstorganisierung:


Ehemaliges GKN-Fabrikgelände wird gemeinnützig


„

Mehr als fünf Jahre kämpfte das Fabrikkollektiv ex GKN für die Konversion der GKN-Fabrik, einem Autozulieferbetrieb, und damit auch gegen ihre Entlassung und die Vernichtung von Arbeitsplätzen. (…) Ende September 2026 beschloss das Industriekonsortium schließlich, dass das ehemalige GKN-Fabrikgelände in Campi Bisenzio bei Florenz gemeinnützig werden soll. (…) Bei der Genossenschaftsversammlung am 12. Juli 2026 stimmten die Mitglieder einstimmig für den neuen GFF-Geschäftsplan. Teil davon ist auch die Entscheidung, sich mit der permanenten Betriebsversammlung vor das Fabrikgelände zurückzuziehen und dafür die Auszahlung der Löhne zu erreichen. (…) GFF ist jetzt in der Lage, ohne das Industriekonsortium die Lastenradproduktion aufzubauen. Dafür wurde eine leerstehende Fabrik angemietet. Der Zeitplan sieht vor, dass im Januar mit der Produktion der Räder begonnen werden kann. Die Arbeiter:innen lassen sich im Bereich Lastenrad- und auch Photovoltaikmontage schulen. Die Produktion von Photovoltaikmodulen und das Recycling werden allerdings erst später folgen

.“

Artikel von Kathy Ziegler

 

 in

express – Zeitung für sozialistische Betriebs- und Gewerkschaftsarbeit

 11/2026


Das Fabrikkollektiv ex-GKN hat die Fabrik für permanente Versammlung davor geräumt – bis die neuen Eigentümer*innen mit dem Plan eines Logistikzentrums auf dem Gelände scheitern…


„

Die Arbeiter*innen halten jetzt vor dem Tor der ex-GKN-Fabrik in Campi Bisenzio ihre permanente Versammlung ab. Sie haben ein Zelt und Solarpaneele aufgebaut und ein Café eingerichtet.

Hier ein paar Eindrücke vom Geschehen vor dem Fabriktor


. Das Interesse an ihrem Kampf ist ungebrochen: Arbeiter*innen von der Baustelle nebenan kommen vorbei, um sich auszutauschen und im Zelt einen Kaffee zu trinken. Leute, die im nahegelegenen Einkaufszentrum shoppen, machen einen Zwischenstopp für einen kurzen Schnack und ein Getränk.


Der neue Besitzer der Fabrik hat die Räumung der Fabrik zur Bedingung gemacht, um den Arbeitern ihre ausstehenden Löhne zu zahlen. Die ausstehenden Löhne belaufen sich auf 16 Millionen Euro. Da es auch um die Löhne derjenigen geht, die den Kampf schon lange verlassen haben und da das Fabrikkollektiv diese nicht gegen sich aufbringen will, haben die ex-GKN Arbeiter beschlossen, die Fabrik zu räumen. Alle Gerichte haben bestätigt, dass die ausstehenden Löhne den Arbeitern in voller Höhe ausgezahlt werden müssen. In der Fabrik sind Maschinen und Materialien vom Gerichtsvollzieher mit Pfändungssiegeln versehen worden, um die Zahlungen zu garantieren.


Die vom Fabrikkollektiv gegründete Genossenschaft ex GKN FOR FUTURE (GFF) hat in den letzten Monaten über eine Million Euro gesammelt. 300.000 davon kommen von Unterstützer*innen aus Deutschland. Mit dem Geld soll die Produktion von Lastenrädern und die Montage, das Recycling und die Produktion von Solarpaneelen finanziert werden. Die Genossenschaft wird voraussichtlich zum 1. Januar 2027 mit der Produktion von Lastenrändern beginnen. Produktionsstätte wird eine ehemalige Metallbaufabrik mit funktionsfähigen Schweißanlagen und weiteren Maschinen am Stadtrand von Florenz, knapp 10 Minuten entfernt. Das Fabrikkollektiv übernimmt zudem zwei ARCI Vereinslokale im Zentrum und am Stadtrand von Florenz: Casa Caciolle und San Bartolo. Dort werden sie, wie bisher, kulturelle und politische Veranstaltungen organisieren.


Die Genossenschaftsversamlung

author: Daron Letts
title: Kotierks win $10,000 on ‘Family Feud Canada’
content:
Knowing that ketchup-flavoured potato chips are the most likely type to turn your fingers red earned an Iqaluit family the chance to win $10,000 on CBC’s

Family Feud Canada

.


The Kotierk family won the game show’s top prize in Wednesday night’s episode.


“It was a lot of fun to watch,” said team captain Kunuk Kotierk during a phone interview Thursday morning. “We had a good laugh.”


He and four relatives went head-to-head against the Jean family from Calgary.


The game show format pits two families against each other to guess the answers to surveys of 100 people. The first family to get 300 points wins a chance to go for $10,000 in the Fast Money round. That’s where two contestants have to guess the answers to five survey questions as a clock ticks down.


Each Kotierk family member wore a colourful atigi, some with ulu prints, sewn by Kunuk Kotierk’s aunt Emily Joanasie.


Kunuk Kotierk won the opening buzzer faceoff against the Jeans by answering

 “the best way to insult a Canadian is to talk badly about blank” with “their hockey team.”


His opponent said “their mother.”


Survey said Kunuk Kotierk had the top answer.


Host Gerry Dee took a moment to chat with the Kotierks following the first round, which the Jeans had won.


Dee asked Jessica Kotierk, manager and curator of Iqaluit’s Nunatta Sunakkutaangit Museum, about some of the artifacts on display.


“The most popular part is the walrus penis bone,” she said.


After the audience laughter died down, Dee replied that she should host the show.


The rest of the game was close and it all came down to a sudden-death showdown which Kunuk Kotierk’s uncle, South Baffin MLA David Joanasie, won. He buzzed in first and correctly named the potato chip flavour most likely to turn your hands red — ketchup.


Kunuk Kotierk and Jessica Kotierk danced in the centre of the stage after the win.


The family went on to win the Fast Money round, earning them the $10,000 and the opportunity to return the next night and compete against another family.


“The next one’s my favourite episode,” Kunuk Kotierk said. “It will keep people on the edge of their seat. I hope everyone has fun watching round two.”


As for the prize money, Kunuk Kotierk said some of his family are discussing trips or new clothing, but he hasn’t decided what he will do with his share.


Their next episode airs at 7:30 p.m. Thursday on CBC. It is also watchable on the CBC Gem app.


The episodes were

prerecorded

 in Toronto in late August.

author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: Quase todas as cidades já sofrem com eventos extremos. O que farão os prefeitos?
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Mal terminou a eleição presidencial e arrisco dizer que a política climática vai ocupar um espaço inédito daqui até as próximas eleições. Enquanto os temas econômicos e em especial o ajuste fiscal domina a agenda de Brasília, a dura realidade das mudanças climáticas vai se impondo em nosso cotidiano. São inúmeros episódios de cidades isoladas pela seca na Amazônia e tempestades deixando prejuízos no Sul e no Sudeste. Sem falar nas lavouras de soja e milho penando no Centro-Oeste.


Essa percepção de que a escolha para prefeitos e vereadores vai ditar os rumos da política é reforçada com a publicação dos

resultados da última pesquisa de informações básicas municipais do IBGE

, a Munic.

O levantamento mostra um crescimento no número de municípios afetados por eventos extremos climáticos. Já chega a 49,5% a quantidade de cidades brasileiras impactadas por alagamentos entre 2021 e 2024, sendo que na pesquisa anterior essa porcentagem era de 35%. Quando falamos de secas, é ainda pior: 59% dos municípios relataram falta de água.


No resultado agregado, é impressionante ver que apenas 385 dos 5,5 mil municípios brasileiros responderam não ter sofrido qualquer tipo de evento climático extremo.

Isso significa que

93% tiveram problemas

 nos últimos anos.

 Me pergunto como estão, neste momento, os prefeitos preparando-se para enfrentar a pior fase do Super El Niño. Provavelmente não estão. Será que os cortes de gastos federais esperados com o ajuste fiscal poderão afetar a capacidade dos municípios de adaptação aos efeitos das mudanças climáticas?


Estamos às portas do verão. É o verão que se segue ao mais quente já ocorrido na Europa. Os dados sobre o impacto das ondas de calor que passaram por lá são impressionantes: uma primeira estimativa indica que

o calor extremo causou a morte de 50 mil pessoas

 nos países da União Europeia. Há uma trágica previsão de que 13,3 mil brasileiros, especialmente do Norte e Nordeste, podem morrer por conta do calor extremo causado pelo Super El Niño, de acordo com relatório do Laboratório de Impacto Climático da Universidade de Chicago,

divulgado em setembro

.


Se ondas de calor se repetirem por aqui, a infra-estrutura das cidades precisa estar pronta para lidar com a realidade de um influxo de pessoas aos postos de saúde. Vejam que já tem sido um desafio lidar com o impacto da poluição por queimadas este ano em grandes cidades da Amazônia, como Manaus e Santarém. Crianças e idosos sempre são os mais afetados.


Há algumas semanas, também foram

publicadas avaliações inéditas

 sobre o impacto do calor e dos eventos extremos na saúde das mulheres.

Em muitos países, são as mulheres que estão nas funções mais expostas ao calor extremo, seja na agricultura ou em subempregos sem qualidade alguma e sem qualquer direito ao descanso.

 Além disso, o aumento da temperatura tem impacto direto na saúde das mulheres grávidas e das mães. Afetadas pela instabilidade causada pelos eventos extremos, eles são vítimas de mais violência, mais desigualdade.


Mais calor também representa mais casos de gravidez de risco, com abortos espontâneos e nascimentos premataturos. É alentador saber que já existe no mundo uma rede formada por profissionais de saúde para se preparam para as mudanças climáticas. Recentemente, fiquei impressionado ao conhecer a iniciativa HERA, totalmente dedicada a apoiar mulheres impactadas pelo calor extremo. Um dos instrumentos que utiliza é

prover um seguro gratuito para mães de baixa renda

. Algo que lhes permite sobreviver a impactos como perda de emprego e quebra de safra.


Precisamos de respostas concretas


Como se vê, os eventos extremos climáticos levam a política ao nível mais básico, exigindo respostas concretas. A mudança climática já é e será ainda mais debatida como uma questão de justiça social. Sabemos que, nos momentos de crise, como foi durante a pandemia da Covid-19, são os mais pobres que sofrem as piores consequências. Agora, quando vemos a urgente necessidade de adaptação às mudanças climáticas, a desigualdade também fica em evidência. Há gente rica comprando terra com nascentes de água e planejando autossuficiência, em alarmante sinal de racismo ambiental. Precisamos de um poder público que nos proteja contra a sanha privatista.

Democrat Mary Peltola was declared the winner this week of Alaska’s closely watched race for U.S. Senate, making her the first Alaska Native lawmaker elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, we speak with Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford, an Inupiaq and Yup’ik organizer from Unalakleet, Alaska. She says Peltola’s win is a significant milestone for Indigenous peoples in Alaska.

“Having somebody represent us in such a large capacity with such a big weight on her shoulders, but still carrying that struggle with her as she continues to advocate for our people and our way of life, is monumental,” says Blatchford.

Peltola is Yup’ik Alaskan and will be the first Indigenous woman from Alaska elected to the U.S. Senate. This is Mary Peltola thanking supporters on Tuesday.

SEN.-ELECT MARY PELTOLA: Alaskans have voted for change, and I’m so honored to be your next U.S. senator. AMY GOODMAN: Mary Peltola campaigned in many difficult situations and places to reach communities across Alaska that are often overlooked in elections. One in five Alaska voters are Indigenous.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Nunavut Arctic College to offer its own teaching degree
content:
Nunavut Arctic College is expected to offer its own credited bachelor of education program next fall.


“We have the skills, we have the knowledge, we have the administrative mechanisms to support the program,” said president Jackie Price in an interview. “So it’s time.”


The college’s current equivalent is offered in partnership with Memorial University in Newfoundland and Labrador, through a program that allows students to complete their studies remotely from Nunavut. Prior versions of the program included the University of Regina and McGill University in Montreal.


Due to funding restraints, the college will offer the new program in Iqaluit and up to four other communities to start, though its administration is still assessing which ones, Price said.


In 2021, the college received more than $34 million for its education program, through a five-year agreement between Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. and the territorial and federal governments.


That money allowed the program to expand to 21 communities through remote learning, Price said. But the funding has run out.


The news comes at a time when the Government of Nunavut is hiring more unqualified teachers, who don’t have formal training as teachers.


The number of teachers approved to work in the territory without a bachelor of education or equivalent degree nearly doubled since 2021, from 54 to 93 this school year, figures shared by the Education Department indicate.


“That’s over 10 per cent of our membership right now that’s unqualified. We would not accept 10 per cent of our nurses to be unqualified,” Nunavut Teachers’ Association president Justin Matchett said in an interview.


He said he hopes the new program will change that.


“We need to strive for quality education for everybody here,” Matchett said.


Education Minister David Akeeagok said in a written statement the number of unqualified teachers in Nunavut concerns him.


While only those with bachelor of education degrees would, ideally, staff classrooms, he said that unqualified teachers receive training and have other meaningful qualifications, such as Inuktitut proficiency.


“Nunavut faces longstanding and well-known challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified teachers, exacerbated by the shortage of teachers across Canada,” he said.

title: "This Is Not Going Well": COP31 Draft Text Avoids Fossil Fuel Phaseout, Bets on "Magic Technologies"
content:
As we continue our week of broadcasts from the global United Nations climate conference known as COP31, we get an update on the formal negotiations from German activist Luisa Neubauer. The

latest draft text

 of the key climate commitments that countries are debating has dropped language about phasing out fossil fuels, but it does include an emphasis on carbon capture and storage — a largely unproven technology that critics say cannot be deployed at scale to curb emissions.


“We have much better solutions at hand, like renewables,” says Neubauer. “This is not going well. We are not doing fine. And if anything, after this conference ends, we need people to take the streets and fight for more justice out there.”

Aire de Santa Fe

Este es el pliego de revindicaciones:


La exigencia de un

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: A New International Order? Xi, Trump & Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in China
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted his U.S. and Russian counterparts for a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, with the leaders of the three biggest nuclear superpowers meeting for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen. Afterward, the countries published a “peace declaration” that affirmed “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.” The declaration also announced a commitment to increase petroleum production, called for reforms at the United Nations and urged the International Criminal Court and similar bodies to “not abuse their jurisdiction.”


While in China, President Donald Trump also had a separate meeting with President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war in Ukraine, though it’s unclear if they made any progress.


“It’s a significant post-1945 moment, which was the last time that we had great summits,” says Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin. “What is the most important takeaway … is an ascendant China. It was China that really set the terms of what was said.”

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Hasan Piker Aims to Raise $1m for Anti-ICE Groups With GTA 6 Livestream
content:
US Twitch streamer and leftwing political commentator Hasan Piker has launched a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed fundraiser for two pro-migrant rights groups – aiming to raise $1m (£759,000).


​Piker, who


began playing

 the hugely anticipated game as it launched at midnight on Thursday,

 has already

raised over $82,000

 from the multi-day “GTA 6: Melt the ICE” campaign.  


If the fundraiser reaches $1m, Piker has pledged to give himself a “Zohran Moustache”, after the New York City mayor unveiled new facial hair earlier this month for Movember.  


The money will be split between the Los Angeles-based


Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights

 (Chirla) and the


National Immigration Law Center

 (NILC). Both organisations have played key roles in securing legal protections for migrants and opposing abductions and other abuses by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).


“NILC and Chirla… are helping the most vulnerable that have been targeted by ICE get legal representation, rapid responses for ICE raids, lobbying congress for change and much much more,” the stream’s fundraiser page on Tiltify says.


​Piker, who was


banned from entering the UK in June

 over his opposition to Israel’s genocide in Gaza,


raised over $1m

 in October 2023 for Palestinian medical aid. Earlier the same year, he raised $1.2m for relief efforts following earthquakes in Turkey, where he spent his childhood, and Syria.


Ahead of the GTA 6 launch on Wednesday, Piker wrote on X: “I never experienced Xmas, since we don’t have it in Turkey but I assume this is the closest one can feel to being a child on Xmas eve. I cannot wait for GTA6”.


At one point during the livestream, Piker encountered a satirical radio show parodying far-right commentators Alex Jones and Nick Fuentes.


“I will admit I’m a little bit sad,” he said, reacting to the gameplay. “I really wish I was getting dunked on by Rockstar.”  


The new release has been described as the most widely anticipated video game ever, and may even be


the biggest entertainment launch

 in history, having made

$1.65bn in pre-order sales

 alone.

title: Women's Peace Monitoring Commission established in Istanbul
content:
The Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission announced its establishment following preparatory meetings involving approximately 100 women.


The commission announced its establishment at a press conference held at the Kadın Zamanı Association. It aims to be represented on the Independent Monitoring Board to be established under the framework law adopted by Parliament. Representatives of women's organisations and many other women attended the meeting, where participants chanted the slogan "Jin, jiyan, azadî" (Woman, Life, Freedom).


The statement emphasised that lasting peace requires more than an end to conflict. It also involves confronting the past, uncovering the truth, ensuring justice and rebuilding society.


The statement drew attention to the impact of war, forced displacement and losses experienced across generations on women, stressing that women's equal participation and authority in decision-making mechanisms are fundamental to lasting peace.


The statement noted that women experience war and conflict in different ways, including imprisonment, poverty, male violence, labour exploitation and displacement, but that these experiences are often made invisible in peace processes. The commission stressed the need for independent monitoring of the process from a gender equality perspective.


The commission said that its first priority would be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595, adopted by Parliament, and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the parliamentary commission's report.


The statement continued: "Following a meeting involving approximately 100 women, we decided to move forward as the Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission. We hereby announce the establishment of our commission. We are still at the beginning of this journey. Our first priority will be to monitor the implementation of Framework Law No. 7595 adopted by Parliament, the rationale behind the law and the recommendations contained in Sections 6 and 7 of the commission's report, as well as the legal and political steps necessary to resolve the Kurdish question and democratise Turkey. We aim to monitor these steps, the laws enacted and the mechanisms established, their impact on everyday life, the obstacles they face, their shortcomings, what remains undone and what is made invisible, through women's eyes and drawing on the experience of the women's freedom struggle. We also aim to make our voices heard on these issues. We believe it is essential to exert pressure in favour of peace wherever the necessary steps are not taken. In this process, we need to speak out more, not remain silent. We will do this through reports, visits, monitoring delegations, various subcommissions and other methods we develop together, and we will regularly share our findings with the public. Above all, we call on all women to monitor this process with us and join the commission at every stage. Let us take responsibility together for building an equal and lasting peace. We remind those in positions of decision-making authority: We are watching you. We women will hold you accountable for peace!"

author: Unknown
title: Evin Zapsu's lawyer: Evin is in severe pain and needs treatment
content:
The health condition of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, who is held at Kayseri Bünyan Women's Closed Prison and was diagnosed with cancer on 16 November, remains critical. Biopsy results and other medical examinations revealed stage four uterine cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. Despite repeated calls for her release, Evin Zapsu remains imprisoned.


Relatives of ill prisoners have called for their release outside the Ministry of Justice, while Evin Zapsu's lawyer, Berivan Çelik, spoke to ANF about her client's health and the latest developments.


'Evin is suffering from severe pain'


Berivan Çelik said that Evin Zapsu remained in good spirits despite trying to conceal the pain, swelling and physical changes. Çelik said that doctors had informed Evin Zapsu, who was diagnosed with stage four uterine cancer with metastases, that she urgently needed surgery. She warned that further delays in treatment could leave her client dependent on others for care.


The lawyer said that she met Evin Zapsu face to face at the prison last Tuesday and witnessed her deteriorating health firsthand.


Despite taking two strong painkillers, Evin Zapsu was visibly suffering from severe pain and had significant abdominal swelling and other physical changes. Çelik said that her client remained in good spirits but was trying to conceal her suffering.


Berivan Çelik said: "Although she had taken two strong painkillers before coming to our meeting, it was very clear that she was in pain, even though she tried not to show it. Nevertheless, her spirits were high and she was smiling. She believed that even if her test results were bad, she would be able to overcome the illness without too much difficulty."


Report concludes that she can remain in prison


Berivan Çelik said that an earlier medical assessment had concluded that her client could remain in prison. Three days after they submitted a request for the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin Zapsu was taken to Kayseri City Hospital, where a medical board prepared a report.


Çelik said that the report concluded that Evin Zapsu was fit to remain in prison, while subsequent biopsy results revealed the severity of her illness.


Çelik also said: "Three days after we first requested the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin was taken to Kayseri City Hospital. A medical board report was prepared at the hospital, and the report issued last Monday concluded that she could remain in prison. However, the biopsy results revealed stage four uterine cancer with metastases.


We therefore submitted another application today. We have not yet received a written response to our previous request. No decision approving or rejecting our application has been communicated to us."


'The masses have spread to her chest and armpits'


Berivan Çelik also referred to radiological imaging and CT scan results, saying that her client's health had deteriorated since the first scans were carried out in August.


Çelik said that masses initially detected in the abdominal area had spread over time and that new masses had developed.


Çelik also said: "The initial radiological scans showed masses only in her abdomen. She told us that these masses had gradually spread upwards towards her chest and that new masses had begun to appear in her armpits. We have the radiological images, CT scans, their reports and the biopsy results.


When we compare the reports from August with her current condition, we can see that the masses have increased considerably and are causing much more pain."


Berivan Çelik said that the doctor who examined her client had told her that she urgently needed surgery to remove the masses. She explained that following the initial pathology results, she and Evin Zapsu's family had consulted an oncology specialist on the basis of the scans taken in August.


Although the specialist provided a verbal opinion, they were unable to obtain a written assessment. Following the biopsy results, they submitted a new application.


Çelik said that they attached the biopsy results to their second petition and stressed that treatment must begin immediately.


'Treatment is not possible under prison conditions'


Berivan Çelik also described the health problems her client faces in prison, saying that the cold conditions force her to sleep with hot-water bottles and that she spends most of her time in bed because of the pain.

title: Janet Biehl: Democratic integration should guide the peace process
content:
American writer and social ecology thinker Janet Biehl, in an assessment she wrote on Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 February 2025 Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, emphasised the importance of democratic and legal steps for advancing the peace process in Turkey.


Statements and letters prepared as part of an international solidarity campaign launched with the participation of 97 intellectuals will be published as an English-language e-book by Daraja Press.


Janet Biehl’s foreword to the book, entitled “The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, was also conveyed to the Imrali Delegation.


In her article, Janet Biehl said that the Framework Law adopted by Parliament was of vital importance for advancing the process. She said that, following confirmation by the National Security Council of the PKK’s disarmament steps, the way could be paved for the reintegration into social life of political prisoners and some PKK members living abroad.


However, Janet Biehl emphasised that, alongside the implementation of the legal framework, additional confidence-building measures were also necessary. In this regard, she outlined a number of demands, including clarifying Abdullah Öcalan’s status, ending the appointment of trustees, releasing political prisoners, guaranteeing the healthcare rights of sick prisoners, and lifting restrictions on Kurdish political activities and the media.


She also identified the release of Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as guarantees allowing PKK members who lay down their arms to participate in politics, as necessary steps.


A pluralistic and democratic society


Biehl said that the assessments made by other intellectuals featured in the book also set out the objectives of the peace process. Key themes emerging from these contributions include a multi-ethnic political system, the coexistence of peoples on equal terms, the democratisation of the nation-state and the construction of a pluralistic society.


Referring also to Abdullah Öcalan’s principle of “democratic integration”, Biehl highlighted the importance of establishing a system in which different peoples can coexist within a shared political sphere, free from relations of domination.


Biehl concluded her foreword with the following words: “I hope that these voices and ideas will serve as guiding lights for the peace process over the coming months and years.”


Janet Biehl


Janet Biehl is an American writer, translator and social ecology thinker. Having worked alongside Murray Bookchin for many years, she is known for her work on social ecology, libertarian municipalism and democratic confederalism.

author: Daniel Avalos
title: Residentes en movilización por el descuido de quienes nos cuidan
content:
Residentes de hospitales de Nación, Provincia de Buenos Aires y CABA realizaron este miércoles un paro y una movilización conjunta. Reclaman una recomposición salarial y mejores condiciones laborales, pero también advierten sobre el deterioro de la calidad de atención y la falta de recursos en el sistema público de salud.


Fotos y texto Daniel Ávalos para ANRed.


No era solamente una discusión por el sueldo. En las caras y en las palabras de quienes marcharon este miércoles había una preocupación que iba más allá de los números: sentir que todo el esfuerzo puesto en formarse, estudiar y sostener guardias interminables no tiene reconocimiento. Son profesionales que eligieron la salud, se esforzaron durante años de formación, y hoy trabajan en hospitales públicos. Atienden pacientes, forman parte de los equipos de atención y sostienen buena parte de la actividad cotidiana de los servicios. Sin embargo, sienten que ese trabajo pierde valor frente a salarios insuficientes, falta de recursos y decisiones de los distintos gobiernos que afectan directamente sus tareas.


 


Con un paro y una movilización conjunta, residentes de Nación, Provincia de Buenos Aires y Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires llevaron sus reclamos a las calles. La jornada comenzó en la Casa de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. Desde allí marcharon hacia el Ministerio de Salud de la Nación y luego al Ministerio de Salud porteño. Tres jurisdicciones, distintos gobiernos y una preocupación compartida.


En la provincia de Buenos Aires, un residente de primer año cobra alrededor de $1.300.000. El reclamo es llevar ese ingreso a un piso de $2.600.000. La diferencia entre ambas cifras no es un detalle . Es la distancia entre el trabajo que realizan y las condiciones materiales en las que pueden sostener su vida. Porque la vocación no paga el alquiler ni llena la heladera. Tampoco debería ser una excusa para naturalizar jornadas extensas, salarios bajos o pérdida de derechos laborales.


Pero hay otra preocupación que apareció con fuerza durante la jornada: la calidad de la atención.


Los residentes advierten que cada vez cuentan con menos herramientas para hacer su trabajo. Faltan medicamentos, insumos y personal. Los equipos se reducen y la demanda de atención sigue estando ahí, del otro lado de la puerta del consultorio o de la guardia. Cuando un profesional no dispone de los recursos necesarios y debe multiplicar esfuerzos para cubrir las necesidades de un servicio, el problema no queda dentro del hospital. También lo padecen quienes llegan buscando atención.


El ajuste también tiene responsables, el deterioro que denuncian los residentes no puede separarse de la política presupuestaria del Gobierno nacional. El ajuste sobre el sistema sanitario tiene números concretos. En mayo, el Ejecutivo recortó más de $63.000 millones de distintas partidas del Ministerio de Salud. Entre ellas, $25.000 millones fueron destinados al fortalecimiento de los sistemas provinciales, y otros $20.000 millones para medicamentos, insumos y tecnología médica. No es una discusión contable. Son recursos que deberían traducirse en hospitales funcionando, medicamentos disponibles y mejores condiciones para atender a la población.


El ministro Mario Lugones está al frente de ese Ministerio y tiene responsabilidad política sobre las decisiones que se toman desde allí. No alcanza con administrar el ajuste ni la precariedad que promueve su gestión, y hablar de eficiencia cuando son los trabajadores y los pacientes quienes terminan enfrentando sus consecuencias. En ese contexto, la situación de las residencias nacionales suma otro problema. El nuevo régimen de becas, establecido por una resolución firmada por el propio Lugones, elimina derechos como el aguinaldo y los aportes jubilatorios.


Los trabajadores también denuncian recortes de cupos y cierres de espacios de formación. La preocupación alcanza al futuro de las residencias y a la posibilidad de seguir formando profesionales dentro del sistema público.


En el documento conjunto, los residentes también alertan sobre el desfinanciamiento de las áreas de salud mental y discapacidad, la falta de recursos para garantizar tratamientos y medicamentos, y el incumplimiento de políticas previstas en la Ley Nacional de Salud Mental.


En CABA, además, denunciaron amenazas y medidas de amedrentamiento contra quienes participan de las protestas.


Esta movilización excede el reclamo salarial. Hay profesionales que identifican que el esfuerzo …

author: anred
title: Los tres megayates que pretendían anclar en el Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego arribaron a Ushuaia
content:
Los cruceros Lonian, Hodor y Sherakhan este miercoles 18 por la mañana, captados por la cámara del fotógrafo Juan Odela.


La flota de megayates de super lujo que desató una fuerte controversia ambiental, legal y geopolítica en Tierra del Fuego ya se encuentra en aguas fueguinas, pero lejos de los ecosistemas protegidos de Bahía Lapataia. El lunes 16 de noviembre, los buques Lonian, Hodor y Sherakhan – los dos primeros con bandera británica – arribaron a la capital provincial y permanecen fondeados en la Bahía de Ushuaia, cerrando en los hechos la pulseada administrativa que obligó a dar marcha atrás con la autorización firmada por la Intendencia del Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego.

Por Agenda Malvinas.


Los registros del sistema de seguimiento marítimo satelital

VesselFinder


confirman que las tres embarcaciones navegan de manera coordinada, operando como una verdadera escuadrilla logística de turismo VIP:


M/Y Lonian:

 Fue el primero en tocar aguas de la bahía local, arribando a las

14:10

. Con 87 metros de eslora y bandera de Islas Caimán, es la nave insignia vinculada al magnate estadounidense Lorenzo Fertitta.


M/Y Hodor:

 Ingresó en segundo lugar, a las

17:08

. Este buque de apoyo de 67 metros —también registrado en el enclave colonial británico de Islas Caimán— funciona como plataforma logística y transporte auxiliar para la expedición.


M/Y Sherakhan:

 Cerró el despliegue de la flota ingresando a las

17:34

, completando el posicionamiento conjunto frente a la costa de Ushuaia.


El desenlace que confirmó la advertencia técnica


La permanencia de los tres buques en la bahía de Ushuaia ratifica, en la práctica, la solución que el propio cuerpo técnico del Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego había planteado antes de que estallara el escándalo.


En el informe conjunto del 20 de octubre

(IF-2026-102110148-APN-PNTF#APNAC)

, siete profesionales y jefes operativos del área protegida habían dictaminado que resultaba improcedente habilitar el fondeo en Bahía Lapataia y el sobrevuelo de sus dos helicópteros, señalando de forma explícita que estas operaciones podían desarrollarse perfectamente en otros sectores costeros,

«como la bahía de Ushuaia – ubicados afuera del área protegida»

.


Pese a ese dictamen categórico, el

intendente Marcelo Almirón

 había firmado el permiso el 27 de octubre

(NO-2026-104217762-APN-PNTF#APNAC)

 a instancias de la agencia marítima local

USHIP S.R.L..

 Solo tras la difusión pública de los expedientes oficiales y la repercusión periodística a nivel provincial y nacional, la empresa operadora desistió del pedido y la Intendencia debió emitir un comunicado de repliegue para dar por cerrada la autorización.


El saldo institucional y la alerta sobre la intermediación


El fondeo actual de la escuadrilla en la Bahía de Ushuaia evita el arrastre de cadenas y anclas de gran porte sobre los bosques sumergidos de cachiyuyo (

Macrocystis pyrifera

), así como la perturbación acústica de helicópteros sobre los hábitats del huillín y las aves costeras dentro del Parque Nacional.


Sin embargo, el episodio deja abierta una discusión de fondo sobre el funcionamiento de los controles estatales en el extremo sur. La secuencia documental expuso cómo una agencia marítima local puede tramitar permisos a medida por encima de las leyes nacionales y los informes técnicos, instalando un precedente de excepcionalidad que, como demuestran antecedentes similares en reservas provinciales como

Península Mitre

 e

Isla de los Estados

, exige un escrutinio público permanente sobre el manejo.


Fuente:

https://agendamalvinas.com.ar/noticia/los-tres-megayates-que-pretendian-anclar-en-el-parque-nacional-tierra-del-fuego-arribaron-a-ushuaia

author: Darío Aranda
title: Un molino agroecológico en plena Pampa Húmeda y el cooperativismo que produce alimentos sanos
content:
Por Mauricio Amaya


Existe un molino que genera entusiasmo en el partido bonaerense de Lincoln. No es un molino cualquiera: es de producción agroecológica y uno de los últimos logros de un grupo de productores y vecinos que, inspirados en otras experiencias, se aventuró a conformar la Cooperativa Newen Pampeana. Tienen un triple objetivo: respetar los ciclos naturales, generar un alimento sano para la comunidad y demostrar que la producción agroecológica es rentable. La historia de un proyecto contrahegemónico y solidario.


Pablo Argilla es ingeniero en sistemas y uno de los referentes de la

Cooperativa Newen Pampeana

, que se conformó hace seis años pero que tiene todo un recorrido previo en la zona del noroeste bonaerense con el objetivo de

retornar a sistemas de producción de alimentos sanos y diversos

.


Todo inició en 2016: “Viajamos junto a mi familia a un encuentro de agroecología en Rojas, organizado por la

Red Nacional de Municipios Agroecológicos (Renama)

, que recién surgía como institución. Nos hicimos más conscientes de la problemática de los agroquímicos en la salud y sobre todo el ambiente, que es lo que más nos sensibilizó. Volvimos a Lincoln con la intención de difundir la agroecología en nuestro territorio, organizamos una reunión en mi casa y se dio una gran convocatoria”.


Entonces conformaron el grupo ConCiencia Agroecológica, que llegó a reunir a casi 100 personas entre

productores, docentes, ingenieros, jubilados, dueños de campo, abogados, veterinarios y comerciantes

. “Empezamos a recorrer establecimientos y experiencias agroecológicas, aprendiendo y conociendo”, añade Argilla sobre las visitas a la

chacra La Aurora

 de Benito Juárez (en el sur bonaerense, distinguido por la FAO),

Guaminí

 y Coronel Suárez, entre otros.


Entonces se inició una transición hacia la agroecología, que antes estaba ligada localmente a espacios de huerta familiar. De forma colectiva, el grupo ConCiencia Agroecológica encaró el proyecto hacia dimensiones mayores y con escala de hectáreas en una zona donde el núcleo es la soja o el monocultivo.


Foto: Cooperativa Newen Pampeana


Una red de iniciativas agroecológicas


Con el proyecto de ConCiencia Agroecológica en marcha se creó un grupo de compras llamado Amaranto, para contactar proveedores de productos agroecológicos de todo el país. Y en conjunto con ingenieros agrónomos, empezaron a formar un equipo de trabajo que para 2019 integraba a 40 productores.


“Nos dimos cuenta que empujábamos por una alimentación sana en la producción pero nuestras alacenas no tenían esos productos. Entonces emprendimos esto en contacto con proveedores de todo el país”, cuenta Magalí Roncoli Arana, productora ganadera.


Forma parte de Horizonte Agroecológico, otro espacio que se desprende de ConCiencia Agroecológica: “Nos dimos cuenta de que varios éramos ganaderos y vimos que la agroecología es muy amplia. Entonces nos agrupamos para intensificar en conocimiento y trabajo en esa área”, añade. Con el apoyo del

Programa Cambio Rural del INTA

, este espacio empezó a funcionar en 2023.


El molino agroecológico en funcionamiento


“Recibimos el cereal, lo mantenemos libre de posibles ataque de insectos a través de un gas que es agroecológico y lo trabajamos en el molino. Es un molino de mecanismo muy simple. Estamos haciendo

harina envasada en un kilo, cuatro kilos y diez kilos

”, cuenta Santiago Antonio Paolucci, de 82 años, sobre el funcionamiento de la molienda.


Paolucci tiene mucha experiencia para brindarle a la cooperativa Newen Pampeana. “Nuestro objetivo es transformar la materia prima en producto de oferta. Hay un mercado que lo estamos haciendo nosotros”, comenta sobre el estímulo de ser parte del proyecto que avanza de forma incipiente. “Viene el trigo, se pasa por la clasificadora de granos, se procesa, se sacan las impurezas o tierra y va al molino. La moledora tiene sus aspiradores, se le saca el polvo y la harina sale con los microgranos justos, mantiene el color original y es una harina sin agregados de ningún tipo”, relata.


Se trata de un molino de "motor martillo" (como se lo conoce en el sector), que funciona mediante el impacto a alta velocidad de una serie de martillos metálicos contra el material para reducirlo a partículas más pequeñas. Lo trabajan dos personas por jornada. En ocho horas, puede producir alrededor de 2.000 kilos de harina.


Luego se hace la molienda y se envasa de forma directa; no se le agrega nada. El salvado va junto …
